chapters.title: Chapter 1
chapters.html:
This is my first Phaidei fic. If any characters are out of character, ah well-- I did my best to transcribe their struggles into a mundane modern setting. What if the flamechase journey was instead about being an underpaid, overworked worker abused by the system?

!IMPORTANT!

Phainon is dealing with the passing of his sister, Cyrene. He is very unwell, and very mentally ill. He is suicidal, and this fic will deal with the implications and reality of that. It is implied he drinks.

Mydei is a rape survivor. This fic will also deal with that. This is not sexualized or fetishized or a kink; I want to explore the very real horror of sexual assault. I cannot stress this enough. This is what the "Past Rape/Non-con" tag is referring to. It will be handled respectfully.

There is very light gore towards the end of the fic. Phainon has a vague flashback to Cyrene's death, and then a disturbing dream. It's not very explicit, but such images will be all throughout the fic.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: dolphinsamurai
chapters.html:
FLAMECHASE INC. is Amphoreus’ top outsourcing company, providing a top notch customer support experience to companies all across the country. Founded by Khaos Petridis in 2004, it has been the most well-rated company in Amphoreus for the past 20 years, boasting all sorts of awards and countless accolades. ’Excellent Customer Service 2018’ , ’Team Performance 2007’ , ’Operational Efficiency 2012’ , just to name a few. The work environment is friendly, productive and stimulates their workers’ creativity. They are truly one big family, where no one is treated better than another. FLAMECHASE INC. prides themselves on equality, benevolence, and a above-industry-standard pay.

That is what it says on their website.

The reality of the truth, however, is that Phainon is chained to his desk, slaving nine hours per day answering calls to pay off for the loan he took out for his sister’s funeral; and his failed pilot school stint, but that's besides the point. His breaks are scheduled, and if he needs to take a piss, the whole Google Teams chat must know. His current project is for a Belobogian company called DolphinSamurai, formerly two companies (Dolphin, specializing in vacuums roombas, hairdryers, steam mops and air purifiers, and Samurai, specializing in kitchen appliances) that have recently merged into one. What it means for him is that he has intimate knowledge of every gear and screw that goes into making a vacuum or an air-fryer, and that he spends the better half of his day teaching elderly people how to remove their vacuum’s floor nozzle. What that usually leads to is him biting his knuckles trying not to cuss out a clearly dementia-addled grandma.

“Alright, ma’am, is there anything else I can help you with? Alright, in that case, thank you for choosing DolphinSamurai. If you want to take the survey, please don’t hang up. Goodbye!” With unimaginable speed, Phainon takes off his headset and changes his status to On Break – it has been three hours since he’s had his last cigarette, and his scheduled break is coming up. As the fog of an exhausting forty minute call with a confused elderly woman starts to clear up from his head, Phainon begins to register a faint buzzing sound next to him. When he turns to face it, he’s reminded of his very best number one kirakira love and peace desk neighbour work best friend, as she likes to call herself. Cifera seems unbothered, not sitting at her desk but rather walking leisurely on a treadmill because of course she’s the type of person with an under-desk treadmill. Phainon is still not sure how she convinced their department managers to let her get it. She’s typing away at her computer with one hand, playing with a fidget spinner with the other, talking into her headset with a customer, all while sparing no glance to the computer screen and rather looking at her phone– Phainon knows that, most likely, she’s watching the baby monitor installed into her house. Which is not used for any baby, mind you, but rather for her seven cats.

“This is Bartholos and this is Arson and this is Tax Evasion and this is Grand Larceny and this is Drug Trafficking and… ” he remembers her trailing off on his first day as she showed her pictures of all of her cats– all rescues, some with special needs. The repeating motif amongst these pets is that they were all incomprehensibly ugly and incredibly fat.

”Why does Bartholos have a normal name?” he asked then, and Cipher made a face. ”My ex-wife got it for us. Bandaid baby. I took the kid in the divorce.”

Now, she’s putting to work her best skill as a customer support analyst: bullshitting.

“Yes, ma’am, of course~ Say, I’ve heard some dogs barking in the background– do you have pets, hmm? Oh! Did you know that your Dolphin NC756 has a special motorized FurBegone accessory? Yes, yes, it’s like an attachable floor nozzle specifically made to clean pet hair. Let me tell you, ma’am, I have seven cats and that thing is a lifesaver! Yeah? Yes! Of course I can order it for you, ma’am, let me just do that real quick~ And since you’re such a loyal customer , how about I throw in a 10% discount for ya? That’ll bring the total down to 29.99 Balance Coins. Alright… Boop! Aaand it’s all ordered, ma’am! Your new accessory should be with you in two to three business days.”

Phainon watches in awe as she finishes up the call. Her voice is feline and honeyed and utterly shameless . She lies like it’s her mother tongue– Phainon knows, for a fact , that she does not have a FurBegone and that it is not a lifesaver. He knows those things break at the first gust of wind because they are made of very cheap plastic, and that they clog up like a motherfucker after two uses. And, most importantly–

“What do you mean, a 10% discount?”

Cipher looks at him with a knowing, shit-eating grin, like he’s just waiting for him to stumble onto her scheme. He likes this game with her, so he plays.

“You know, a discount. For 10%.”

“But you said that would bring the total down to 29.99.”

“Cooooorrect!”

“But a FurBegone costs 29.99 at full price .”

Cipher grins, and puts her hands on her hips– proud. Phainon snickers at that, and leans back into his chair. He brings his hands to rest on his stomach, fingers intertwined. “You know, she can always go on the site and see the real price.”

“She’s a sixty-two year old grandma, she’s not going to do that.”

“It’s going to break, like, right away.”

“It sure is.”

“Accessories aren’t covered by the warranty.”

“Nuh-uh.”

“So when it breaks, she has to purchase a new one.”

The woman winks at him, mischievous, and waves her hands like a magician would. ”Bingo~” Phainon laughs, because how could he not? Some of the tension from his shoulder eases, and he sits up with a slap on his thighs. “Cigarette?” he asks, already digging through his pockets for his lighter. Cipher basically leaps to the occasion, grabbing her bag as she goes.

He is not sure how he has become so close to Cipher, but she has a way of getting under your skin– that, and spending 9 hours every day essentially shoulder to shoulder, has helped. She sees right through him, and that scares Phainon. The difference, however, between Cipher and any other person, is that she sees the rot and shrugs her shoulders. Makes a joke out of it. Teeters on the edge of a dangerous blade, close to breaking skin and spilling blood; she, however, wields that blade bravely. Grabs it by the sharp end and twists it further. She’s ruthless, and relentless.

It was a Saturday night hazed in the after-glow of several hours of drinking– things do not go well when he drinks. It was only a few months after he started working at FLAMECHASE– a company team bonding event. Too much alcohol, too little water. He was in the office’s kitchen, head in hands as he sat at the table, and the clock struck well past midnight. Cipher was leaning against the counter, watching him with careful eyes. He started lamenting about his sister, flame extinguished too soon, because all roads eventually lead back to Cyrene. She let him talk, until he mentioned having to work this miserable job to pay off her funeral, and how suicidal it’s making him. At that point, Cipher raised a sharp brow and tutted her lips.

”Nobody made you bury her in a bed of pink flowers, dude. Ya kinda did that to yourself.”

”She would’ve liked it.”

“She was dead on impact. She doesn’t like much of anything anymore.”

He should’ve gotten mad and maybe slapped the make-up off of her face then, but he didn’t– because she was right. A small revelation. He has no one else to blame. The grand, opulent funeral– it was for him. It was his apology to Cyrene, and one that fell on deaf cold ears. He knew, then, that Cipher could be trusted to give him exactly what he needed– acid.

So, they smoke together. Every break, on the benches in front of their office building, fifteen minutes every three hours. They usually go through at least two cigarettes, but more often than not it’s three. They talk shit about their customers, about management, and Cipher shares funny and gross stories about her seven monsters. Every time he tries to press further into her own past, she pulls back gracefully. It’s almost enviable. A friend, but more of a stranger. A comfortable kind of distance that Phainon can use to lash himself with. Humiliation looks good on him.

“You know, putting money in FLAMECHASE’s pockets doesn’t necessarily mean more money in your pockets. You don’t need to lie to grandmas.”

“Oh but Phainon, you wound me. You think I do this for profit? My dear boy, I am simply lying to grandmas for the love of the game.” she smirks, sharp like all of her edges. Phainon is thoroughly entertained. “And, either way, HR takes notice.” she winks, “Who knows, maybe I’ll be promoted to Escalations one day.”

“I’m sure you will, Cipher, and then you’ll have even more bargaining power against women with Alzheimer’s.” She throws her head back and cackles, then recoils back to take a greedy pull out of her cigarette. A car pulls in near them, and her eyes instantly shoot towards the source of the sound.

Castorice steps out from a white Honda, a slight and shy girl. Beautiful like a butterfly, though in a way that resonates a quiet sort of strength. Her long floral-patterned summer dress swishes behind her as she closes the car’s door; she looks troubled. Her eyebrows are knitted together tight. Wordlessly, she sits next to Phainon on the bench and digs through her braided bag for her e-cigarette. Phainon open his mouth to greet her, but Cipher is quicker.

“Now there you are, Princess Homebody~” she calls out, turning to look at Castorice from where she’s standing up in front of Phainon. “You’re three hours late, miss. That’s unlike you.” Castorice sighs, and rubs her forehead. Her shoulders are stiff. “My sister’s carer had an emergency, so I had to stay with her for a bit more. I talked to management, I’ll make up for the lost hours.” Phainon knows that means working for twelve hours in one day. Gently, he grabs her hand, a subtle motion. Gives it a small squeeze.

“How is she?” he asks, and his voice is soft. He can practically hear Cipher checking out of the conversation now that it took a serious turn. In his peripheral, he sees her turn around and pull out her phone.

“She’s, well– She’s…” Castorice struggles to find words, and settles for sighing and leaning back against the bench. “We’re trying to keep her comfortable. It, uh, won’t be long now. Maybe a few months? I don’t know. She’s starting to, you know, have difficulty, uh. Breathing.”

Phainon nods slowly. Castorice’s sister has amyotrophic lateral scoliosis. It hit her out of nowhere, and it hit her hard. Going from two paychecks to one has taken its toll on Castorice, so she works part-time night shifts as well to support their living expenses. He gives her a moment of silence, not saying anything (what is there to say? ) but also not moving his hand from hers. A quiet support, grounding. Castorice takes a drag out her e-cigarette and moves her face upward to face the sky– she stays like that for a bit, looking at the birds flying overhead, thinking. After a moment, she closes her eyes, takes a deep breath, and looks at Phainon.

“I spoke with Tribios.” she starts, and Phainon does not like her tone; it’s inquisitive, expectant.

“Right.”

“When her mother died, she went to a grief recovery support group.” There it is. Phainon’s face twists despite his best efforts. “I want to go when Polyxia passes away.”

Phainon nods absent-mindedly, and tries to pretend like he doesn’t know what she’s asking of him. “That sounds great, Castorice.”

She frowns a bit, barely perceptible. “I want you to come with me.”

Phainon presses on with his act, and laughs. He retreats his hand from hers– this does not go unnoticed by Casotrice. Her frown deepens. “Why? As your like, support buddy?”

Her face softens, and she presses closer to him. Now, she’s holding his hands. Her touch is feather-light and gentle, the way everything about her tends to be. Quiet support. Something that borders too closely on pity; it’s bitter in his mouth. Castorice’s voice drops to a whisper. “I mean for you, Phainon. For your sister.” Phainon squirms in his seat, and puts some distance between the two. He can feel his heart tightening in his chest. He laughs again, and this time it sounds very nervous. “Nah, nah, I’m good. I’m dealing with it well.”

”No the fuck you’re not!” Cipher says all of a sudden, because of course she’s been listening in. She is damn near omniscient. “You’re dealing with it like shit.”

“Cipher, please…” Castorice chastises, and gives Phainon a small timid smile. “Look, you think about it, okay? Really, I’m serious, give it some thought. You have time.” She looks hopeful in a way that makes Phainon want to scream; there is no hope here .

“Okay,” he says, because he can’t say no to Castorice when she looks so kind and so worried. “I’ll think about it.” She smiles at that, wide and bright, pearly teeth and all. She’s too good for this job; too good for him. Wasted niceties.

He will think about it, that is not a lie. What he doesn’t tell Castorice is that he already made up his mind. It’s not for him.

They spend the last five minutes of their break with more leisurely talks. As always, it turns into a gigglefest over Cipher’s phone as they watch videos of her cats being funny or stupid or mischievous. When it’s time to go back to work, Castorice looks to be in a significantly better mood. She is his work neighbor too, in a way– her desk is directly behind his, so they’re back to back. Sometimes she taps his shoulder so he can help her with a procedure. Other times, he taps on her shoulder and makes funny faces at her so she’ll laugh.

The next two and a half hours pass by a lot smoother than the first three did. Most of the calls are quick and boring– product registration, questions about the warranty, and common fixes. He teaches people how to remove their vacuum’s floor nozzle, how to empty it’s dust cups, what the lights on the motor mean. He orders replacements for steam mops, air-fryers, and toaster grills. Nobody yells at him.

His last call comes in eight minutes before his lunch break. Phainon picks up the call, does his introduction, and waits for the customer to state their grievance, but is met with nothing. There is silence and heavy breathing for ten seconds, and Phainon starts to think it’s a buttdial. “Hello?” he tries.

“Uh, yeah, sorry, I…” a man, probably in his fifties, starts talking. “I cut myself on one of your electric woodfire grills.” Phainon can’t help but smile a little– this is perfect, because this case reads “None Of My Business” in bold letters. This is a case for Tribios or Cerydra or whatever unlucky motherfucker over at Escalations takes up the call. “Alright, sir, I’m very sorry to hear that. Unfortunately, since I’m just a call center agent, I am not allowed to deal with this situation, so I’m going to send it forward to one of my higher-ups at Escalations. However, to speed things up, we can go ahead and start a video call so I can get a picture of your injury in case you need to press a claim.”

FLAMECHASE offers a video call option for customer support purposes– using a third party app, Phainon sends a text message with a link to the customer’s phone. When he accesses it, he will be able to see through the phone’s camera; just like FaceTime. Phainon leans back and waits, Snipping Tool at the ready to take a screenshot of the injury.

The camera turns on. He is not sure what he expected– a scrape, maybe a surface scratch. What he sees, instead, is a deep red gash across a man’s palm– half an inch, maybe an inch deep, cutting across the entire surface of his hand. It still gushes blood, red, terrible. He gasps, and seizes still in his chair. A brief image: his car beeping, his chest crushed between the seat and the airbag, a wound across a girl’s forehead. He does not recognize her. Blood trickles like spoiled honey down her beautiful face. Her eyes are blue, perfectly crystalline, and unseeing. He knows those eyes from somewhere, maybe from his own face. Maybe from his mother’s. She does not answer when he calls for her.

Phainon starts to sweat. His fingernails dig into his office chair. His clothes are too tight for him. It is entirely way too warm in this room. A fan buzzes somewhere in the back of his mind. He thinks his eyes might pop out of his head why is it so hot here oh god he’s still bleeding. His heart threatens to beat out of his chest and impale itself on his monitor. Is he crying? He feels a warmth on his face, under his eyes. Someone is speaking to him from his headset. He calls her name, softly under his breath, but she does not answer. She broke all of her teeth on the dashboard.

Cipher takes notice of the scene next to her, her attention piqued as she was just finishing up the call. She steals a glance at his monitor where the man is still showing his wounded hand, then at Phainon’s unmoving face, teeth clenched, eyes big with horror. She cringes, entirely way too violent of a spectacle for her, and puts down her headset. ”Escalations!” she calls out in the office, “We need Escalations, quickly! It’s an, uhhhhh, claims situation. Some guy hurt himself.”

He’s breathing hard. There are hands on his shoulder, firm and strong. “Come on, Snowy, get’a hold of yourself,” Cipher says somewhere above him. Tribios from Escalations, his team leader, swoops in with dexterity and urgency. Wordlessly, he’s maneuvered off of the chair as she sits down and takes over the call. Castorice, mid-procedure, has noticed; she’s turned around on her seat. ”Is he okay?” she mouths to Cipher, and Cipher just shakes her head. He’s sitting up now. His knees are weak. He’s going to throw up. Tribios is finishing up the call, and it took all of two minutes. She’s taken the picture, written the ticket, and has promised she will personally forward the case to DolphinSamurai’s management and their legal team. She closes the call. Disconnects his computer from the system. She turns to look at him.

“You should go home, Phainon.” He does not like the way she said it. Like he’s small. Like there’s something wrong with him.

“I can’t– um,” he starts, and his words choke in his throat. A moment. “I still have three hours left.”

“You can go home,” she repeats, firm. She is judging him, certainly. He wants to scream at her.

“Yeah, bud, you really should, I mean– you totally freaked ou–” a stern gaze from Tribios is enough to silence Cipher, and for once she seems to retreat and look ashamed.

“I can’t– I don’t want to make up for it, I…” He cannot spend twelve hours in this place. He will kill himself. He will shoot his brains out in front of the building and his brains will spell FLAMECHASE on the sidewalk.

“You won’t.” Tribios touches his arm. “I’ll speak to management for you. You won’t.”

She’s already handing him his jacket. He looks to Cipher, lost. She shrugs, grins, and makes a ’shoo’ motion with her hands. Behind him, Castorice is still in the middle of a call– but she spares him a glance full of pity.

It’s always pity with these people. He clenches his jaw. Grits his teeth so hard he thinks they might shatter justlikehers . A gummy smile flashes in his mind. She was all that was good in the world and what’s even left I mean is it just this? Is it just this until he dies? His feet are moving without him willing them to. He is out of the building, cold summer wind in his face. He does not feel his fingertips. Static under his skin. He thinks the world might be spinning around him, and he’s at risk of being thrown off of its axis. Somewhere along the way, Tribios has called him an Uber. He gets in, wordlessly, and the driver does not ask where he’s going. She knows his home address from HR.

It does not feel real. Life after Cyrene. A half-formed dream, maybe. An aborted fetus. He gets home. It is the same little apartment it’s always been. They rented it together. Rent is bearable still, even with Cyrene’s paycheck gone. The apartment is a piece of shit anyways, in a dilapidated little neighborhood at the edge of the city. The landlord practically begged them to rent it, and it felt like it was free of cost when she was around– it was never about sharing rent, however. They have never been apart, not since he was born. Older sisters; grains of sand on the beach. Too many to count. Too few words to speak. Her immensity can not be matched. There will be no poems. He leaves his key on the table, next to a bottle of water that he has not moved in eight months– her gloss, pink and glittery, is still on it.

He moves through the small hallway, and makes a mental note to get cockroach repellent– the thought stops him in his tracks. He slumps against the wall, runs a hand through his hair, and lets out a wheeze. He laughs, bitter, chortled. Your sister is dead and you need cockroach repellent.

Phainon passes over his bedroom, into the next room over. It’s her room. With shaky hands, he turns the doorknob and opens it. It is utterly untouched, and has been for eight months. He hasn’t even vacuumed. Thick dust gathers on every surface like a wedding veil, painting the room hazy and grey. Her bed is still unmade, purple flowery duvet thrown aside in a rush. A pile of clothes rests by her closet; she did not know what to wear that day. She must’ve picked something nice, nonetheless. Something feminine and flirty, probably, because she liked to get the attention of cute girls. Phainon doesn’t remember.

He dares not enter her room. It is far too sacred for him. His feet stay planted on the threshold, and he looks– for a minute, for two, then for six, ten…

Every time he enters her bedroom, he is expectant. Hopeful. As if he will open the door one day and see her bundled up under her covers, tapping on her phone. Sometimes, he would walk in on her practicing her dance moves. There are countless posters of Robin on every wall. She had such big dreams. She was going to make it out– be somebody. Somebody more than this. More than him; better than him. A singer, an idol, somebody loved and adored the way she deserved to be. She had a modelling contract to sign the next week. Her big break.

It’s funny how those things work.

He does not know how long he stays in her room, but by the time Phainon retreats into his own bedroom, the sun is setting. He does not eat; he never really eats anymore, only to stay off the hunger. Sleep takes him as soon as he lays his head on his pillow. He does not remember a time before the tiredness.

Like every night, he dreams of Cyrene. Her pallid face framed by carnations, eyes white and milky like the bottom of a sink. She goes to speak, but chokes on blood. It spills out of her like bile, red and sticky. Her mouth is rows upon rows of black splinters, viscous, viscera. She smiles, wide and gummy, and stretches out her arms like she did when they were younger; when he used to jump in her arms and she would spin him around. ”Nini~” she calls to him, but she has the voice of screeching hawks and bellowing alligators. She beckons to him, open, naked on the embalmer’s table. She looks cruel. Phainon runs up to her and goes to hit her.

The dream always ends there. He wakes up clammy.

Your sister is dead, and it’s a new day.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: four and a half months
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

!!IMPORTANT!!

The first half of this fic has a big suicide TW. Phainon has a big suicidal breakdown and has very explicit suicidal fantasies. If you wish to skip it, it starts with "He is so ashamed. He is so so little and so so very ashamed." and ends with "On the fringes of his consciousness, somewhere boundlessly far away from him, a conversation unfolds, ignorant of his own presence in the room."

Please keep in mind that the above is only for the explicit suicidal fantasy. He continues being suicidal for several paragraphs and, yeah, as I've said in the previous chapter, this fic is going to deal with his suicidal ideation heavily.

Big shoutout to my bestie kind-of-beta reader kind-of-editor Gael who listens to me infodump about HSR and Phaidei and Castorice despite knowing nothing about any of this shit. They actually wrote the last part of the fic, the one with little Cyrene, and I added onto it to make it fit the scene.

Their original scene.

Phainon uses the rest of his paid sick days, all three of them, to stay home after the incident. The hours of the first day blur into each other, melting like candle wax under a flame. There is nowhere to go. He stays in bed for thirteen hours, scrolling on Tiktok. It’s mostly animals. Some new workout plans that he bookmarks for later. The occasional anime edit. He goes to the bathroom once, and only because he absolutely needs it. He does not eat. He sleeps the other eleven hours, but in bouts and fits of unconsciousness– never restful.

Cyrene haunts every corner of the apartment. He would be laying under the covers, feeling as if his bones have turned to iron, the sound of cars speeding outside his bedroom lulling him to sleep; and just as he is about to pass into unconsciousness, he hears her laugh down the hallway. Other times, he catches a flash of pink in the corner of his eyes, swift as a will-o'- wisp. The smell of her perfume, cotton-candy sweet, is so deeply ingrained into his nostrils that he doesn’t think he’s smelled anything else since her funeral.

She comes to him in her white burial dress, sometimes. Rarely. Silent in the dark corners of his room. Toothless, a finger raised up in accusation.

Phainon opens up their text messages. Reads through them, rushing through the barrage of “I miss you”s and “I wish you were here”s of the past eight months. He goes back to the time where she had a voice; get milk when you come home

What else is there to say? She has always been the prophetic kind– intuitive, damn near an empath. Always knew what to say, how to say it, her hands gentle on the top of his head– a redemption of some kind when he cried in her lap, when the world was too loud or too mean, like a priest absolving him of his sins. His eyes wander to Cipher’s face, and he is shocked by the kindness that they find there.

She jokes about this sometimes, when they’re together on their girl’s night out . Pokes and teases him about his dirty apartment. All of his most embarrassing moments, his lowest of lows, late-night calls from the rooftops of Marmoreal Market or the bridge ledge. Her– enigmatic, elusive, otter-sleek and slippery like an eel. Him– the remnants of a failed abortion.

Phainon is looking at her now and– he sees her, for the first time. The furrow in her brow exaggerated like a muppet, the small scrunch in her nose where it wrinkles like a lion’s. Her eyes, now blue now green, are clear and beautiful volcanic lakes, overflowing with strange grief and sorrow. There’s something luminous about her visage right now, in front of him. Something almost saintly. The light from the window behind him hits her face and dresses it in patterns of sun and shadow. “I’m scared, Phainon,” she says, and the emotion is too much for her– she cannot bear to look at him when she says it. She turns her head the other way, her whole body twisting with it, bearing her back to him. “You’re my best friend, and I’m just… scared. Of losing you. And I want to help.”

This is new. This is shockingly new. She’s never like… this. Open. Vulnerable. In their eleven months of friendship, he doesn’t remember a time where she’s talked about her emotions. It comes hard to her, he knows. The way she’s saying these words– it’s as if she’s actively fighting against throwing up.

Four and a half months. This is a vitally important timeframe. Cipher knows. Castorice doesn’t, but she doesn’t have to know. She is perceptive though, and can sense that the conversation has shifted to a dangerously intimate territory. So, with that knowledge, she backs off a little. Gives them their space.

Four and a half months. He sees Cipher physically cringe at the memento. Her whole body shudders. It takes a lot of bravery for her to look back at him, but she is brave and so she does look. She’s blinking back tears, too prideful yet to let them flow. Phainon has managed to make both of his friends cry in the span of thirty-five minutes. It’s kind of his talent; letting people down. This is coded information. A conversation that they’re having actively around Castorice, and that only they can understand. Four and a half months. If Castorice feels excluded, she doesn’t show it. But this is something that’s between him and Cipher. Sacred and defilatory, like a cursed idol that they both carry in their pockets. This is not a burden that Castorice has to bear as well. Phainon’s shameful little secret that he has roped Cifera into keeping, shoved in cabinets and under the sink, where it can only grow exponentially bigger and more powerful; black mold.

(Castorice has come to expect exclusion; something has always been fundamentally wrong with her. She can’t quite put her finger on what, however. There is something wrong with her that is not wrong with anybody else– not even with Polyxia, whom she shared a womb with. Boys liked Polyxia. Polyxia had friends, and Castorice– well, she had Polyxia. So she takes this exclusion, the slow emotional push away from her and towards each other, with a straight face. Because they are her friends, but something is wrong with Castorice– and it’s not their fault. A sea of flowers separates her from other people. She reaches out, and they fade into flakes like faraway memories. In the face of Cipher and Phainon’s cryptic veiled words and telepathically understood sentences, she turns away with respect, and starts rubbing her hands together.)

There is a beat of silence. None speak. A magpie chatters outside the window, gaining Bartholos’ attention. Lazily, he struts to the window and immediately, all eyes are on him. His claws make small clinking sounds against the hardwood floor, and his big orange eyes are filled with determination and ambition. Castorice is the first to snicker  from where she’s retreated within herself. Her face lights up with glee, and she goes to coo at Bartholos. “Aren’t you the best little hunter in Okhema?” she crouches down to scratch under his chin, which the cat accepts happily. “Yes, you are. Yes, yes you are!” Cipher took her phone out the moment she caught a whiff of Bartholos’ shenanigans, and now she presses the button to stop recording. She leans back and laughs. “He does this all the time,” she says, “Doesn’t know how fat and rotund he is, but he’s still got that hunter’s instinct. I’m telling you, Phainon, the roaches are not safe with Bartholos around.”

Phainon’s eyes crinkle painfully when he smiles, sore and swollen from all the crying. But he smiles, bearing teeth a little crooked. “Should I take the roaches off the lease then?”

Cipher slaps her thigh at that and guffaws. “HA! Yeah, you better! Cas, come on,” she shuffles off the bed and puts a hand on Castorice’s back. “I’m gonna go get the bags. I’m starting with the bathroom. You get the living room.”

“What do I get?” Phainon rises from the bed, heavy-boned, exhausted.

Cipher has already made her way to the kitchen (how is she so fast?) , and her voice cuts through the apartment as she speaks. “You get some Luofu food from that place you like. Zhuming cuisine. Very yummy. We got you like four big takeout boxes.”

Perplexed, Phainon turns to Castorice for an explanation. She pets Bartholos two more times before she straightens up. Her expression is weightless when she looks at him, and her shoulders are relaxed. “You don’t have to do anything, Phainon. You can just rest while we clean. Please.”

“Whaaat? I can’t let you girls work your asses off while I’m twiddling my thumbs in bed.” Castorice giggles, then hums.

“Then… maybe you could get the dishes, when we’re done?”

“And until then?”

“Just keep us company. And put on a shirt.”

Phainon grins, big, genuine, loud. “Deal.”

So, Cipher and Castorice clean. At first, Phainon retreats to his bedroom, a twinge too embarrassed and too well-behaved to get in their way. Slowly but surely, however, small requests come pouring in.

’Can you get me a new roll of paper?’

’Where’s your tile cleaner?’

’Where’s your vacuum?’

’Bring me a new bag.’

’Can you wet this for me?’

’Take the trash outside, please.’

When Phainon retrieves the vacuum (which has been gathering dust on the balcony for four and a half months) for Castorice, her mouth falls open as if she’s struck dumb.

“Phainon, this is like… professional grade.”

“Hah, yeah. Cyrene and I saved up a lot to get it.”

She seems genuinely excited for some reason, and takes to it like a child with a new toy. When she turns it on to vacuum the rug, Castorice exclaims with excitement. “It can handle the carpet like it’s nothing!”

Cipher is fast . Impressively fast. She’s done with his mangy bathroom in under two and a half hours. When he sees her walk out triumphantly, Phainon has the nerve to be a little suspicious . As she moves onto the kitchen, he goes to check.

And yeah, no, it’s clean. It’s hotel room clean– it’s probably cleaner than it’s ever been, even back when he used to love cleaning it. The tiles look as if they’re brand new, shining bright and baby blue. The bathtub is pristine, and Phainon has forgotten it’s supposed to be white and not a yellow-y light brown hue. He can practically see his reflection in it. It smells good . A little citrusy. The toilet actually looks inviting for once. There are still bugs scurrying around, but they will be dealt with as well. He puts the toilet seat down and sits on it. Just sits, taking in the nice smell and the cleanliness. It’s nice. It’s really, really nice to just sit in a clean room. As his eyes wander around, they settle on the bathtub curtains– and he realizes, a little perplexed, that Cipher changed them. She got him brand new ones, with cartoon cat patterns.

And, ah– that’s just really kind of her, isn’t it? His previous curtains were fine, a little old but not torn. These, however… Well, they’re just very nice. Phainon goes to feel them with all the reverence of touching the Golden Fleece. He thinks these curtains are infinitely more precious.

Castorice has a difficult task with the living room, considering it’s the most spacious room in the apartment; at the same time, however, it’s the least lived in. So while there’s a lot of dust , there’s not much filth . She convinces him to have some of the takeout they brought over while she goes dustbunny hunting. And, well– as previously stated, he can never really say ’no ’ to Castorice when she looks so kind. So, he eats, perched like a gargoyle on the sofa with his feet planted on the cushions in case she needs the room to move. When Castorice turns around, she takes a look at him and snickers. “You look like L.”

“Hm?” is all Phainon can answer through a mouthful of noodles.

“You know, from Death Note?”

He chews a bit faster and swallows.

“Hah. Yeah. ‘Cuz of the way I’m sitting?”

Castorice beams. “Yes! You’re sitting just like him!” Phainon laughs at that, though it comes a bit weak and forced. The tiredness from a suicidal breakdown has set in heavy on his bones– Castorice is starting to look a little awkward, a bit disappointed by his reaction. Disappointment is not exactly the right word– Phainon knows she struggles with social interactions, and she tends to beat herself up for making ‘mistakes’. Every time she’s not met with the “appropriate response”, like laughter or lively conversation, she gets scared. Becomes small, and retreats a bit into herself. Phainon can see it now on her face, the way her smile falters a bit despite her insistence to keep it on her face. She shifts her weight from one foot to the other, a little stumped, as if unsure of what to do next.

“I’m just tired, Castorice,” he says, and he tries to be gentle. “It’s been– well, it’s been. Hm…”

“I wish you would talk to me, sometimes. About this stuff,” Castorice replies, and her voice is very hushed.

“You… don’t really want that, Cas, seriously.”

“I do.” she insists, “I really do, Phainon. I want to help.”

’Sweet girl.’ His heart breaks a little bit, and he wants to tell her that there’s really no helping this . But that would break her heart, and she’d certainly find herself at fault for it. “You’re already helping,” Phainon says instead. “You’re cleaning my shithole. That’s huge, Castorice. I can pick up the rest.”

“I wish you’d let me carry some of it.”

“You’re already carrying a lot.” She opens her mouth to argue against that, but Phainon keeps talking. “I’m really sorry. About earlier, I mean– the crying, and the things I said. I’m sorry for scaring you.”

“I wasn’t… scared. More… worried? I’ve talked a lot of people out of suicide, so I wasn’t like. Scared, you know. I was just concerned.”

Phainon blinks, because what– when did Castorice talk people out of suicide? What people? She’s talked at length about how she never had any friends besides Polyxia, and how he’s her first friend. He looks at her strangely, then decides it’s not appropriate to press on. “That’s… Well, I’ll keep it in mind. For next time.”

Castorice gives him a smile and oh it’s heartbreaking– it’s big, hopeful, all charmingly crooked teeth, and full of sweetness. “There won’t be a next time, Phainon. Don’t worry.”

There will be a next time. And there will be a last time.

A beat passes in silence as Castorice resumes the dust wiping; at some point, Bartholos trots in lazily and jumps in Phainon’s lap, pawing at his takeout box. As he’s wrestling with the grey beast, he hears Castorice clear her throat. When she speaks up, her voice is quieter, almost timid.

“I’ve been meaning to ask, um… Why does Cipher have the keys to your apartment?”

Phainon’s hand freezes on his chopsticks as the frosty fingers of an icy hand run down his spine. He chews at the inside of his cheek. Castorice does not turn around, simply waiting with her back to him. She has stopped any action. He has too. The expectation of an answer hangs heavy over his head, and lands heavier still on his shoulders. His first, knee-jerk reaction, is to tell her ’it’s not any of her business’ – because really, it’s not . His rational thought, however, tells him this is Castorice, and she doesn’t deserve his bad temper . Phainon chews on his bottom lip while he mulls the question over, trying to find his best escape route. Then, he decides to appeal to Castorice’s common decency. “It’s… I don’t really wanna talk about it right now.”

Her shoulders slump, but he sees her nod. “I get that.” is all she says.

Castorice finishes the rest of the living room in silence. It’s not exactly awkward but it’s– charged, in a way. Tense. It wasn’t a lie – he really doesn’t want to talk about it now, or ever. But she can certainly tell that there is an answer that he is withholding from her and…

Really, it’s simply too heavy and shameful. And Phainon has had his daily share of shame already. He will tell her one day, or maybe he will never tell her because– he really, really wants Castorice to like him.

It’s 9 PM, almost 9:30, by the time they’re done. Phainon is washing the dishes, as he promised to do, while Castorice and Cipher are smoking at his tiny dining table. “Ya got any plans tomorrow?” Cipher asks all of a sudden.

“Uh… probably just rotting in bed and refusing to pee for ten hours at a time?”

“ Charming! That’s not happening. Castorice and I are taking you out on a girl’s night out.” Phainon can practically hear the smirk on Cipher’s face.

“A girls’ night out…? Like… one of our girls’ night outs or…?”

Their , meaning Cipher and Phainon’s, girls’ night outs include spending upward of 250 Balance Coins on drugs probably laced with baby powder and downing shots that are 80% alcohol in cheap nightclubs. Then getting kicked out of said nightclubs for starting fights with creeps that were grinding and grabbing on Cipher. Then purchasing more cheap alcohol from a corner store and consuming it in a park. Then crashing Phainon’s place and drinking some more. Then having a sleepover (more drinking included) and waking up for work the next day with legendary hangovers.

Not quite Castorice’s vibe.

“Nah,” Cipher waves her hand dismissively. “Something more Castorice’s speed. Coffee and cakes, brunch and then a movie.”

“So like… a girls’ afternoon out? Am I one of the girls now?”

Cipher and Castorice both laugh at that, but ultimately Phainon agrees to their little date. Just as he’s finishing up the dishes, Castorice excuses herself to go to the bathroom. He sits down heavily in her seat and pulls out a cigarette.

“Can’t believe you gave me your damn cat, Cipher. Is it permanent?”

Cipher shrugs, plays with her fidget spinner. “Just for as long as needed.”

Phainon huffs at that, a little amused, and goes to light up his cigarette. “Now I actually have to keep on top of the cleaning,” he muses half-mindedly, more to himself than to Cipher. “Don’t want old Bartholos getting sick.”

His eyes dart to Cipher and he finds her sitting there with a smug grin on her face, like she’s a cat who finally caught a mouse. She raises her eyebrows a little bit, and Phainon groans.

“ That’s why you gave him to me. You’re giving me a responsibility. You fucking babytrapped me.”

Cipher howls at that, thoroughly entertained, and puts out her cigarette. “That, and to keep you company. Don’t forget about the insecticide I got you, yeah? Instructions on the label, and it’s pet safe, okay?”

Phainon nods, and there’s not much to say after that. It’s squeaky clean and the air is actually breathable now. He didn’t let them go into Cyrene’s room however– that remains untouched, like a sanctuary to a cold God. He snatched her old water bottle, smeared with lipgloss, before either of them could get to it and throw it away– it’s in his room now. Much like a serial killer keeps trophies of their victims, fingers and pieces of scalp, so does he keep trophies of Cyrene; little trinkets of a past life lived only in half, perhaps a little mundane, and maybe if he prays over them enough, if he loves them enough, they’ll come to life in the shape of a real girl.

Phainon watches as Bartholos struts into the kitchen, stretches, and plops down on the floor with his belly up. He wants to go and pet his tummy, but suddenly his hands feel very heavy.

Cipher offers to drive Castorice home, and she accepts because it’s already very late and Polyxia’s caretaker’s shift is gonna end soon. She’s riding passenger princess in Cipher’s black car, watching how the cat-shaped air freshener swings back and forth on the rearview mirror. Her mouth is dry when she opens it to speak,

“Cipher, why do you have the keys to Phainon’s apartment?”

The answer comes quickly, not hesitated, as if Cipher expected her to ask this and has rehearsed her answer, “That’s none of your business, Castorice.”

Yeah, Castorice thinks as she deflates, leaning her head against the window. I’m starting to think it’s not.

When they arrive at her apartment building, Cipher offers to walk her to her door and Castorice politely refuses, already feeling a bit tender and very sad. The climb up the stairs to her apartment seems like it will never end, stairs stretching endlessly, until finally she hears the sound of Love Island playing from one of the apartments; Polyxia likes trashy TV, and the sound of couples bickering pulls Castorice back into her own body.

She walks in and says goodbye to Polyxia’s caretaker. Castorice looks towards the living room and catches her sitting there in her wheelchair, watching the TV with rapt attention. She joins her, laying on the couch, and doesn’t say anything– simply turns her gaze towards Love Island , watching without paying attention, giving her eyes something to do. Just puttering.

They’ve always been very different, her and Polyxia. Castorice was really into Harry Potter and Polyxia was really into Twilight. She was an awkward, gangly highschooler with acne while Polyxia won Miss Freshman . Castorice is into staying at home and writing fanfiction, and all of her friends that aren’t from work are autistic queers on Discord. And clearly, as today has proven, her IRLs don’t like her that much; which is fine, she doesn’t like herself either. There’s something very wrong with her, she’s come to accept this. Castorice chews on her bottom lip anxiously.

”You’re upset.”

Polyxia’s text to speech startles Castorice, and she actually jumps. Polyxia chortles in response, because she can’t quite laugh anymore, but where there’s a will to tease your little sister there’s a way.

“How could you tell?”

”I can read your mind, remember? Come on. Tell me what’s wrong.”

So she does tell her, because Polyxia is kind and easy to talk to and very very lovely. The night ends with Castorice sitting on the floor, weeping with her head in Polyxia’s lap, the way she’s done since she was little. She takes her sister’s hand and places it on her head, because Polyxia can’t move it on her own anymore and Castorice really needs the physical contact right now. She feels her fingers twitch weakly on her scalp, almost imperceptible.

She feels very stupid, because Polyxia’s life was uprooted last year and everything she had was taken away from her -her job, her make-up artist side-gig, and her friends- and here’s Castorice crying to the Dying From Motor Neuron Disease girl because her fwiends don’t wike her vewy much .

“... This is a little stupid, Polyxia, I’m sorry,” she says after she’s calmed down a bit, “I shouldn’t do this to you.”

When she cranes her neck to look at Polyxia, she finds a question dancing in her eyes– ”do what?” she asks without asking.

“This–” and Castorice gestures broadly at herself, red faced and puffy-eyed, “It’s kind of a non-issue, right? Like yeah, maybe they’re closer to each other than they are with me, but they’re still my friends and– you know, they invite me out and stuff sometimes, so that’s nice. It’s just– I’m sorry. You have a lot on your plate, um, I shouldn’t put my silly little problems on you.”

Polyxia has lost nearly all of her movement, but some of her facial muscles are still working. She frowns a little, and her eyes dart to the screen mounted on her wheelchair. She blinks at it for a while, before her robotic voice sounds out again.

”What’s that supposed to mean?”

“You know, um,” Castorice shies a little, “The ALS? It’s kind of the elephant in the room. You’re– y’know. It’s hard, I mean… I imagine it must be. I imagine you must be feeling a little scared. Very scared maybe.”

She hears Polyxia hum, actually hum, because she can’t talk anymore but she can still make little sounds. It’s a wise, thoughtful sort of hmm . A long while later, she speaks again.

”No, not really. I’m not really scared for myself, not anymore. I mean, I’m more scared for you. I made peace with this, you know, and once you make peace with it, it becomes bearable. It’s just life, and I’m enjoying it to the fullest. I don’t really think about dying anymore. It’s no use, so I just make the most of my time here. Besides, I have you. I just worry about what you’ll do after I’m dead more than I worry about the death itself. I don’t think this is stupid at all. I know you’re lonely, and I wanna hear about it.”

“But… don’t you get sad, at all?”

”Of course I get sad. I get sad sometimes and if I had a choice, I’d rather not be sick. But I don’t have a choice, and the point is, Castorice– my sadness isn’t more worthy of being Sadness than your own sadness just because I’m sick and you’re not.”

Castorice just listens. Her sister went to a lot of therapy in the early stages of ALS, and it shows– perhaps Castorice should’ve joined her. Polyxia blinks at her screen some more.

”Honestly, I’m mostly just bored. Mrs. Elena is nice, but she’s not much of a conversationalist. If I feel well tomorrow, I’d like to join you and the others.”

Polyxia doesn’t really have friends anymore, and that shit makes Castorice feel homicidal. She got diagnosed and every person in her life kind of dipped– her long-term boyfriend, her college friends, all the people she used to buy drinks and gifts for. Castorice is not proud to say that she got blocked by all of them because she went into their DMs and told them off. Polyxia really didn’t appreciate that, said ’I don’t need a knight’ , but she still found it very funny. ’Just, y’know, fuck them.’

Yeah. Fuck them.

So, Castorice wipes her tears and agrees that it would be lovely if Polyxia were to join them tomorrow. She texts her group chat with Phainon and Cipher and they agree as well.

The next day is good. It’s really good actually– it’s so good that Phainon is getting a little paranoid and he thinks that he’ll get run over by a car or hit by a meteorite or something, because nice good days just don’t happen to him.

They all meet up early for brunch at a nice local place, the cozy sort with vines growing on the red brick wall. It’s one of those hot hipster places for self-important assholes with twirly moustaches that are a little too performative about liking ’big tiddy goth girls’ . But hey, credit where credit is due– their drinks are top notch and they make a mean frittata.

Which is exactly what Phainon orders, a tall glass of mango lemonade and a frittata. Castorice orders an XL chocolate oreo milkshake and a huge portion of french toast, because she really wants diabetes and is on a quest to go into a diabetic coma before age thirty. Cipher is more normal about it, ordering a rösti and a macchiato.

Polyxia, on the other hand, orders three bottomless mimosas in glasses as tall as her head– to Castorice’s desperation.

”I already ate at home,” she says when Phainon teases her about it, ”And I don’t like anything on the menu anyways. What the fuck is a quiche Lorraine?”

Phainon loves hanging out with Polyxia, and has done so many times before. Most recently on her and Castorice’s birthday, one month ago, when he got a little drunk and let Polyxia bum one of his cigarettes. He held it to her lips while she smoked. Polyxia joked that the hardest part of having ALS was having to give up smoking. When Castorice found them like that in the kitchen, she just sighed all disappointed and walked out.

Polyxia is funny, like really funny, and she’s a bit daring, a bit of a wildcard. He met her in the earlier stages of her ALS, when she was wheelchair bound but still had movement. She always teased him, leaned with her cheek on her hand and called him ’pretty boy’ and said she’ll ‘take him for a ride on her wheelchair if he sits in her lap’ .

Honestly, she’s exactly his type, because he likes people that he can volley with and that bully him a little. He also likes people he can bully, so they have to be able to take it. All of her flirty teasing got to him at some point, and he had a little schoolyard boy crush on her for a bit. It was some nine or ten months ago, so not long after they met. When he told Polyxia about it, she just laughed.

’That’s nice and all, but I’m gonna die and I’d rather not waste my time.’

’Don’t you mean, you’d rather not waste my time?’

She grinned then, all toothy. ’Be serious, Phainon. No time spent with me is time wasted. I’m a fucking catch.’

They spend a good several hours at the brunch place, chatting and laughing. Cipher seems to be in a good mood, and Castorice is… trying her best. Something seems to trouble her, but Phainon doesn’t want to put her on the spot. Instead, he chooses to let her be.

The waiters are getting a little bit antsy when it becomes clear they’re not gonna order anything else, so he asks for the note. Phainon ends up fighting with Cipher about who’s gonna pay and comes out victorious.

“Come on, I can’t have a lady paying. That would be ungentlemanly.”

“Tastefully misogynistic, Phainon,” Cipher chastises with a roll of her eyes.

The brunch place is pretty close to Phainon’s place so, with the sun setting slowly behind them, they decide to walk to his place and watch a movie. The weather is perfect; one of those lovely July afternoons, where it’s warm but not too warm. Every so often, a breeze blows and ruffles Castorice’s long hair. It gets all in Polyxia’s mouth. Phainon is very content and very fond.

They watch Five Nights at Freddy’s when they get to his apartment, because that movie sounds positively stupid and very funny.

And by God, yeah, it’s awful. It’s so bad. Polyxia laughs so hard at some point that she chokes and gives her sister the scare of a lifetime. Cipher can’t stop making dumb comments, and at some point she starts imitating the actors in the movie. Phainon laughs so hard he’s crying, and even Castorice looks less troubled than before, all tickled pink.

After the movie, they hang around for a bit more. Bartholos walks out from Phainon’s bedroom, does a big big stretch, and jumps up in Polyxia’s lap. She makes a little surprised sound, and then demands that somebody help her pet him. Phainon grabs her wrist and strokes Bartholos’ back with her hand, making him meow and purr.

They file out not long after, because it’s getting late and it’s really dark out now. They say their goodbyes, he sees them out of the apartment, and then Phainon is left sitting alone on the couch, and…

He feels good. He feels really, really good actually. It was a nice day. He laughed a lot. It was nice seeing Polyxia again, and it was nice spending time with Cipher when they’re both sober and not suicidal.

His apartment feels like a home again, at least for now, and he’s kept his promise– he swept the floors today, because the insecticide worked and there were a bunch of dead bugs on the ground. He fed Bartholos, changed his water bowl, and even made his bed. As he goes to retreat to his bedroom, he does not linger by Cyrene’s room anymore. Doesn’t even think about it, honestly, as if it’s just some room in an apartment and not the womb holding all he’s ever loved.

Phainon is half-asleep as he lays in his bed, stuck between wakefulness and dream, when he hears the wooden boards outside his bedroom creak. A little dazed, he cracks his eyes open. The light on the hallway is turned on, though he can swear he turned it off. Golden light rushes through the door, a little cracked, sending a perfect luminous stripe towards him.

She stands in his doorway like she used to when he was small and needed comfort from a nightmare. Cyrene looks barely seven years old, dressed in her Disney princess pajamas, clutching the plush blanket given to her as an infant. She asks him, softly as if not to wake anyone at all, to protect her from monsters. She says she's scared; he can save her.

For a moment, he can almost convince himself he's still the best brother in the world, invincible and protective, smart and capable, and now, finally, bigger than her. Older than he was when she was seven, just like he always wanted to be. He thinks that it’s his turn to be the older sibling, the big brother, and so he pushes away his covers and invites the specter into bed.

She presses up against him, small and cold like a cut of pork hanging from a hook. She sleeps, or so he thinks, because her breathing gets very steady and very slow. Phainon’s hands come to comb through her short hair, and he gazes up at the ceiling because he knows that if he looks down at her, she will be gone. So, he looks the other way, as he’s always done, and thinks of nothing. Polaroid caught in time, a perversion of a memory from some twenty-two years ago– Cyrene, seven years old, much braver, and him, five years old, suffering from night terrors after their parents’ divorce. She always pretended to be the scared one, always asked him for comfort so that he’ll still feel like a big strong boy at the end of the day.

He is making it dirty, somehow, by indulging this. He knows it’s wrong, and fake, and a sure sign that he’s completely lost his mind. But she is so small, so precious, as she cuddles up to his chest, sucking on her blankie, her tiny hands fisting into his shirt. She is very, very cold, but if he pretends very, very hard, he can almost trick himself into thinking it’s her. If everybody believes a lie, then it might as well be reality.

He tries very hard to believe this lie, and he tries very hard to love the little Cyrene. He rubs her back and tells her all the things he never did when she was still alive. Perhaps he can love her back to life.

And as he sinks into this moment, falling asleep with the twenty-two year old ghost of his sister’s child self, he thinks can almost forgive himself for killing her.

The thought of it has him heaving into the trash for the rest of the night.

Sometimes, if you’re unlucky, your sister dies and it’s all your fault. Sometimes, you go a little crazy about it and you end up hallucinating her child self.

You still have to go to work.

Chapter End Notes

Right, so, this took longer than expected, and this *chapter* was longer than expected so I had to break it down further. Being 15k words into a fic and not having the other half of the ship even show up is kinda crazy but I promise you this IS Phaidei-centric. However, a lot of things have to be set beforehand, most importantly the relationship between Phainon, Cipher and Castorice and the one between Castorice and Polyxia, since those 2 are foils to Phainon and Cyrene.

Some tags have been added. Click here to see them. Some more trivia/information.
