Chapter Notes

Yay Mydei is here!! I went into a fugue state and wrote 14k words in a week. I really love this fic. Enjoy! :^) I think I'll take a little break after this lol

IMPORTANT!!!

Mydei's POV is just a general TW for child abuse and domestic violence/domestic abuse. There are some gore-y/disturbing descriptions of Gorgo's dead body, but it's a little surreal as well.

Hyacine has been in this room for the past four consecutive hours and at this point it’s getting a little hard to think.

This room being the HR office of FLAMECHASE, and by four consecutive hours she means, you know, doing her job.

Her job –Human Resource Specialist– is usually easy. It’s the sort of job you clock into and kinda dick around all day most of the time, because once you get past the hurdle of boring paperwork, it’s smooth sailing. And she can’t really complain, because she started as a customer support analyst, AKA one of those people getting yelled at for eight hours a day. She trained under Anaxagoras (put a pin in that, we’re going to come back to Anaxagoras) and then swiftly transferred to the HR department as soon as possible (having a bachelor’s degree in Psychology helped, thankfully), because holy fuck that was truly unbearable.

So, objectively speaking, HR is easier than on-call customer support. You just protect the interest of the company (while saying you’re actually for the employees but that’s bullshit and Hyacine knows that’s bullshit) and yeah, you’re an active cog in the capitalist machine moreso than other employees and most days you end up wasting the time of people in need for a job; but she has to eat and the call center was making her suicidal.

Hyacine thinks of the HR lady wojack Phainon showed her and yup, that’s pretty much her. At least she fought for thirty minute lunch breaks and actually won them from higher management, with the support of Anaxa (this isn’t it, keep the pin there) and Aglaea. So she can at least rest a bit easier at night.

There is a time in the year, however, where the job goes from boring and bearable to downright hellish. And that time period is the summer, when they do recruitments .

Together with the rest of the HRlings they sift through job applications and recruitment sites, they pick the most decent-looking candidates, and then Anaxa handles the actual interviews, because they’re the head of the HR department.

That’s kind of where the issue arises. Anaxagoras.

So, and this is well-known in the company, the head of HR (that being Anaxagoras) and the head of Customer Support (that being Aglaea) are locked in a six-year-old dick measuring contest that started when they were both bottom-of-the-rung call center operators.

There are two steps candidates have to go through before they can be hired: the interview with Anaxa and, if they pass that and Anaxa considers them good enough, the final interview with Aglaea.

You see, the thing is, there is nothing those two love doing more than pissing each other off– and this has only worsened now that they both have actual positions of power in the company.

Anaxa will pass forward under-qualified candidates or people that are outrightly bad in the interview so they can become Aglaea’s responsibility. In turn, Aglaea, the hiring and department manager, will hire them so that they circle back to being Anaxa’s responsibility. Anaxa baits her,  Aglaea bites back, and the company gets burned.

It’s a vicious cycle. It’s snake eats tail. It’s Ouroboros.

Now, this is a fast-moving industry anyways, and it’s kind of cannibalistic. They are on a constant rotation of people quitting and new people joining, and the standard for quality isn’t sky high. They’re not exactly looking for the Albert Einstein of customer service, and most people that are bad at their job end up quitting after a few months anyways– so while Anaxa and Aglaea’s petty back and forth doesn’t actually affect the company that much, it affects Hyacine. Why , you might ask? Well, you see–

Lately there’s been a push from senior management, the people that are above Aglaea and Anaxa but below the board of directors, to expand their customer support analyst team and get more people on-call. HR’s workload during recruitment season was heavy anyways, and now it’s doubled -or even tripled- in size with the recent expansion. Besides the recruitment itself and the interviewing, they’re also tasked with doing quality assessment for their employees and the new trainees alike. This means listening to recordings of their calls.

Training in FLAMECHASE lasts two weeks (way too little), and then the new kids are put in this Customer Support Limbo for another two weeks where they’re still technically in training but they’re also very much taking real calls, though for fewer hours a day and less pay. This is less of a test run and more of an acclimation period, like putting a frog in water and slowly turning up the heat. Technically speaking, based on this two week period, the heads of HR and Customer Support are supposed to work together and choose who gets hired for realsies and who gets axed.

Alright, that’s great. Refer to fig. A, labeled “Anaxa and Aglaea’s school playground fight”.

This means a lot of people that are utter dogshit and have no interpersonal skills are being hired.

Now, how does this affect Hyacine?

Because now she has to spend eight hours every day contemplating the inherent goodness of human nature as she listens to the newly hired trainees’ calls, and wow. Wow . It was bad before, but now? She’s genuinely questioning her life choices. It’s painful, it’s downright painful, and Hyacine spent her early twenties volunteering in psychiatric hospitals and doing counseling for kids with cancer– this is the most emotionally affected she’s been by a job. The second hand embarrassment is so bad she has to close her eyes and rock back and forth, like actually self-soothe , to get through a call. It’s a young boy, nineteen years old, who ended up yelling at an elderly customer because she was too confused and too slow to speak.

Her break is coming up, so she takes off her headphones and turns her head up towards the ceiling, her eyes still closed. She hopes that the sky will come crashing down on her right now. She prays to whatever God will listen for this misery to end. Jesus Christ, she needs a cigarette and she needs Little Ica.

After a bit, she comes back to herself, stretches her arms, and looks at Anaxa who is seated across from her. They’re looking worse for wear. Actions, meet consequences. Their head hangs low, hands all running through their green hair, pulling and tugging. The capitalist fuckmachine has thoroughly broken them. She’s witnessing a thirty-seven year old gown-ass adult having a nervous breakdown because a nineteen year old kid that they pushed through is bad at his job.

“You know, Anaxagoras–” Hyacine starts, “I remember this kid from recruitment, and he was always fucking awful. You don’t need to keep doing this, oh my God, just give in and do your job properly!”

Anaxa is silent for a minute and then, slowly, they lift their head to look at her.

“I hope I get glaucoma in my other eye and I hope it kills me.”

“...Okay, well, first of all– glaucoma is not fatal. Second of all, like, answer me?”

They sigh and lean back in their chair, arms crossing at their chest. “No.”

“What do you mean, no ?”

“I won’t let her win.”

“Win– This isn’t a competition, Anaxagoras.”

“It is now, and I won’t let her win it. I’m committing to my stance.”

Hyacine frowns and wow, wow , she really wants to kill them right now. There’s a pen next to her, and if she’s fast enough–

“You’re being ridiculous. We’re supposed to be professionals.”

Anaxa simply huffs and turns their head away defiantly. “Hmph.”

Hmph?! What the fuck kind of answer is that? Is this real? Is her life real? Is this a dream? Perhaps she died and this is her own personal hell.

A beat of silence passes.

“...There is that one guy that’s pretty good, though,” she says, perhaps trying to find some light in this eternal damp darkness she’s caught in.

“Which one? The Kremnoan?”

“Yeah, the uhh–” she sifts through some papers, looking for the guy’s CV. “Mydeimos, yeah.”

She sees Anaxagoras contemplate for a moment, moving their head from side to side as if weighing the pros and cons. “Yes, he’s serviceable. Kind of a natural at it.”

“Yeah,” Hyacine agrees.

“Mhm. Yes.” Anaxagoras agrees, as well, because for some reason they always have to have the last word. Hyacine looks at them. Anaxa looks back at her.

“...Good talk,” she grabs her bag and her cigarettes, “Buckle in, teach, because we have four more hours of this bullshit left.”

She pats them on the back on her way out and, as she hurries down the hallway, Hyacine can hear the sound of Anaxagoras’ maniacal laughter resounding throughout the office– they have completely lost it.

Deserved, if she’s being honest.

He is small, very small, two years old or perhaps two and a half. He is outside his house, on the little patio, and the grass is a little gross and a little yellow. But it’s a nice summer afternoon and the world has taken on that sleepy, blue-ish haze before the sun sets. He is playing with his trains, making them crash into each other and making boom noises. He sees a small bug crawl on one of his trains and he squishes it with his thumb. He laughs, a little high-pitched and a little chubby cheeked. Mommy and Daddy are yelling inside the house, and he’s not sure what it’s about because he never really understands. He just knows they get very, very upset with each other and sometimes they break things.

Sometimes they would be eating dinner in peace, him with his nuggies and mashed potatoes, Mommy with her glass of wine– and all of a sudden, Daddy would slam the table with his fists hard enough to make the cutlery jump, and he would start screaming at Mommy about this or that. And then she would get mad too, and then she would also start screaming back. That’s when he hits her, and then she hits Daddy back.

”...deimos…” his uncle calls from somewhere very, very far away. He gets up, wobbly because he’s a late bloomer and he just learned how to walk. He goes a bit farther than his father allows him to, usually. He stares down their driveway, looking for the source of the sound.

”Mydeimos…” a bit louder now, clearer. He would like to answer back, but the issue is he can’t talk yet, and it’s making Mommy very sad. The boy shrugs and figures it’s nothing, so he goes tiptoeing back to his trains. Sits down heavily on his knees and reaches sideways for his favorite green train.

When he turns back and looks down at his toy railway, Mommy’s cold face stares up at him, her eyes glazed over and milky-white. Her lips are blue-ish purple, frozen in a scowl, and she looks so so scared, kind of like the pictures the nice lady at the therapy center showed him. Dark red bruises extend on her pale throat, dragons grappling with each other, something far bigger and far more sinister than he can understand. Flies fall out of her gaped mouth and maggots suckle on her breasts, rotten black milk, spoiled, foul. Bile and insects and everything the Heavens have deemed unholy– swimming like koi fish in a pond. Her stomach is swollen, bloated like a sailor’s corpse, and the world smells of pomegranates.

She is very blue all over. She looks very sad, a twin of the Virgin Mary icon Daddy makes him pray to every night. He does not notice how his hands, adult and streaked with red ink, are gripping her by the throat.

Mydei wakes up in a cold sweat.

It’s a recurring dream, and he’s had it since he was nine years old. It always plays the same. He’s always playing with his favorite toy trains, and then Krateros calls him away, and then he turns back and he’s killing his mother.

He groans and reaches over for his phone to check the time– 6 AM. He woke up one hour before his alarm, because fuck his life. It’s his first day of work too, and he’s made sure everything went right the day before. He ate well and went to sleep early and didn’t even workout, just to make sure he gets a good night’s sleep.

Unfortunately– The Horrors.

Mydeimos would like to linger on them and maybe it would do him some good to unpack literally any of that; however, if he does, he won’t be able to function for the rest of the day.

So, deep breath. Lock them away tight. Take a second and compose yourself, Mydeimos, because you’re supposed to be a functioning member of society. Sometimes your mother is murdered and you have to go to work.

Work. Yes. He pushes the covers away and weakly gets to his feet– he’s a little unstable, like his body doesn’t want to cooperate with his mind. What does his body know? It’s always betrayed him in some way or another, always a little malformed and misaligned. Something like a half-assed abortion made by a lazy doctor.

Kitchen. Go make something to eat. Do something , don’t think very hard.

Hephaestion is in the kitchen, scrolling idly on his phone. There’s a half eaten sandwich in front of him. He raises his fox-like eyes at Mydei when he hears him approach, and smiles.

“Good mornin’, Mydeimos~” he chirps, sing-song.

“Why are you up?”

Hephaestion stutters a bit and then laughs, taken aback. “What, are you a cop? Am I not allowed?”

“No? I’m just asking. It’s early.”

Mydei opens the fridge while Hephaestion answers him, “Couldn’t sleep well. Was a bit anxious for you, little lion. New job, very exciting!” Mydei scoffs like that, a little amused, and fishes out the bacon and the eggs from the fridge.

“I don’t believe you. Want something to eat?”

“Nah, I ate.”

Hephaestion sounds like he expects something, but Mydei can’t tell what it is so he doesn’t say anything. Instead, he focuses on his eggs and bacon. “Is Ptolemy up?”

“You know he is. It’s re-sit exam season, I don’t think he slept. Leonnius and Perdikkas are at work, though. Peucesta’s still asleep, because–”

“Peucesta doesn’t have a real job, yes I know,” Mydei finishes for him, smiling a little. “Ptolemy! Come! Food!”

Ptolemy looks like a zombie when he drags himself out of his room, doesn’t even say ’hi’ or ’good morning’ . Simply sits at their long dining table, next to Hephaestion, and waits to be served. Mydei doesn’t mind, because he likes serving them. He sets down a plate of bacon and eggs in front of Ptolemy, then goes to cook his own food.

“You call me to breakfast like I’m a dog…” Ptolemy grumbles through a mouthful of food. Hephaestion laughs at that and stretches his lithe arms. “That’s ‘cause you become a dog when exams roll around, my friend. You know pulling all-nighters won’t actually help you study better, right?” He reaches over to boop Ptolemy’s nose, which the other really doesn’t appreciate. He pulls away with a scowl and slaps Hephaestion’s hand away.

They get into a little catfight, like girl characters do in old cartoons, as Mydei sits down with his own plate.

The other two chat about something, and Mydei’s not really paying attention because he’s still a bit bristled from his dream.

(”Mydeimos,” his mother says as she reclines on the bed, back leaning against the headboard. She’s nursing a black eye, holds a pack of ice against the bruise. She grabs his arm suddenly, roughly, and it hurts. “Don’t get yourself involved with men, okay? You have to promise me.”

“I’m not– I don’t…” he tries to say, a little startled, because he doesn’t even know he likes boys yet– how does she?

“Promise me, Mydei. You have to promise me.”

And she sounds… scared, and rushed, like she’s running out of time. Like her livelihood, her wellbeing, depends on this– on him.

“Okay. I promise,” he says then, not really knowing what he’s promising.

But it makes her smile; a soft, weak smile, tired. Pained. And then she pulls on his arm, gently, and he stumbles into bed with her. Naturally, almost by instinct, he goes to nuzzle into the crook of her neck where he can smell her strong, cloying perfume. She’s always smelled so good, kind of like gunpowder.)

“Hellooo??” Mydei is pulled back to reality from where he’d zoned out by a series of snaps and the feel of Hephaestion’s light hand on his shoulder. Mydei flinches away  from it, but the other man remains unfazed. “I asked you something, Mydei~”

He blinks, dizzy and not quite himself, and tilts his head at Hephaestion.

“I asked if you’d bake me a cake today.”

Mydeimos frowns, stuffs his mouth with a forkful of bacon. “Sure, I will, but why?”

Hephaestion scoffs at him, and Ptolemy gives him a tart ’Dude.’

“Uhh, like, check your phone? You can’t actually be serious.” Hephaestion sounds a little amused, and there’s no actual bite in his words, but Mydei is starting to get anxious. He could swear it was the 10th of August, not the 11th. Mydei reaches over for his phone, turns it on, and–

It is the 11th. That’s right– he remembers now. Miss Aglaea told him that he’ll start on ’the next Monday’ and he never cared to check for the specific date; and honestly, time has always been weird for him. Dates mingle and melt into each other in his head, hours pass in the span of minutes. Sometimes it’s 10 AM, and then he blinks, and suddenly it’s night and he’s in bed and twelve hours have passed by him without his knowledge. A life half-lived, glimpsed in brief moments of time. He tries to conjure up Gorgo’s face, find the similarities between his and hers, the arch of his nose or perhaps the curl of his eye– instead, he finds himself holding chalk dust, taste astringent, crushed to pieces by hands bigger than his, crueler than his.

Ah well, it’s been like this since he was a kid, so he doesn’t think about it too much.

It’s probably fine.

That being said, it’s the 11th of August. Mydei feels embarrassed and he has the decency to drop his fork and blush; hang his head in shame.

“You’re right,” he mumbles, “I’m sorry, Heph, I could swear it was the 10th. Happy anniversary.”

Hephaestion’s hand squeezes his shoulder, and his voice gets very gentle. “It’s okay, my friend, I’m not mad at you. I was just teasing, really!” He gives Mydei a little laugh, airy and a bit weak. “Stop pouting, it’s a happy day,” Hephaestion pokes his cheek, “One whole year cancer-free. Who would’ve thought I’d live to see the day?”

He lifts his face to Hephaestion’s and– he is skinnier than when they first met, yet fuller than he was last year. Irreversibly changed, not necessarily for the worse but– different. A little more tired, a little older, his skin more pallid than it used to be. His hair is short now, and Mydei has always liked his long hair.

(“You can’t cry,” he told him then, through his oxygen mask, “Please don’t cry for me, Mydei. It’s going to be okay,” and then his hand, now small like a child’s, came to hold his.

And it only made Mydei cry harder because his hands were so little now, he was so little now, like the shadow of the boy he met in college. Both teenagers and both stupid, taking photos of each other making out with ancient marble statues and getting chased away by the museum’s security guard. Hanging out with their toes in the cold water of a lake. Watching Rupaul’s Drag Race together and getting a bit too into the competition. Cooking all sorts of tasty meals for him. Kissing that one time when they were both very drunk and very lonely.

“It’s not going to be okay. You might die.”

“It’s okay if I do.”)

“ I did,” Mydei says, remaining steadfast. “I knew you could do it.” Hephaestion’s face softens, eyes crinkling at the edges and smile stretching like a wheat field; luminous, golden. “That’s very sweet, Mydei, thank you. So… cake?”

“Yeah,” Mydei beams, “Cake.”

They return to their rooms after breakfast, because it’s still early and there’s nothing to do. Hephaestion and Mydei bully Ptolemy into finally going to sleep. Not long after, Leonnius and Perdikkas return from their work; Leonnius from his graveyard shift as a security guard, Perdikkas from his overnight shift at the hospital. He’s already cooked breakfast for the two, and it’s waiting in the kitchen looking all appetizing.

Mydei starts getting ready at 7 and by 7:30 he looks presentable– more than presentable, honestly, he looks handsome . Like he’ll leave a good first impression on his coworkers, which he’s not really interested in doing; he has all the friends he needs right here.

Mydei sits on the edge of his bed and reaches into his drawer for his pill organizer, pops open the tab labeled ’Monday’ . Paroxetine for his depression. Venlafaxine for his panic attacks and anxiety, because for some reason the Paroxetine doesn’t quite cut it. Lithium, his mood stabilizer. Two of each, one of Lithium, a nice handful. Down they go– he doesn’t take water with them. He likes how bitter they taste.

The perfect serotonin cocktail, specifically designed by the greatest mixologist of our times (his psychiatrist), to make sure he doesn’t end up on the news or as a ‘Kremnoan Young Adult Suicide Statistics’ entry. Did you know it’s the second-leading case of death among Kremnoans aged 18-25? He’s almost out of the danger zone, being 25 exactly, but– oh, dang it, it’s also the second leading cause of death among Kremnoans aged 26-35.

Just for good measure, Mydei also takes a Vicodin (totally legally prescribed and medically necessary, thank you very much) for his back, because it’s kind of bothering him and he doesn’t want it to be a whole thing later.

Ah. He’s perfectly souped up now, thinking at a molasses pace. Sedation. Quiet. Mydeimos breathes out, long and hard, laborious. His doctor said he’s reaching his body’s upper limit of lithium intake and that they should slowly ease him off of it. They're talking of less intense stabilizers. A mix of Quetiapine and Lamotrigine, fiddling with the dosage. It will make him tired and hungry and very, very quiet; more than he already is. Maybe it will quell some latent psychosis that wants to claw its way up his brainstem. They're waiting for it -the psychosis- like a sailor's wife waits for the clouds on the horizon; like he used to wait for the schoolbus every morning. The psychiatrist sat him down very gravely one day, a routine check-up, and had told him, succinctly and sternly, that ’he is two very bad days away from full-blown schizophrenia, and the Lithium isn’t helping.’

Mydei’s been putting the weaning off, because if he doesn’t take his Lithium, he’ll start breaking shit in the house. But he waits for the psychosis to ruin his life, one box to tick on a very long list he has to fill out with his taxes; waits for it like a heated lover, legs spread, saying ’Yes, fuck me! Fuck me hard!’

And, at the end of the day, why not? What difference would schizophrenia make? He’s been half a person since he was nine, and only a quarter person since he was twenty-two.

His mouth feels like cotton.

Hephaestion knocks on his door frame and leans against it. Mydei blinks himself out of his haze. “Looking good. You nervous?”

“No, not really. The job’s not difficult.”

“Let me walk you to your car, I feel like stretching my legs a bit.”

They are silent as they make their way to where Mydei parked his car, a block or two down because his usual parking spot was taken. Asshole. It’s not official, but it was his . As he fiddles with the car keys, he hears Hephaestion sigh behind him. “I’m going back to work next week,” he announces, out of nowhere.

Mydei stops in his tracks, and a familiar anxiety brews in his gut– he’s not sure what that’s about. He’s afraid, but of what? “All out of sick days?”

“Unfortunately.”

“Are you gonna be okay?”

“Dunno. I’m kinda nervous about rejoining polite society,” Hephaestion tries to joke, but his voice falters. “But what can ya do? The work never ends. So much time has passed, I think I even forgot how to do math.”

Mydei doesn’t know what to say. He stands there, a little still, hands steady on his keys, not moving to open the car door nor turning to look at Hephaestion. He’s scared, yes, and maybe it is the change. Hephaestion is safe at home, lounging on the couch, close to his CPAP machine and the ontology ward. What if he gets sick away from home, at work? What if the cancer comes back? Mydei is not sure what cancer’s got to do with a boring accounting job, but his body seems to think they’re intrinsically linked.

To be fair, his body can’t tell the difference between a minor disagreement between friends and being threatened with a gun.

He wants to swoop Hephaestion up and tuck him into his pocket, somewhere very far away from the rest of the world where nothing else can hurt him again. His hand is trembling on the key and he’s gripping it with force, and he was really really small and weak and he couldn’t have protected her even if he tried and he should have gotten help sooner and he shouldn’t have ran away so far but he didn’t know any better and he tried his best–

(A pool of blood soaks his bare feet, cruor stuck to her pretty golden locks, the ones he loved brushing and braiding so much. He looks next to the oven and finds a piece of her scalp there, hair still attached to it. He grabs it, brings it to his mouth to kiss, and stuffs it in his pocket.

Even while dead and pale and faceless, she is so beautiful.)

“You know, I never thought– ah, nevermind. You have to go to work.”

“No,” Mydei prompts him, “Go on. I have time.”

“I really thought I was gonna die. I was this close, too. I never thought I’d get the chance to work again. Maybe I’m actually a little excited, now that I think about it. Life after cancer is kinda boring.”

Mydei kind of feels like crying a bit, and he really doesn’t like this. Somehow, it feels like Hephaestion is leaving him, even though he’s worked that job since college. It’s stupid. He feels like when he was a kid and his mother told him to stay very still and very silent in his room while she went to deal with his father.

Mydei chews on his bottom lip. “I’ll make you that cake today,” is all he says before he gets in his car and drives to work.

It’s been about a week since his Professional Grade, Peer-Reviewed, SSS+ Mental Breakdown™.

Phainon had expected something to change but, ultimately, the only thing different is that now he’s suicidal in a clean apartment– which, objectively, is an improvement. Unfortunately, it’s not enough of an improvement. He haunts the halls of his home like a dilapidated ghost, and some nights he sleeps in Cyrene’s room, surrounded by her clothes and her smell and the small pieces of her flesh strewn about like bait for wolves. His reflection in the mirror is misshapen, as if distorted. He has grown dragonlike, terrible, frightening.

But– but ! If there’s one thing Phainon is good at, it’s lying; well, actually, it’s more accurate to say acting. (what even is the difference?) Either way, he’s good at acting, because Phainon is a blank slate that people can take turns pissing on and drawing the vague shape of a human. He has many roles in his repertoire, such as: The Good Friend, The Sexy Lover and, his favorite, The Perfect Employee.

Because, yeah , the work is shit and there's little to no chances of actually advancing in the company, so it’s kind of a dead end job. It is, however, something that he can be good at. And he really, really needs to be good at something.

Phainon has been the most consistently well-performing employee since he was hired, and has won Overall Employee of the Month four times in a row!

Which means absolutely jackshit because the pay is still ass, and he’s still up to his neck in debts, but hey– a man’s gotta have his pride, and this at least makes him feel like he’s useful . He’s making the multi-million company even more millions. He’s capitalism’s most well-behaved dog, who’s a good boy oh you are yes you are, now work for nine more hours like the obedient little puppy you are. He can practically feel Khaos Petridis scratch behind his ear and maybe feed him his cock for dinner. Or something like that.

There’s a tale about a man punished for his transgressions against the Titans, forced to push a boulder up a mountain for all eternity, but Phainon doesn’t think that’s thematically relevant to his current situation.

It’s an exciting day, however, because today they get a new batch of employees . It’s thirty or so newbies, so it’s about to get a little more crowded– not all thirty of them are gonna be working from the office, of course, since they fully have the option to work remotely if they so wish. Only severely mentally disturbed people, such as Phainon, Castorice, and Cipher, choose to spend nine hours of their day in this hellhole.

Still, it should be at least five or ten newbies puttering about.

Cipher is walking lightly on her desk treadmill,  a leisurely pace, while Castorice is sitting on his desk. Phainon is leaning in his chair, trying to look all casual. The desk next to him, on his right, has been mostly vacant since Hyacine transferred to HR– not a day goes by where he doesn’t deeply mourn the loss of his very best number two love and peace desk neighbour work best friend , mostly because in a sea of troubled individuals, she’s actually pretty well-adjusted. People have taken over that spot every so often since she left, but none of them stuck around for long.

He’s already starting to see some new faces and it’s actually pretty thrilling, because positive social interaction gives him the best head high and makes him feel like he’s worth something for once. Phainon loves performing, especially for new people, especially when the prize is a good first impression and a boosted ego. God knows he needs it.

“Ya think there’s gonna be any cute new girls, hmm~?” Cipher mewls, stretching a little and fiddling with the speed on her treadmill.

“Cipher!” Castorice says, utterly scandalized, “Workplace relationships are inappropriate!”

“Yeah, okay, Castorice,” Phainon chimes in, teasing, shifting so he can sit with his cheek in his hand, “I’ve read that Ratiorine office AU you wrote~”

Castorice gasps in horror and brings her hand to cover her mouth. “S-shut up!!” and she turns so so red, kind of like a tomato; cute Tomatorice.

“What the fuck is an ay yew ? Who’s Ratiorine…?” Cipher makes a face like she just spoiled rotten eggs.

“Oh~?” This is his favorite thing in the world; teasing Castorice, because she gets very flustered and very funny. “You don’t know~? Castorice writes these smutty, erotic little stories about the characters from a video– hmph?? ”

Phainon’s efforts to embarrass Castorice are cut short by a soft, cold hand slapping against his mouth– the victim has jumped down from the desk and has fully put him in a headlock, surprisingly strong for her size, one arm around his neck and the other coming to cover his mouth and stop him from talking. She’s squeezing his throat. Hard.

What a way to go.

“Stop talking!! Oh my God!! What is wrong with you?!” she screeches, like actually screeches, and Phainon can’t stop laughing from under her vicious assault. “Cipher– Cipher!! You didn’t hear anything, okay??” Cipher is laughing too, doubling over, snorting all unladylike.

“I don’t know, Princess Homebody, I’m kind of interested now~” Cipher manages to say after she catches her breath a bit.

Phainon is actually getting a little lightheaded because holy fuck , Castorice is skinny and all, but she’s powerful . So he pulls the ultimate move, and this is a dirty trick he’s not proud of– but desperate times call for desperate measures.

Phainon lolls his tongue out and starts licking her palm.

Castorice is relentless though. His last line of defense crumbles like a child’s Jenga tower; instead of letting go and jumping up saying “kyaa~~ yucky!!” , she squeezes harder.

“...Castorice?” a gentle, soft, accented voice breaks through the chaos. The light at the end of the tunnel– his salvation, a modern-day Jesus Christ of Nazareth.

Aglaea heactuallydoesn’tknowherlastname of FLAMECHASE INC.

An elegant browbone leading into the gentle slope of her nose, cloudy blue eyes, perfectly styled hair, golden manicured nails. She’s always dressed fashionably, all ruffled white shirts and expensive materials and gold accents; and smells so good too. “Why are you killing my Employee of the Month?”

It seems like Castorice has, indeed, added Mydei to it. He quickly adds Mydei’s phone number to his contacts, and starts reading back on the messages he’s missed.

Dummyrice🔮💜 has added Mydei Work

Dummyrice🔮💜

hi guys

i’ve added mydei

he’s new so please be nice to him!! ^_^

Cipher😼😼

im cipher

like a kremnoan shieldmaiden?

Cinny🍰🎀 Dude…

Not. appropriate.

Mydei Work

Thanks for adding me.

No, I don’t have a hot older sister. I’m an only kid.

Sorry.

👎

The thumbs down is pretty funny, Phainon will give him that. In this groupchat, they’re in a habit of sending random pictures of their everyday life, so Phainon starts by sending a picture of him watching Love Island with his dinner, and then another one showing Bartholos napping on his lap. Castorice sends a selfie of her at her second job looking all bored, but says he should catch up with Polyxia one day on all the Love Island gossip. Cipher sends a picture of her cats fighting, and Hyacine sends a picture of Anaxa with their back to the camera, leaning on their cane as they move some papers around, because she’s still at work.

Mydei is a little late, but he sends a picture of a bowl of chocolate cake batter and Phainon groans out loud , because of course this dude also bakes . Is he the perfect man, or what?

It’s quiet after that and Phainon settles into a comfortable mindlessness, watching TV without thinking of anything at all; which is like, the best case scenario for him.

It’s an everyday constant battle for Phainon to just feel fine , and comfortableness is a little bit out of his reach right now. So he’ll have to take it.

As he’s getting ready for bed, and it’s nearly midnight, Cipher sends him a private message.

Cipher😼😼

Phainon

oh no

Cipher😼😼

so new guy mydeimos yea?

Phainon

cipher!!

Cipher😼😼

Phainon

weirdo…

Cipher😼😼

so like??

Phainon

why give it to ME?

Cipher😼😼

Phainon ???

Cipher😼😼

.

Cipher😼😼

Phainon hovers over the Instagram app, unconvinced of what he’s about to do, and then says  fuck it  and types in his username. A profile pops up, and the profile picture is a low-angle selfie of him with his sunglasses on, his long hair in a bun, and the sun behind him.

'Mydeimos Polemos’

Weird last name, but okay. Phaion clicks on it, still a bit unsure, and is relieved to see that Cipher is following him, so she’s not being totally stalkerish about it. He has a whooping 73 followers, nothing new posted on his story, and… he doesn’t seem to be super active on social media. His last post is from three months ago.

It’s a little strange, Phainon thinks as he scrolls through his profile– Mydei uses his account more like a digital photo album than social media. He doesn’t really show off stuff or even posts many pictures of himself alone. There’s a few of him, pretty recent, at raves and concerts, looking devastatingly handsome. Most of the time, however, he posts big photo dumps that seem to have a common theme, and he doesn’t even caption them. For example:

Phainon’s attention is immediately piqued by a picture of two ferrets. One of them is a simple brown sable, the other one has this gorgeous white undercoat with light brown stripes; it kind of looks like it’s made of caramel. The post itself is a photo dump with thirteen slides, and Phainon goes through all of them. Most photos are of the ferrets being silly or cute, playing with each other, but there’s also one video. It’s filmed from Mydei’s point of view and the caramel ferret is skittering around at his feet. He picks it up onehanded, gets up from where he’s sitting, and throws it into a box of packing peanuts. Then he goes back, at which point the ferret jumps from the box and comes to wiggle and squeak by his feet again. Mydei repeats the same action a few times, throwing the ferret into packing peanuts over and over, laughing lightly, until the video abruptly ends.

Another post is a slide with twenty-one photos, all of them being taken at a museum of sorts. There’s pictures of Classic orange-red clay vases painted with black silhouettes, depicting various everyday labours, moments from legends, and religious rituals. One in particular catches Phainon’s eye; Phagousa and their Maenads. The Titan is depicted as a great wave in the middle of the ocean, using their watery limbs to hold up their worshippers –a group of naked, mad women– as they dance and drink and copulate under the starry night sky. Most of the other photos are of bronze and marble statues depicting philosophers, warriors, and Titans. There is one that shows Nikador sitting at Thanatos’ feet. Both Titans are sculpted as humans– Nikador in their battle armor, looking fierce in their crested helmet, staring down at their sword with determination. Above them, veiled in a shroud and with their face hidden, Thanatos is gently holding a flower.

There are also pictures of ancient swords, spears, engraved shields, and even an intact suit of Kremnoan armor.

Phainon likes this kind of stuff, though he’s not very good at history. Math was always more his speed, but in a perfect world, he’d be rich enough to collect antiques.

Before he scrolls further down, he stops and thinks he should follow him because he’s starting to feel a little creepy . He even goes to message Mydei about it privately.

Phainon

hey dude

cipher found your instagram and she shared it with me

is it cool if i follow?

Mydei Work Okay.

👍

But I don’t post much.

Well – now that he has permission, Phainon happily presses that follow button. A few minutes later, Mydei messages him back.

Mydei Work

neikos496?

Cringe.

👎

Phainon

listen.

i made it when i was young so i didn’t care about it being cool

just used my last name

Mydei Work

You know you can change it, right?

Phainon

i got attached to it

Mydei Work

Why do you have so many followers?

Phainon

i’m simply HIM

Mydei Work

👎

Phainon gets a notification saying Mydei followed him back. Somehow, this feels like a victory, though Phainon doesn’t know what he’s competing for or even what he’s competing in .

Phainon returns to instagram and clicks on the next post, which is from exactly a year ago. It’s a simple, short video– a man who is not Mydei is in a hospital, and he’s very happy. The nurses are standing around him, cheering and whooping, and he’s very, very frail– skinny like a twig, bordering on fatal, his olive skin pallid and washed out. His head is wrapped with a scarf and he’s so weak that he needs a walker to get around. He rings a big bell on the wall, and that’s when Phainon realizes that this is an ontology ward, and this is a video of Mydei’s… friend slash brother slash boyfriend after finishing his cancer treatment, officially in remission. This is very intimate, and Phainon feels like he’s not privy to this moment, like he’s intruding on something very happy and not meant for him; still, he thinks it’s cute that Mydei felt the need to post it on his personal instagram.

Further down his page, there’s a photo dump of his tattoos– and now, that one’s dangerous. Phainon knows he shouldn’t click on it because the cover photo is of Mydei’s broad back, and just that is making him a little hot under his collar. He is just a man though, and God has made them weak-willed and easily tempted. He’s also a terminally bisexual man at that, which doesn’t work in his favor; so he clicks on it and takes a good gander.

A tapestry of woven muscles unfurls before him, perfectly interlocking like they were hand-stitched by a legendary artist. Every dip and divot is accentuated by those red streaks, as if a bloodied and wanting mouth has traced the lines of his muscles, and they are so striking against Mydei’s tan skin– sun-kissed, tawny and smooth like clay waiting to be kneaded. One of the streaks slips down from his powerful ribcage, a red ribbon coaxing the eye to his tapered waist, cooing ’Touch me, see how I bend and sway beneath your palms’ – Phainon considers it for a moment, palms itching to squeeze the two divots above his hips and see the way those muscles shift under his hand. See the way his back might arch, the way Mydei might sigh.

Alright.

Enough of that post.

Phainon’s already in dangerous ‘creep’ territory because he’s three years into Mydei’s instagram posts. ’Just one more’ he tells himself, and then he scrolls all the way down until the very first post on Mydei’s page. It’s from five years ago, and the cover photo is him as a child. He can’t help himself, curiosity gets the best of him.

First photo – Mydei, maybe eight years old, smiling big, looking weirdly plain without his tattoos. He’s a bit toothless and very scrawny, smaller than an eight year old ought to be. He’s holding up a comically small fish and, from the background, he seems to be at a lake. A man’s big hand is on his shoulder, but the photo is cropped and Phainon cannot see his face.

Second photo – Mydei, three years old, sitting in a man’s lap. He is looking off into the distance, fist in mouth. The man is leaning his chin on his head, but it’s also cropped and Phainon can only see his thick black beard.

Third photo – Mydei, seven years old, on his first day of school, looking snazzy in his little suit and his big Lion King backpack.

Fourth photo – Mydei on his first birthday, wearing a birthday hat, cheek pressed against the most beautiful woman Phainon’s ever seen. ’He looks just like her’ Phainon realizes. Her eyes are big, green, crinkled from where she’s smiling with a mouthful of pretty white teeth. Her skin is olive like his, her hair the same strawberry blonde. She looks happy.

Fifth photo – Mydei, fifteen years old, posing with a diploma– first place at the National History Olympiad. Very impressive!

Sixth photo – Mydei, eighteen years old, side-hugging an older man. The other man is rugged, handsome, going gray at the edges of his hair and beard. It seems like he’s blind in one eye.

Seventh photo – Mydei, nine years old. The half-blind man is kneeling next to him, and they are on the porch of a house. The man is smiling, gripping little Mydei by the waist, and Mydei’s whole demeanor is awkward, maybe a little frustrated even. He’s looking into the camera, and he looks very sad.

And then…

Eighth photo – The same woman, much younger, just as beautiful, perhaps a teenager. She’s posing with a younger boy at a beach and, from what Phainon can tell, it might be the same half-blind man from the other photo. He’s a little pimply, a bit awkward, gangly; next to him, she’s radiant, her hair cascading down her back in curls.

Ninth photo – The woman, a stunning bride in a white gown. She’s glowing, the very picture of a new wife, and she’s perfect . Her blonde hair is done up, tied in a high loose bun, and her makeup is subtle, enhancing her natural features rather than painting on new ones. She’s looking into the camera, unsmiling but not unhappy– rather, she is dignified, graceful. Composed only to hide the excitement beaming from every inch of her posture. She’s holding a big bouquet of lilies, and a big golden ring is on her finger.

Tenth photo – The woman in a hospital gown, exhausted, tired. She’s laying down in the bed, holding a small bundle in her arms, smiling down at it warmly.

Eleventh photo – The woman laid in a big cozy bed, looking lovingly at a baby. Her hand is on his tummy and he’s gripping one of her fingers, seemingly wanting to put it in his mouth. Her eyes are so tender, so full of affection, that it all seems so fragile, as if made of porcelain. As if it could all be broken very easily.

Twelfth photo – A little blonde girl, five years old, holding a squirming, crying baby in her arms. The photo is very old, black and white.

Thirteenth photo – The woman, now in her twenties, holding a beer in one hand. She’s toned, hot , wearing a crop top. It looks like she’s at a party and she’s having a lot of fun. The camera captured her while dancing, hand raised above her head. She is slim but not without curves, wearing blue jeans that hug every divot of her body. Her stomach is flat, covered in a thin sheen of sweat, her face a little red with exertion.

Fourteenth photo – The woman, still in her twenties. It’s a selfie and the angle is a little awkward, because it’s taken with a handheld camera. She’s making a silly face, sticking her tongue out, furrowing her brows and crossing her eyes. This one is the most obviously cropped of them, because Phainon can catch another figure in the picture– half of a man’s face, one golden eye, a big black beard.

Fifteenth photo, the last one – The woman, older now, in her late thirties. She’s at a waterpark with Mydei. Mydei looks miserable , like he just cried, and he’s pouting the way kids do. He’s wearing Lion King swimming trunks and a yellow bucket hat with lion (or bear?) ears on it. The woman is standing behind him, kneeling down at his level, holding him by his waist. Her head is on his shoulder. She’s wearing a matching bucket hat. The light in her eyes has dimmed, but still she smiles, as if in defiance of something– reckless, toothy, boyish, a smile untrained in photogenics, sincere as a sunburn. There’s a big black bruise on her shoulder. She’s tired.

Phainon clicks the button on the side of his phone and locks it. He rests one hand on his chest, where his heart is beating very fast. He’s feeling very tender, as if somebody cracked him open and scooped up his heart, leaving only inflamed innards and infections. Rattled a bit, yes, and thinking of all the photos he has with Cyrene and his parents; trips to the beach, high-school graduations, Christmas parties with big presents and magic.

The entire span of a human’s life in snapshots, laid before him, all of the most intimate and beautiful moments; there are very few pictures, he notices. Only fifteen, and the museum trip had twenty-one. His chest feels raw, wounded tight as a screw about to pop, and there’s a familiar sting beneath his eyes where tears are fighting their way out. He could cry, something in him deeply touched, as though little Mydeimos with his toothless smile grabbed his hand and looked up at him, all innocent and naive.

There’s something wrong with those photos, Phainon thinks, they have cast some sort of evil witchcraft on him, that green eyed woman a sorceress; because he feels very fond all of a sudden, as if he’s known Mydei all his life, or possibly he knew him in another life. He wants to gather him in his arms, the big Mydei and the small one as well, and just hold them for a moment. Perhaps love something back into him, maybe something he’s missing.

It’s just– it’s very sad and very small. It’s very sweet , all the little moments of Mydei’s life, the dark corners from where he’s managed to dig up some happiness. He was a fat baby with rolls, and then a small child, and then a handsome young man. Mydei always looked a little distressed in all those photos, upset, something not quite right behind his eyes; fishlike, staring into nothing, smiling because he had to. There was a bruise on one of the photos, he doesn’t know which, a small one on his wrist.

Phainon is not stupid. He knows a memorial post when he sees one, and that’s exactly what that was. He’s done the same with Cyrene, poured all of his love for strangers to see, displayed it on billboards and transmutated it into expensive funerals; hoping that through publicity, through the humiliation of grieving openly, absolution would follow soon after.

It never did; it never does.

That’s not the way Mydei did it, however. It’s not like how Phainon has flaunted the image of his dead sister. The way Mydei did it– it was more noble, more distinguished, like a wound scarred over a thousand times. It was respectful, loving, kind. Photos shared with his loved ones and his friends, her loved one and his friends. A celebration of life, not a blasphemy of one.

The woman’s face is burned in his mind, beautiful and sad like dead mothers tend to be, perfect because she is deceased. A ghost not of a person, but of an entire time; childhood, or an approximation of it. Something golden, delicate, yet fierce as a prowling lioness might be. Always so defiant. He wonders what her perfume smelled like.

(If he were to check, and he does not, the post only has one comment, from one man named Krateros. It reads: ‘She was beautiful. The best big sister.’)

Phainon opens his phone again, navigates directly to Mydei’s DMs.

Phainon

are you asleep?

Mydei Work

We just met.

Take me out to dinner before you booty call me at midnight.

Phainon

lol

no, it’s not like that

i was just thinking

you work out right?

do you wanna work out together sometimes?

or are you the type of guy that’s married to his gym?

The typing bubble pops up and then disappears many times until Mydei messages him back. It takes him nearly a minute to reply:

Mydei Work

👍

Alright, that’s good.

That’s a start.

Chapter Notes

This is shorter than usual, I had more planned for this chapter but I felt like it had a lot going on already. Please enjoy! I love reading everybody's comments so please leave a comment if you have anything to tell me or ask me ^_^ Things are starting to pick up, it's getting a little erotic, so uh. Beware? Enjoy?

!IMPORTANT!

Alright, so-

First and foremost, I'm starting to introduce elements of Mydei's sexual assault, such as his slight aversion to touch. It's referenced throughout the first half of this, but he doesn't name why it happens. I've also briefly edited the previous chapter to reflect this, just a small line about him flinching. It's not a huge part of his trauma response, but it's there and I want people to be aware that it's happening.

There's also a scene of homophobia and child physical abuse. It starts with "You're no damn sissy," and ends with Whatever, it's probably fine.

Phainon has a big mental breakdown in which he EXPLICITLY SELF-HARMS both physically AND emotionally(!!), starting with Phainon reaches for his phone, clicks it open, and ending with Tomorrow is his day off. He spends it in a vicious cycle of drinking and [REDACTED, TW]

The following scene is Cipher's reaction to the above mental breakdown. If you want to skip it, since it's a little heavy, it starts with Cipher is in the middle of a call when she gets a notification from Phainon. and ends with She can’t take much more of this.

Hanging out with Phainon is like hanging out with the Sun.

’He burns too hot’ Mydei thinks, absentmindedly. Phainon, drenched in so much sweat that his shirt clings to him, has turned the speed on the gym’s Stairmaster so high he’s practically running up on it. They’ve been at it for fifty minutes, him on the Stairmaster, Mydei jogging on the treadmill neighboring Phainon. The sting of exhaustion has set in deep in his chest, aching deliciously, his throat dry and parched like a bird in the desert– yet, he does not drink, does not reach out for his bottle of water. His eyes are transfixed on Phainon, and he himself– bewitched. Mydei does not look ahead of him as he should, at the treadmill’s console, because he is pulled in far too violently by Phainon’s gravitational field.

Magnetic. Arresting. He cannot look away from the other man.

“ –and I told the customer, ’Sir, no, I cannot do that for you, it’s against company policy’ and then he– ”

It is incredible how much Phainon can talk. He has been yapping, uninterrupted, since Mydei met him at the subway station. For Mydei, it’s one of those days where words feel like lead in his mouth, where his throat constricts around sounds and he feels like throwing them up in a sickbag. The lights in this gym are too bright, the buzzing of the cheap LEDs incessant and relentless where they flicker above his head. Harsh white light bathes them both in moonlight, making them glow resplendent and melancholy; it feels like a dream.

It all feels like a dream, like he’s seeing the world through the colorless shards of a dimmed kaleidoscope. In this alabaster castle in the sky, Phainon blazes like the sweltering metal beaten into shape by a blacksmith.

Mydei has not gotten a word in, has not even tried (it’s one of those days) , but Phainon has kept himself entertained, chatting with a vaguely Mydei-shaped brick wall and making a game out of guessing his silent answers.

“Not feeling up to talkin’ today, Mydei, hmm? That’s okay, Castorice gets like that too sometimes. It’s a little charming!” Phainon has told him when they met that day, tilting his head unsophisticated and offering him a toothy smile. He reached over then, slinging his strong arm around his neck and pulling Mydei closer; all friendly and affable, as if this was normal, as if Mydei wasn’t constructed from noxious clay. Good-natured even, giving where he was not supposed to give, feeding a ravenous beast. ’No, please,’ Mydei thought, too stunned and too tired to speak; almost afraid, almost desperate. ’I’ll get you dirty.’

With it, Phainon stole the very breath away from Mydei.

He’s been left split in half by it, fractured like this father’s precious china after a day of drinking. A burst blister of a man, raw and tender and spoiled with pus– Mydei tries to grasp at his innards as they unspool from his belly, yet still he finds them twisted and knotted into a gory nest on the floor.

Mydeimos cannot be normal about people. He consumes that which he loves, rapacious and carnivorous; too much when it does not matter, too little when it does, equal parts aloof and clingy. Measuring his attachment style would drive a psychologist to suicide. He has been both the recipient of ’What are we?’ and the clingy asker, three weeks into a relationship and begging on the floor for all that which he is unworthy of.

Mydei has always been weird , he’s come to accept that. Eldricht and eerie like the weeping ghost of a woman haunting an old mansion. He has been the two year old unable to speak, stubborn as he is now with words, the nine year old growing askew and awry like a poisoned vine crawling up an impaling pike. Now, for the past three years, he has grown more twisted still, monstrous, unrecognizable in the mirror; the reflection of a dead fish, bleached and blurred by the strain. A stubborn wisdom tooth, roots contorted and wrenched, unwilling to be pulled out despite the ache.

( ”You’re no damn sissy,” Eurypon had told him when he had been a rawboned seven year old, pulling him by the ear all the way to the car, pushing him inside and slamming the door.

He had caught him and his girl cousins playing in Auntie’s nailpolish, painting each other’s nails. His were purple and magenta. He spent the entire ride back home peeling the polish off.)

Whatever. It’s probably fine.

“Mydei~” Phainon coos, his face dusted pink from his toils on the Stairmaster. “You’re looking at me all weird, what’s wrong?”

Mydei suddenly realizes that he’s been leaning forward, as close to Phainon as their gym equipment would permit. He pulls back in a flash as if the closeness scorched him, the frog realizing he’s boiling, and scowls at Phainon with a scoff; this only serves to make the other man laugh all airy and easy, showing off his cute dimples. Mydei wants to break his finger on his canines.

Slowly, throughout their workout, the words come back to him; non-verbality dissipates alongside with the floating feeling of non-existence, leaving him more grounded, more present. He blinks away the bleariness of disassociation when they’re in the locker room, unwinding from the gym session. Mydei is patting the sweat from his neck away with his shirt when he hears Phainon gasp.

He turns to see Phainon a little doubled over, his loose gym shorts rolled up to the crease of his thighs; he is massaging them. Mydei’s eyes cannot help but wander to them (he is just a man) . He finds a pair of milky white thighs, smooth and supple, peppered with soft white hairs. They ripple with strength with every press of Phainon’s hands, flesh shifting and rolling like tidal waves. They suggest softness, plushness, yet hardness all the same; a concealed predator, enticing a drunk man with a drink and trapping him with the hangover. His mouth dries up, and he is parched, and the drive to surge forward and mark those thighs is overwhelming, pressing on the roof of his mouth. He wants to know how pliable they might be under his teeth, wants to rip the meat off of them.

Mydei pulls his gaze away, up towards the little shocked look on Phainon’s face. ”Mydeimos!” he exclaims, sounding utterly scandalized. Mydei can only tilt his head at this. “I didn’t know your nipples were pierced! ”

Suddenly, he feels very naked– which he is . An unfamiliar heat rises to the tips of his ears. “Idiot, of course you didn’t. I didn’t tell you,” he manages to say with small difficulty, throat atrophied from disuse. He coughs to clear it.

And then Phainon gets that heinous little look on his face, utterly profane, that stupid mean smirk crinkling the corners of his eyes. “Mydei, that’s naughty! What else is pierced?” his eyebrows wiggle, and Mydei misses the implication.

He opens his mouth and lets his tongue loll out, permitting Phainon to see the little ball pierced on it. “Mhh ‘ongue.” For whatever reason, Phainon’s expression only gets more mirthful as if he were a starving man presented with a feast. “Can I touch it?”

Mydei sputters, taken aback, and pulls his tongue back inside his mouth. He thinks he must look a bit like a chameleon at this moment. He flushes properly now, face hot and peachy.

Perplexingly, he actually gives this some thought, entertaining this ridiculous demand. He mulls it over in his head, eyes darting around the empty locker room, and then landing back on Phainon’s sweet, expectant face, his pouty lips. For a reason he cannot bear to admit, Mydei finds that he cannot deny Phainon this. His lips press into a tight line and then, as casually as he can manage, feigning nonchalance, Mydei simply answers, “Do whatever you want.”

The giddiness is practically radiating off of Phainon as he crowds into Mydei’s personal space, pushing him backwards; Mydei’s back hits the wall. Horrified, he realizes that he does not mind this ; and even more terribly, he realizes he craves more as he steps closer to Phainon.

(Mydei is weird about physical contact, jumpy and flighty, hates when people sneak up on him or touch him– on bad days, not even Hephaestion or Ptolemy or the rest of his friends. This is probably fine. He does not think about it, cannot think about it. He does not think about why he doesn’t hate it when Phainon touches him.)

Phainon’s hand ghosts over his jawline as if testing Mydei’s resolve– or rather, asking for his permission. Mydei does not give him the satisfaction of a nod, instead he challenges him to take what he wants; he grasps Phainon’s forearm, neither pulling nor pushing, but applying pressure. Phainon looks bashful all of a sudden, flustered, but he takes the dare hook line and sinker. His previous determination falters for a moment, blue butterfly wings unfurling to reveal something far more vulnerable, far more hungry. Phainon schools his expression almost as soon as he feels it slip from him, filling back with wonted boldness. A small shy smile spreads on his face, deceiving in its tenderness– Mydei can feel its sharp edges stabbing at his back.

With a touch so delicate, so featherlight, that it makes Mydei want to scream at him, Phainon grips his jaw, thumb at his bottom lip. He keeps his mouth pressed close, stubborn to not go down easy– it makes Phainon click his tongue, a frustrated ’tsk’ . “Seriously, Mydei…” he says, playfulness dancing in his voice. He likes it when Phainon is playful. “You’re always so difficult with me… It took us two weeks to schedule this little gym date because you’re so dang busy all the time~”

Mydei furrows his brows and parts his mouth to remind Phainon that he was equally as difficult to schedule with. “You were als– hmphh–”

Quick as Nikador’s lighting, Phainon seizes the opportunity to hook his thumb inside his mouth, running it along his molars. “Well… If they were cats, I would say… yes? They’re laughing and their body language is relaxed. So like, if they were my cats, I wouldn’t be worried.” Cipher shrugs as she talks, downing another sandwich.

This isn’t exactly Hyacine’s definition of a fun day out , but she’s had the displeasure of being friends with teenage boys before she transitioned, and this is kind of how it went.

Except these aren’t teenage boys , they’re grown ass men with jobs and they pay taxes, and oh my God Mydei has Phainon in a headlock now and Phainon is turning purple. “Alright!” Hyacine yells out, grabbing the pitcher of lemonade. “That’s enough, boys, come on! Have something to drink, take a break! ” and then under her breath, “Jesus Christ…”

Hyacine is starting to sound like her sister-in-law when she’s wrangling her kids, except her kids are three and five years old .

They both drop it, almost in an instant, as if they needed a responsible adult to step in. Grown ass men, Hyacine can’t fucking believe this. They straighten themselves out and Phainon starts approaching the girls casually, his stride relaxed, as if he wasn’t about to meet Saint Ica at the Pearly Gates. They’re both flushed pink all the way down to their chests, breathing hard and gasping for air, and covered in so much sweat their shirts are damp.

With all the grace of a toddler, Phainon grabs the pitcher of lemonade from Hyacine and drinks directly out of it, bringing it to his mouth and holding it with both hands– and still, he manages to spill some on his shirt. He slurps as he drinks and catches an icecube in his mouth, crushing it between his teeth and chewing on it. Hyacine immediately thinks of her five year old little nephew, mysteriously sticky all over, his mouth all dirty with spaghetti sauce and his grubby, moist fingers covered in Cheeto dust reaching out for her. Phainon inelegantly passes the pitcher to Mydei, who’s just as badly behaved when he drinks.

Hyacine catches a strange glint in Phainon’s eye and she sees the way his lips curl upwards cruelly; falconlike, a hawk waiting high above the clouds to dip down with ferocity upon an unsuspecting pigeon. Predatory. Ill-intended. Her breath catches in her throat and she starts to get up, but it is as if she’s cursed to move in slow-motion. She barely makes it to her feet before it all unfolds in front of her, all too quickly for her to intervene.

In a fraction of a moment, the very second Mydei is done drinking, Phainon snatches the pitcher away from him and pours the remnants of lemonade on his head, slaps him over the face, and then takes off running. Mydei stands there puzzled for a second, unable to process what just happened, struck dumb. He’s looking at Hyacine all helpless, as if she might have the answer to what just happened. She just shrugs with a sigh and tries to reach and help him, but then–

The fire returns in his eyes, a dangerous determination. He frowns and scowls, his face twisted with demonic grit, and then he chases after Phainon with a growl.

’Back to square one.’ Hyacine thinks as she sighs and sits back down on the blanket. Mydei tackles Phainon to the ground, and they wrestle for dominance.

She hears Castorice gasp softly next to her. “Intricate rituals…” she says, almost reverent.

The boys fight for one more hour, at which point they’re completely spent. They are both red in the face, satisfied with big stupid grins on. Phainon’s shirt is a bit torn and hanging off his shoulder– Mydei must’ve ripped it at some point in their struggle.

Castorice and Cipher spend some time at the water fountain, washing the dried stickiness out of Mydei’s hair while Hyacine chides Phainon, all in good humor. “No, Phainon! Bad, bad Phainon!”

Later in the evening, things calm down, and only because Mydei and Phainon are so tired they actually just go to sleep, all of their energy spent. They fight over who gets to lay their head in Cipher’s lap, to which Cipher simply says that she has enough space on her thighs for both of them. They nap as she’s playing with their hair, scratching their scalps.

Hyacine smiles at the sight. This was nice. Her phone jingles and lights up, so she goes to check the notification– it’s from their work groupchat.

It’s from Tribios.

Oh no.

Tribios

Hey, guys!

I have something exciting to share

Surprise! We’re gonna be team building in nine days

I rented this nice table at this pub/bar thing

Good drinks, good food

So please make sure you attend! It’s to improve social relations between us

And I’ve already booked the babysitter and cleared your schedules for that day, sooo

You don’t have much of a choice

❤️

Agy is coming as well

I invited Naxy too, but…

You know how they are

Alright, toodles! ❤️

Chapter End Notes

i don't know how i feel about this chapter. it feels like the emotions are all over the place but, honestly, phainon's emotions are very volatile. he's fine one moment and then incredibly suicidal the next, and then 10 minutes later he's back to normal and ready to have a picnic date with his friends. i guess that's reflected in the fic? shrug

mostly this chapter was meant to set up mydei's and phainon's dynamic, but then uh phainon took over and derailed it. so i decided to break it down into more parts

shoutout to my beta reader/editor/bestie gael whos literally mydei in terms of mental illness. they called me, and i quote, " a gay mentat who wants to memorize a man's ball smell so bad you write 40 thousand words about how he wants to kill himself"
