chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

This was supposed to be one entire chapter, however it was getting long (over 14k words) and it's. Heavy. This chapter and the next one are very heavy, this is the blister popping, and I felt like there needed to be a break between The Horrors 1 and The Horrors 2. It's going to slowly get better from here on out.

!IMPORTANT!

This chapter has a general big TW for SELF HARM, SUICIDE, SEXUAL ASSAULT Below are the specifics vv

Click me

For all of its faults, of which there are many , FLAMECHASE’s break room is actually kind of nice. They just got a brand new kitchen set, new fridge, counters, sink, even a small oven; full renovation. Their coffee machine is old but trusty, the professional barista kind, and there’s a smoothie maker as well. There are high-quality cherrywood coffee tables circled by soft beige armchairs, mustard-yellow barstools around the island, and they even have a vending machine with snacks and drinks.

It’s all very… corporate millennial, chevron-patterned tile floors and huge stickers of “inspirational quotes” on the walls (Phainon’s personal favorite is “A dream doesn't become reality through magic; it takes sweat, determination and hard work”. God. He should kill himself in front of the board of directors.) Cringiness aside, it’s a cozy little place away from the hustle and bustle of the call floor.

Phainon inserts the coins into the vending machine and selects the number for ’Coca-Cola’ because he’s genuinely addicted to it. Good yummy cola. Castorice is next to him, pouring the fourth sugar packet into her coffee– which, by the way, is 70% milk anyways. She’s just drinking milk with sugar at this point and it just so happens to be vaguely coffee flavoured. Mydei is waiting for them in one of the armchairs, scrolling on his phone all stoic and mysterious. He’s absent-mindedly chewing on his home-made lentil salad because he’s like, a health freak and super strict about carb intake and good nutritional value and all that. One time, Phainon asked him how he got that body of his and Mydei answered by scoffing and saying “It’s 70% diet and 30% training.” – which is factually incorrect, because Phainon is built the same and he eats like a fussy toddler.

Cipher is not with them, though they did invite her to spend their lunch break together. She said she’d rather smoke five cigarettes and get some pastries from down the street, claiming that she’s too lazy to walk back all the way to the break room just to hang out. “What?” she said then, eyes a little mean, “We hang out all the time anyways, do I have to spend every waking moment with you?”

Cipher gets like that sometimes. She pulls away and stops answering her messages for days on end, makes excuses to not spend time with him or Castorice. If they ask her out for drinks, she claims that she has to take care of her cats. If they suggest going for a walk in the park, she says she has other plans with her ’other friends’ ; Phainon knows that’s bullshit, because he knows she doesn’t have other friends, not since her wife took the friend group in the divorce. Her only other friend is Hyacine, and Hyacine is too busy with her job and her TikTok account to chill with them.

Phainon reckons that the only reason she hasn’t completely ghosted them yet is because she has to see them every day at work. Still, Cipher is funny and easy-going and is down with all of his bullshit ideas most of the time so he’s just enjoying her presence, even though he knows it won’t last forever.

He has a bad feeling about it this time, however. She usually sends him memes throughout the evening after they’re off work, or pictures of her cats, or she just sends random messages in their groupchat. He even asked her to play League together and she blew him off, which never happens because Cipher loves nothing more than to carry with Rengar jungle or K’sante top. It’s been dead silent since the last time they talked– which was when he had a suicidal breakdown, so… Phainon sighs at the thought of it. He kinda deserves it, or maybe she needs some space and time which is like, conceptually fine, but emotionally it’s making him want to rip his hair out.

Phainon knows it’s selfish to push her and intrude on her like this. He just hopes that if he waits long enough she’ll come back.

Phainon sighs, long-suffering, and Castorice pats him on the arm. The vending machine has spit out his cola. He reaches for it and they join Mydei together, each sitting in an armchair.

“So,” Phainon cracks open the bottle, letting the acid get out. “Tribbie’s team building tomorrow. Excited?”

Mydei just lets out a non-committal grunt, but that’s just how he communicates sometimes. Castorice shifts uncomfortably and brings the coffee cup to her lips. “I don’t know if I can make it,” she says, blowing on it to cool it down, “It’s kinda late, and my sister’s caretaker leaves at 8 PM. So. You know, I have to be with her.”

Phainon hums into his coke, relishing in the refreshing acidic taste. After a big, big gulp, he shifts to lean his head on Castorice’s shoulder. Just really gets into her personal space to bother her, because bothering the fuck out of Castorice is one of his basest needs; it’s kind of like how, every time Bartholos yawns, he sticks his finger in his mouth. She sighs but permits it. “Why don’t you bring her with you? I’m sure Tribios won’t mind, and the table is big enough to accommodate one more person.”

Castorice clicks her tongue. “Is the place, uh, accessible? Does it have a ramp? Elevator?”

Phainon bites the inside of his cheek– he has not considered that. Does Castorice consider that every time she goes out with Polyxia? Wow. He’s a little embarrassed for not thinking about it. “I looked up the place online,” he answers, “It’s kind of a fancy pub-bar situation, not old money fancy but like… Millennial rich hipster fancy, I guess? It’s in one of those old historic buildings, so I don’t… know if it has a ramp. I haven’t seen one, haven’t looked for it.”

“Then we can’t make it.” Castorice says, and she’s all heated up and angry all of a sudden. She shrugs his head off her shoulder and Phainon backs off. She’s pouting, and not in the cute Dummyrice way, she’s actually upset, eyebrows furrowed, staring into her coffee as if it killed her family. “That’s fucking bullshit. I can’t go anywhere with her.”

“That’s… not her fault.”

Castorice whips her head around so fast that her ponytail hits him square in the mouth. When he meets her gaze, the look in her eyes is fierce like he’s never seen before. “Of course it’s not her fucking fault, Phainon. I’m not mad at her , I’m mad at–” and she gestures broadly, at the world around them, “Everything else.” She leans back with a sigh, takes a sip of her coffee. Phainon looks at Mydei for help, but Mydei just keeps scrolling on his phone.

Something something laying in the bed you made. Alright. Phainon retreats more into his seat, shrinking like a kicked puppy

“Castorice,” Mydei speaks up all of a sudden, barely caring to lift his head from his cheek. He’s still looking into his phone. “Don’t be cross with him– he’s just a little peeved that I’m stronger than him, and it’s making him act stupid.” Castorice cranes her neck to look at him, struck dead in her tracks. Who the fuck says ‘cross’? Phainon is actually so stunned that he does an entire 180 and turns to face Mydei fully. He cannot believe his fucking ears.

“No, you’re not.” Phainon says simply, warning in his tone, signaling that there’s no argument to be had here. He’s not taking the bait.

“Yes, I am.”

Phainon huffs, kind of like an old dog sighing as he’s gearing down to sleep. This is incredulous. Preposterous! Utterly despicable! Phainon wants to grab him and push his head into his salad. “No. You’re literally not. We’ve been to the gym together, we lift the same.”

Instead of being a man and replying to him, Mydei’s eyes flit to Castorice– God , she looks so miserable, eyes wet and tired, her mouth droopy. She looks like she hasn’t been sleeping well. The corners of Mydei’s mouth crinkle in a little smile, and he’s all handsome dimples and beautiful arched nose. “Don’t you agree, Castorice?” and he has a lilt to his tone, one that always indicates play . Easy-goingness, ”let’s just have fun” .

Castorice sniffles a bit, her eyes darting between the two men, and then she just kinda gives a half-hearted, weak chuckle. “..Yes, Mydei, I think I do.”

Phainon inhales sharply and leans back into the armchair, hands gripping his knees. Alright, so this is how they’re playing it. Wow. Wow . They’re ganging up on him. This is betrayal.

Mydei stabbing him in the stomach and Castorice stabbing him in the back. That’s fine. Years of League have taught Phainon how to 2v1. He shifts towards Castorice and grabs her hand. “Castorice,” he starts, solemnly as an aging king, “We have been best friends for almost a year. We trained under Anaxagoras together. I was your first friend . There’s no way you think he’s stronger than me, didn’t I carry that new couch you got? Up all those stairs?”

It’s true. Castorice got a new couch some three months ago, and she was worried about getting it up the stairs when it arrived– to which Phainon, of course, offered to help her out. He is strong, stronger than the average man. That’s him, Phainon Neikos, professional strongman, and pinnacle of health– if you don’t account for the smoking habit, or the drinking habit, or the not-eating-or-sleeping habit, or any of his habits. Still, he managed to carry that couch up several flights of stairs and didn’t even break a sweat.

Castorice laughs, wipes at her tears, and lifts her bare shoulders in a shrug. “I don’t know, Phainon, I don’t remember that… And Mydei’s arms are larger.”

Phainon drops the heartfelt act, pulling his hands away from hers and raising them up like an innocent man accused of murder. “ WOW, OKAY! First of all, they’re not that much bigger, second of all, like– that’s not all it takes to be strong, you know? My back and thighs are bigger.”

“That’s because you’re overcompensating, Phainon.” Mydei leans in all predatory, like a lion waiting to strike. “Admit it. You can’t lift a couch, I don’t believe you.”

“I– this is bullshit , I literally did it! Castorice!!” and he points a finger at Mydei, poking him right between his pecs. Castorice is laughing heartily now, amused and carefree. “I can lift a couch one handed. Matter of fact, I can lift fourteen couches in one hand and Bartholos in the other.”

Mydei leans in closer, further into Phainon’s personal space, and his face is so close – Phainon blushes a bit, all pink like a virginal princess. Then Mydei meanly laughs in his face, a loud singular ”HA!” , before backing out. “I believe you about the fourteen couches, but I don’t believe you about Bartholos.”

Castorice snorts next to him. “Every time that cat jumps off the bed, it knocks the earth off its axis.” she chimes in, giggling. Phainon likes it when she giggles, because she snorts like a little pig.

Phainon doesn’t forget this whole Bartholos ordeal, though, because the second he steps into the apartment after his shift is done, he goes hunting for that damn cat. He finds him licking his paw in the hallway, completely unaware and just as fat as he last saw him nine hours ago; what was Cipher feeding this thing? Bartholos senses his presence and while he is usually the lovey-dovey type, all rubbing against his legs and purring and shit, today he knows he’s in danger. Cat’s intuition or whatever Cipher calls it. Bartholos slowly turns his stupid head up to look at Phainon, who’s standing in the doorway like a serial killer from the bad slashers Hyacine likes. The cat’s big dumb round eyes lock in with him, orange to blue, fire and water. His paw is still suspended in the air. His cute little pink tongue is sticking out just a bit. Blep. Phainon almost feels bad for what he’s about to do to this poor innocent creature. Almost .

None dare make the first move.

A western whistle plays from somewhere in the distance. A tumbleweed rolls in front of them. Phainon’s fingers twitch, and he brings his arms out slowly slowly …

It then happens all at once.

He leaps towards the cat at a moment’s notice. Bartholos yowls, perhaps in fear or perhaps it is a warcry, and he bolts away. He skitters in place at first, his paw pads unable to find any purchase on the polished hardwood floor, but then his razor claws come out and those give him the oomph to propel his body weight; he leaves little scratch marks on the floor.

It’s a legendary chase– except, no it’s not, because Phainon is, you know, a human being and Bartholos is a cat. Phainon is bigger, stronger, heavier, faster, and has longer legs; Bartholos, on the other hand, has lost the genetic lottery on every front. Fat, ugly, misshapen with really short legs and a big belly so he just ends up looking like a rectangle on four sticks. Phainon grabs Bartholos by the sides and lifts him up into his arms. He’s meowing and squirming and very unhappy.

Phainon has a point to prove though– and a plan to make it up to Bartholos later. Phainon holds the tomcat under his arm like a fucked up clutch as he sets up his phone’s camera, leaning it against the kitchen counter, and sets up the timer. He manhandles Bartholos so that he’s perched on his hand– just as the timer is about to run out, he lifts him up towards the heavens, and the camera snaps a series of pictures in quick succession. He sends one of them, the best one, to Mydei.

Phainon

[Attachment.jpg]

told you i can do it

Mydei starts typing almost immediately, as if he was expecting the message.

Mydei🦁

Photoshopped.

👎

“This fucking guy…” Phainon mutters under his breath, and at this point Bartholos is screaming and clawing at him. Too bad, fat guy, Phainon just clipped your claws the other day. You are helpless. From Bartholos’ point of view, the gentle giant that feeds him is rattling him around for the purposes of impressing his weird crush situation. Horrifying. Phainon switches his phone to recording mode and pressed the red button.

“Okay,” he says into the camera, “I’m gonna prove to you it’s not photoshopped, dumbass.”

He lifts Bartholos again, and Bartholos is looking really funny right now, holding onto Phainon’s arm for dear life with his dull claws and looking around with his big eyes for help.

He keeps bouncing his arm up and down as if he were weightlifting. Once he feels his muscles getting sore, because yeah, he’s strong but this is still ten kilograms of pure fat and muscle, he lets Bartholos down. The torment is over, little one. Daddy proved his point. The cat runs away and hides under the couch.

Phainon sends the video to Mydei, and Mydei, once again, responds right away. Phainon wonders if Mydei is sitting under his covers with his phone in hand, waiting for his messages like a worried war-wife, giggling all schoolgirl-ish when he gets a notif. Probably not, though.

Mydei🦁

Poor cat.

You’re cruel, Phainon.

A small pause.

Mydei🦁

He reminds me of my ferrets a little.

Phainon

i saw them on your instagram

what are their names?

Mydei🦁

The sable one is Nikador, the light brown one is Kokopo III.

Phainon

the THIRD?

what happened to kokopo I and II

Mydei🦁

The War.

Phainon

???

Mydei then immediately sends him a picture of the cheesecake he’s eating. What the hell, sure.

Mydei was not exactly laying under his blanket and giggling ”all schoolgirlish” every time Phainon sent him a message. Instead, he was sitting leisurely at his dinner table, stuffing his face with cheesecake and huffing fondly every time Phainon sent him a message. He pushed his buttons further because he really likes how whiny Phainon gets when he’s mad.

Now, a few hours later, he is huddled between Peucesta and Leonnius, shoulder to shoulder, presenting his case before the Council of Five Gay Men. Peucesta looks like he’s about to murder him. Leonnius is squinting at Mydei’s phone and zooming in on the photo Phainon just sent him, the one where he’s holding Bartholos up.

“Phainon is just like that, Peucesta. The boyish, charming type.”

“Bro, he finger-fucked your mouth– your words, not mine, and now he’s sending you pictures and videos of him in a tight short-sleeve number where he’s flexing his arms.”

“That’s all correct.” Mydei answers.

“Right, and you’re still asking us if we think he likes men?”

Mydei simply nods, shrugging a little. He has completely exasperated this man– Peucesta throws his hands up and leaves the room. Hephaestion, on the other hand, looks extremely entertained. He’s sitting on the armchair next to them, legs folded under him. “Mydei~” he coos in that voice of his, “You’re so sweet and innocent!”

Leonnius seems to have thoroughly investigated Phainon’s photos, both the one with the cat and the gym selfie they took back then. He returns Mydei’s phone to him and nods sagely. “He’s a fruit.” he announces like a judge giving out the verdict. Guilty of gay, and the sentence? Capital punishment. Mydei presses him on. “Why do you say that?”

“He’s got a gay face. Anyways, what’s for dinner?”

…Very enlightening.

“I’m making spanakopita.”

Dinner rests heavy in his gut by the time he’s all set in bed. He’s full and content. The blue light of his phone illuminates his face in the darkness of his room, painting it pallid like moonlight– as with most nights, he’s messaging Phainon.

Phainon likes sending voice messages and short videos because he’s ‘too lazy to type’. Mydei looks forward to them, because Phainon is nice and funny and he’s got this all encompassing quality to him; the world stops and revolves around him, everything reduced to the 0s and 1s that make up their messages. He captures every room he’s in with his personality, so colossal, so bright. Mydei likes being around him because Mydei gets to be silly with him– he loves his friends, don’t get him wrong. They understand him in a way Phainon never will, being Kremnoans, and it’s not like he’s not himself when he’s with them, it’s just…

He’s a different Mydeimos. Still him, but just another side of him. Calmer, more stern. He has to be in order to put up with Peucesta and Hephaestion’s bullshit, with Ptolemy’s bad moods, with Leonnius’ flamboyance, with Perdikkas’ pessimism; and he loves all of these things to death about them, all of their quirks and flaws and the little details that make them them . He wouldn’t change them for the world. There is a space in his heart engraved with their names, and it will be forever there no matter what happens, what pulls them apart or brings them together.

But Phainon is different too, in a refreshing and exciting way. Newer. His endless facets fascinate him, an onion with infinite layers. He wants to know what he looks like bare and naked and full of filth, wants to know how he gets angry and upset, wants to know how pretty he is when he cries. Wants crawl into his ribcage and poke at his ruby red heart, too big for his own good. Break open his beautiful skull and see what nebulas pour out. He wants to dissect Phainon beautifully, and see all the parts that match up with his, all the ways in which they are alike– all the ways in which they are different, too.

He sighs wistfully into his pillow. He’s had crushes before, most notably on Hephaestion when they were both dumb college kids, but this, too, is different– he is different. Older, meaner, a little more chipped in all the wrong places, growing uglier by the day, less of anything and more of nothing.

Mydei keeps replaying the most recent video Phainon sent him. It’s shot from his point of view and it shows Bartholos happily gulping down one of those Churu purees. He’s getting it all over his whiskers and his snout. When he’s done, Phainon puts aside the tube and starts petting behind his ears, which makes Bartholos purr like crazy. ”See,” Phainon texted him alongside the video, ”He’s not mad at me at all.”

Mydei is fixated on the video, because Phainon’s lovely slim fingers are in it. He’s got beautiful hands, large but elegant, like a pianist. His nails are short, manicured, well taken care of. Phainon is very tidy in general, almost sterile in quality, like he takes very good care of himself but only because he wants to hide something. Mydei glimpses the ragged edge of a scar stitched closed, vertical, pale and raised against Phainon’s smooth wrist. He hadn’t noticed it before, hadn’t thought to look for it either. He feels a strange kinship over it, the intimacy of the razor, the fascination with watching blood drip down in droplets; he knows it, bears the marks like Aquila bore the Sky, smaller and more subtle, horizontal (all of that to say; less deadly) . Mydei has noticed that Phainon sometimes has trouble flexing his thumb, and now that he thinks about it, his grasp on objects is unstable at best. Yes, he remembers now– Phainon sometimes randomly drops things, completely unprompted and for no apparent reason. He complains of pain in his wrist and his arm. Mydei hums. Distal median nerve injury, most likely. Common with this suicide method, but his isn’t severe. It could be fixed with surgery.

His gaze fixes back on those fingers, supple and alluring. Mydei remembers them soft to touch, uncalloused (unlike his own), gentle. They felt good on his skin, on his arms and on his jaw. His caresses were inquisitive, looking to explore and not claim; barely-there grazes that were both stubborn and timid. He sighs into his pillow. It has been a long time since he’s been touched lustfully by someone, three years to be exact, and even then, it was different from how Phainon did it.

Phainon asked.

Mydei’s never really enjoyed sex, it was something he did but never really understood . To be fair, though, none of his past lovers were exactly good at it either. They were all hurried and kind of selfish, and Mydei felt like he was more so stuck in a whirlwind than sharing a moment of passion with someone.

But he liked the attention, at least. The way it could almost feel like love if he pretended very hard. He liked feeling useful, like he was good at something for once. It was a nice little lie.

And then, well…

Mydei suddenly thinks of the weight of Phainon’s fingers in his mouth, how they pushed down his tongue and caressed his teeth. The heat of Phainon’s chest against his, his beautiful flushed face filled with wonder, and everything was so mellow and so meek . The way he stroked his nape and lingered down to rest his hand on his shoulder, the way he was breathing so hot and sweet. He looked absolutely wrecked, the poor thing, as if sticking his fingers in Mydei’s mouth and just petting his jaw was the best thing there ever was. Mydei loved it. It was more exhilarating than any blowjob he’s ever gotten.

So why, now, is he feeling like throwing up?

The enormity of his desire disgusts him.

All of a sudden, he feels like he is too small for his skin, like it’s ill-fitting. Like there are a million bugs skittering under it, an entire bevy of them, flesh-eating; he feels them from the crown of his head to the tips of his toes, skittering. The only remedy, he thinks, must be ripping his skin off. Letting squirming maggots eat it, and regrow a new epidermis. A clean one. Untouched. Unsoiled.

When his gut twists with nausea, it is in the shape of Adrianos.

”What a mark he’s left on you! Woe is you, Mydeimos, that you must carry it around! Always with you. Never apart.” The chorós sings, star-like, the cruel Fates unspooling the tragōidía of his life. Oedipus Rex. Antigone. Philoctetes. He unfolds as if by the pen of Sophocles. Uselessly stuck in this cycle, vicious Mobius strip, eternally looping back onto itself.

This is all it is. This is all it will ever be. This is all he has become.

Mydeimos slams open the door to the bathroom and falls to his knees in front of the toilet, as if he could vomit out all of the illness inside him.  The labour comes up empty, and he ends up dry heaving with his head in the bowl. Peucesta must’ve heard him retching, because he peeks out of his room and comes to see.

“You good, Mydei?”

Mydei’s hands are shaking where they are gripping the porcelain toilet, and he has become damp all over. His shirt clings to his body, wet on the chest and on the armpits as though he has just ran a marathon. His face has taken on the veil of pallor, growing white and hollow– carved from cheese, harsh and unpretty. He looks at his friend with tired eyes, molten gold dimmed into daffodil yellow. His lips are cracked. Peucesta regards him strangely, equal parts worried and bored; he has this long black hair, bone-straight, a face marred by piercings, every inch of his body covered in tattoos. Thanatos themselves come to take him, Mydei reckons, yet he is not so lucky.

“Yeah,” he blubbers out, “I’m good, just… the pie. It didn’t do me good.”

“Ah…” Peucesta seems unconvinced, but unwilling to press further. Mydei does this sometimes– used to do this often. He thought he had moved past it, but clearly hasn’t. “Alright, man.”

The brief walk back to his room is wobbly, and then he collapses into bed like a corpse thrown into a pauper’s grave– heavy, as if his bones were weighted down with steel. He sinks into the mattress, but not as if it were a fluffy cloud– he sinks on it as if it were made of nails, impaling him in all the good pressure points to leave him unmoveable, paralyzed, and numb. If that were possible, he could grow roots here, become dressed in robes of moss. Flowers would grow out of his fingernails, white lilies– or perhaps something less innocent, deadly nightshade or oleander. He could sleep then, the King of The Woods, as Georios slept after the earth was formed.

He could sleep forever.

When Mydei reaches for the small razor in his nightstand’s drawer, he does not do it in a panic or a haze. He does not despair, he never has. He reaches for it calmly, as if it was just simply another one of his daily deeds, like buying groceries or washing the dishes. Something that simply has to be done. He pats around the drawer’s bottom for it, and when his fingers find its sharp edge, Mydei stops to consider it.

You see, he has this app on his phone that counts the days since he last self-harmed, and Mydei just broke one continuous month. And despite it all, despite the wall that stands between him and reality, he was proud of it. Happy, even. He likes seeing the number get bigger and bigger, strangely enough. Maybe it infected him with a bit of self-worth, who knows, but it’s enough to halt him.

Alright, no cutting. His therapist will be very proud. He resorts instead to biting his hangnails until they bleed, which is not cutting and it means he doesn’t have to reset the count.

And it still gets the job done, too.

The light bulb in his therapist’s office flickers above his head. Its light is yellow, sickly like jaundice, and it bathes the entire room in an eerie glow. Mydei is on the couch, clutching a throw pillow in his arms and idly playing with the tassels around its edge. In front of him sits his therapist, a stern-looking older woman, legs crossed. She’s holding a spiral-bound red notebook in her hands, and she has been holding it every session for the past five years. Sometimes, as he speaks, she will write down something in it.

Mydei is not speaking now, however, so she is not noting anything down– he is not speaking because he is transfixed by the light fixture. It’s one of those modern abstract lights– Mydei thinks that it looks like a legless jellyfish, or perhaps a frozen nebula exploding. The lightbulb keeps flickering, and he can hear the electricity humming inside it. He blinks uselessly at it, mouth a little open.

Mrs. Sofia clears her throat, and he lazily drags his eyes to look at her. Her face is unreadable as it has always been. “Mydeimos?”

“...Yes?”

She sighs, though not out of frustration, and yeah– there she goes. Writing in her notebook. Her hand comes to push her glasses up, and then she’s back to boring into Mydei with her eyes– brown, warm, beautiful. “We have to get you off Lithium.” Mydei doesn’t say anything, but the question is clear on his face, found in the furrow of his brow. “You were talking and then spaced out for thirty seconds.”

Mydei makes a face, scrunches up his nose as if he smelled spoiled food. He does not want to get off Lithium, does not even want to think about it. To this, Mrs. Sofia also makes a face, though a subtler one; a curt ‘oh come on ’ look. She taps her pen against the notebook, and the sound of it makes Mydei want to tear it out of her hands and throw it out the window. Maybe take out the lightbulb while at it too. “Lithium toxicity is life-threatening. It can lead to seizures, and it’s been known to cause end-stage renal disease. Mydei, I promise you there’s better treatments for bipolar. It’s a short-term medication. It was prescribed to you as an emergency .”

Mydei pouts at that and crosses his arms over the pillow like a hug. He presses deeper into the couch, as though he might disappear inside it– as though this was a consequence he could run from. “I don’t want to talk about that right now. I have an appointment with my psychiatrist in a few weeks.”

Mrs. Sofia nods, slowly, and Mydei can tell she’s not fully convinced. She shifts her crossed legs around, now crossing right over left. “Before you spaced out, you were telling me about this man you met at work.”

“Oh. Yes, Phainon. So, uh, how do I say this… I’ve been meaning to tell you, but honestly I– forgot? But, um, we went to the gym together and he put his fingers in my mouth.”

Mrs. Sofia can’t even pretend to not be surprised, that’s how off-guard it takes her. Her eyebrows twitch upward, mouth falling open a little bit before she schools her expression back to the familiar sternness. She nods. “How did that happen? Please elaborate.”

Mydei takes a deep breath and averts his gaze, because this is all just really embarrassing. “So after we worked out, we were in the lockers and he noticed my tongue piercing. And then he asked if he could touch it, and I said yes, and so he did.  By putting his fingers in my mouth and kind of um, touching around. And he held my jaw too. And it felt– it was, you know, it was…” Mydei wants to die. “You know.”

“Sexually charged? Intimate?”

He covers his face with his hands. This is not what they usually talk about. He’s been seeing her for the past five years, and at first it was to heal the dad-murdering-your-mom trauma, but that kind of got put on hold for a while when Adrianos happened. So they’ve been going in circles about that particular thing for the past three years, and they’ve slowly started to go in circles about the mom thing too. They don’t talk about his sex life because there is none. Mydei is completely and utterly desexed. He doesn’t even masturbate– he gets the urge to, of course he does, but he doesn’t do it. He doesn’t, because it makes him feel guilty and dirty and he can’t orgasm anyways because of his meds. Suffice to say Mydeimos has considered himself somebody that has fully moved on to a sex-free life which, apparently, is not true.

And that’s bad, it’s bad that it’s not true. It’s bad that the fires of his libido are being fanned, because his libido disgusts him. The very thought of it makes him want to hurl. He thinks of Phainon caressing up and down his arms and kissing him on the lips, chaste as a knight kissing his lady, and saying ”Mydeimos, you are so beautiful, you’re perfect, I love you so much.” and he gets so squirmy and toasty and he wants to giggle into his pillow and kick his legs up. His fantasies rarely move past kissing and cuddling and tracing the sun tattoo on Phainon’s neck. Sometimes, though, he imagines grabbing Phainon’s hand by the wrist, running his thumb over the scar there, and leading him to shove his fingers down his throat as far as they’ll go. Swallowing around him, eyes fluttering closed like butterfly wings. He does not have a gag reflex, and Phainon would gasp at that, and he’d go pink all over to the tips of his ears. He would moan and make sure Phainon feels every vibration, and then he’d look up at him with pretty golden eyes, all innocent and doe-like with their thick eyelashes, and he would have these alluring tears in his eyes to make him look all the more titillating. Mydei would lick Phainon’s fingers, swirling his tongue around them and pressing his piercing deep on the underside of his fingertip. In this particular fantasy, they both cum untouched and then they get married, live happily ever after and never argue and neither one of them commits domestic homicide.

This, all of this, all of the soft feelings in his chest squeezing his heart, the way he imagines the smell of Phainon’s musk, his lovely lips on his, fingers intertwined, makes him suicidal. It makes him have panic attacks that feel like his heart is going to stop. It makes him feel as if he’s crawled ten miles through shit and mud and vomit, it sends him to the shower where he scrubs his body until it turns pink and inflamed.

“Mydei.” his therapist brings his attention back to her, and he groans a bit– almost whines. He shifts on the couch uncomfortably. “Would you say that the interaction was sexually charged?”

“Uh… yeah, I guess. Something like that.”

She writes down something quick. “Right. And how did that make you feel, in the moment?”

“I– uhm. Oh, I…” he laughs nervously and shifts even more, starts pulling on the pillow’s tassels. “I don’t know, I mean, you know…”

She just cocks an eyebrow. Cruel.

“In the moment, it felt… nice, I guess? I liked it, I think, it felt…” he gestures broadly with his hands, at nothing in particular.

“Were you aroused?”

Mydei chokes on his spit and sputters. “Y-yeah? I guess.”

Mrs. Sofia scribbles something in her notebook, and then she’s back to him. “And you allowed it to happen?”

“Hm?”

“You permitted it? Consented?”

Mydei grows very tense all of a sudden, and his fight or flight instinct kicks in. He wonders if he still has to pay if he runs out of his therapy session. “I said ’do whatever you want’ to be a dick, but I meant yes.”

“Alright,” she fixes her glasses, “And how did you feel afterwards?”

“I felt normal, and then at night when I was in bed, I suddenly started feeling all weird. Um. Dirty, I guess? Like I did something wrong, or… then I thought, yeah, I let him do it, but what if I didn’t?”

Mydei sees Mrs. Sofia emote for the second time in five years. A small look of surprise, and then it’s back to the poker face. “Pardon?”

“Like, I said yes, but what if I didn’t?”

“You verbally said ’yes’ –”

“I said ’do whatever you want’ .”

“Basically ’yes’ . Were you being coerced? Did you feel unsafe, as though something bad might happen if you turned him down?”

“No, I don’t think Phainon’s like that. If I said no, he’d just laugh it off and move on.”

“Right, so there was no pressuring involved?”

“No.”

“So then…?”

“It’s like… I wanted it, but what if I didn’t actually want it?”

“That’s impossible. You can’t want and not want something at the same time.”

“I– no, you don’t understand,” and now he’s getting agitated, and that feeling is creeping up the back of his head, and he kind of wants to cry. “What if I didn’t actually want it, but I still said yes, and then it still happened?”

“I suppose that would be sexual harrassment.” “Yeah."

“But you did want it.”

“But what if–”

Mrs. Sofia puts down her pen, loudly . “Mydeimos, you are in control of your actions and of your thoughts. You are an adult and you are capable of consent. It’s yours to give. Even if it has been violated, or you’ve been pressured, you still own it. You cannot give it out by accident. You are allowed to want something.”

“...Okay.”

She clicks her tongue, tilts her head, and she’s got that look in her eyes that Mydei recognizes– the one that forewarns of something painful. “It’s easier for you to accept your consent being violated than it being respected. It’s more familiar. You are in uncharted waters. You feel it’s more natural for you to have something taken away by force than to give it out freely– and the fact that you have completely avoided any sort of sexual behaviour doesn’t help. You want it –and Mydei cringes at that– , so why don’t you let yourself want it?”

“I’m–” and his voice is very, very small. “I’m scared, I guess.”

“What are you scared of?”

“Of getting hurt again.”

“Are you going to live your entire life in this fear? Do you want to? Does it feel good? Are you happy? ”

Mydei sighs, shaky, long-suffering. “No. But I don’t know how to fix it.”

“You have to try. The issue is that you don’t try . To be completely honest, we’ve been doing this for a very, very long time, and I see very little progress–”

“I am better. I am doing better.”

“You are on heavy medication . The goal is to get you off of them. Would you still be doing better if you weren’t taking pills?”

Mydei looks at her, eyes wide and wet, mouth aghast. She’s never been like this before. ”Are you mad at me?”

Mrs. Sofia takes off her glasses and puts them aside. She rubs the little indents they’ve left on her nose. “I am not mad, Mydeimos. I am concerned.” Her face turns softer, her voice gentler. “Mydei, I’m going to say something very upsetting. You can’t control it. No matter how much you try, you can’t control other people’s actions. There are nuns who live in complete seclusion among other women, and they still get assaulted. The responsibility of not being assaulted doesn’t fall on you .”

“Are you saying it will happen again?”

“No, I’m not saying that. I cannot see into the future. It might. It might also not. This is not a reason to stop living. You have to live with the uncertain–”

“You don’t get it.”

“For the sake of professional boundaries, you’ll have to trust me when I say I do. ”

Mydei is silent for a very long time. He looks at her. She looks at him. And then, he speaks again, hushed, whispered. ”I don’t know how to fix it.”

“I’ll help you. You have to try.”

“I can’t exactly– just go and… fuck him, you know, we’re not there yet. I don’t know if he likes me like that.”

“That’s not what I’m telling you to try–”

“Do I just go and fuck a random person?”

“ No. Listen to me. It’s the feelings you have to try and live with. Those feelings of desire, lust, sexual attraction. Live with them. Sit with them. They’re normal, they’re not dirty . You’re not dirty for having those thoughts, Mydei. Do you understand me? You are not dirty. You are not a dirty person.”

That’s when Mydei breaks into tears, ugly and blubbering. Mydei learned how to cry very, very quietly when he was little, and he still does it nowadays. Small little sobs and clenched teeth and hot angry tears scorching down his face and leaving tracks. Not a sound made. “I’m just– I’m so– I’m so sad, and I’m so mad and–”

Mrs. Sofia hands him the box of tissues, and Mydei takes them. “I know. That’s okay. It’s okay that you feel like that. You didn’t deserve that, and it’s not your fault. You trusted him– that’s okay. You weren’t stupid for trusting him. You can trust people again.”

“I don’t know, like– if– if I do like, how do I even do it? Sex…”

Mrs. Sofia takes a deep breath and thinks very carefully. “You do it with a person you trust very much, that’s the hard part. You have to let yourself trust them. And then you take it very slowly. It doesn’t have to be all at once. You take it at your pace, little by little, as much as you’re comfortable with. You don’t have to go all the way in one sitting.”

“What if they don’t like that?”

“Then it’s not the right person.”

“Okay.” Mydei blows his nose. “Do I– I mean, like, masturbate?”

Mrs. Sofia hums, then nods. “That could be a good start. Doing it by yourself– it’s safe.”

“Yeah, okay. What do I do with Phainon?”

“Don’t do anything in particular– be yourself. Do whatever you want. Flirt if you want to, or ask him out on a date. Be his friend. Let it happen naturally. And don’t run away.”

“Oka–”

“And get off Lithium.”

“Okay.”

They spend the rest twenty minutes running in circles about the same subject they have for the past five years– the whole murdered mom thing. While Mrs. Sofia suggested they continued on the sexual assault topic, Mydei told her that he’s not comfortable talking about it anymore; that made her really proud, he could see it in her eyes. Setting boundaries or whatever.

It’s the same song and dance, and he’s getting tired of it, and he can tell she’s getting tired of it too. All options thoroughly and utterly exhausted. He refutes all of her claims, her techniques, her years of experience and her fucking PHD as well. He wants to get better, asks how, and the answer– try. Trust people more. Unlearn shame. Unlearn stubborn independence. Get out there. Love. Let loose. Relax. Sit with the uncertainty, get used to it, become immune to it. It might happen again. It might not. You might do it. Mydeimos you’re covered in blood, Mydeimos stop you’re hurting me, Mydeimos you’re fifteen years old and you are knee deep in a sea of blood and there are creatures in the water Mydeimos I am so afraid. Mydeimos why did you run Mydeimos why didn’t you run faster. Mydeimos it’s so cold here and I am so very alone. Mydeimos I miss you. Mydeimos I love you. Mydeimos I hate you YOU ARE HURTING ME. Why are you hurting me? Mydeimos I am so small and I just want to love you.

You are just like him.

“I feel like,” Mrs. Sofia cuts in. She has noticed the glaze in his eyes. “We should talk about the cat.”

“No.”

When the session is over, Mrs. Sofia speaks up again. His hand freezes on the doorknob. He does not turn around. “Trauma is a liar, Mydei,” she says, and he can hear the click of her heels as she moves around the room. “It’s a really good, beautiful liar. It will tell you that if you just do the right thing, if you protect yourself enough, if you learn your lesson and be more careful, then you will be safe. Secure. You won’t have to worry about it again, it won’t happen. That’s the lie, and here’s the kicker: the goalpost keeps moving. You’ll have a few good days and then you’ll wake up all sweaty and scared and think I am not safe . And then you will be even more careful, take even more precautions, isolate yourself more. No amount of preparation will be good enough, no amount of preparation will change what’s already happened. Next thing you know, you haven’t seen the sun in weeks. Don’t you want to see the Sun?”

Mydei mulls it over in his head, worrying at his bottom lip. ‘The Sun…’

Tribbie’s team building is in a few hours and he has to get ready, because–

He will see Phainon today. He really wants to see Phainon today.
