It’s 7 PM and Phainon is in front of his bathroom mirror, looking back at himself obsessively and trying his hardest to make himself into something resembling a human being.

It’s been a little over a month since his very public mental breakdown and Cipher’s emergency intervention. This is how things are going for him:

He keeps up with cleaning the apartment and the cockroach issue is all but eradicated. Taking care of Bartholos actually helps, and he’s starting to wonder if this is a more permanent arrangement. Every time he seriously contemplates suicide (and we’ll get there), he steps back and thinks of the cat– how he’d be lonely and confused and hungry and thirsty. The responsibility keeps him alive. He has a new crush, and things are going well. Castorice went deep-diving in Mydei’s social media presence and found that one of his friends’ boyfriend tagged him in a picture from Pride, so he definitely likes men. Mydei is patient and indulges in his bullshit, he fans the flames of his ego and his competitive side. He likes bullying Mydei, knows that Mydei can take it, and the guy throws it right back at him. It’s perfect.

That’s all nice and good, and by all means there is a significant improvement in his day-to-day life, so then why…

Why does he still want to kill himself so damn bad? Time bleeds down into a cursed chalice and mixes together into thick muck– he drinks it and wakes up to realize that it’s midnight and he’s spent the entire day trying to not commit suicide. He thinks of it often. Thinks of it most of the time. Mydeimos could be talking to him about ancient Kremnoan military strategies and Phainon would be staring at the sky, thinking about how nice it would be to deepthroat the barrel of a shotgun. He wakes up and makes his coffee and thinks about dumping the entire pot of boiling water on his head, hoping that the shock would make his brain seize and stop working. He looks up the success rate of drinking bleach, looks up the consequences of surviving a fall from the top of his building.

He’s not planning, not really, not anymore and not like he did back then. He’s not really planning on doing anything, because of Bartholos, but he is thinking about it. Kind of like a baby sucking his thumb, the thought of suicide is the only constant comfort in his life.

Cipher doesn’t speak to him anymore. Doesn’t speak to anyone, really, not even in their groupchat. When she comes to work, she is tired. Pale. Smaller, as if she’s lost weight, as if the clothes are swallowing her up. She is twitchy and nervous and shaky all over, and when Phainon tries to strike up a conversation, she slips out like a weasel. He’s picked up a very good thing and threw it against the wall. He wanted someone to keep him together and, in turn, he has shattered them.

Shattered. This is how he feels sometimes, like fine china knocked down by a mean child. Barely holding himself together with glue, crumbling like old wax. The hallucinations come and go. They have not gotten worse, but they have gotten clearer, more cruel, have taken a more terrible shape. He wakes up sweaty and cold and paralyzed, unable to move anything but his eyes, and there is Cyrene pressed up against his chest, looking at him with big frightened eyes. She is crying in those moments, sobbing tears that make her pretty face all splotchy, and she asks him over and over– why . And he doesn’t know what to tell her, can’t speak anyways, and he just wants to gather her in his arms and apologize.

There is too much grief in his body and he doesn’t know where to put it. He cries often, most days, but it is not enough. It feels like every tear piles on and grows into an obelisk, and instead of his heart feeling sated, it feels heavier.

The shape of his suicide ideation has started to shift from setting himself on fire to praying he gets cancer and dies. Crossing the street without checking and hoping that a car comes and obliterates him. He wants the burden of death off his shoulders and onto someone else’s, and he wants something big and public so that people would know to check on Bartholos.

There are good days, better days. There are also worse days. They hang in a fragile balance.

It is better. It also doesn’t make a difference.

Phainon washes his face, hoping to reduce any redness and puffiness from his crying fit. Tribbie’s little team building bullshit is in an hour and he has to catch the subway because he will not fucking get in a car , and it’s just– he wants to sleep. If this was happening literally last month, Phainon would’ve excused himself and apologized profusely and say that ’something came up’ . But now, he’s…

He’s trying. He’s trying really, really hard. He’s trying because he doesn’t want to embarrass himself anymore, and he doesn’t want to let people down anymore, and he wants to be good . So, he tries and forces himself out of the house. Who knows, maybe something good will happen, like maybe Cipher will throw her hand over his shoulder and start with her banter, or maybe Mydei will push him against the wall and suck him off. Something like that.

Phainon runs his hand through his hair and fixes every little stray strand. He fixes his shirt and smoothes his jeans, and he looks– presentable, handsome, cute in his previously Cyrene Approved™ outfit. He looks like he can be someone . Enough of Phainon, he can be Phainooon~ Ahh, Phainon, you’re so silly!! You’re so funny and goofy, Phainonnn, oh you make me laugh so hard!!

So, despite it all, despite the burden, he opens the door and goes outside. Catches the bus and then the subway. The mere thought of getting behind a wheel sends him in such bouts of panic that he’s afraid his heart will give up– and nonetheless, his car is sitting wrecked and fractured in some junkyard. He does not have any money to repair it, and even if he did, he does not want to nurture his sister’s grave.

His sister’s grave. Phainon leans harder on the filthy subway pole. He should visit it sometimes, anytime . Probably should clean it up and bring some flowers, or just stand there and talk to her, or–

He’s never visited it since burying her. Perhaps, he thinks, if he ignores the physical proof of her death, she would unrot and raise anew like Mnestia from the golden cocoon. Reborn, clean, radiant, alive again. His mouth goes dry– she, she’s just bones now. At this point, almost nine months later, she is just bones. Her beautiful face, so kind, so lustrous– he hasn’t, he’s never thought about it like that before. The image of maggot eating her eyes, writhing in and out of her mouth, is striking. Bugs crawling over her body like soldiers laying waste to a city, eating from a feast not meant for them. His sister with her easy smile and her pretty voice. All the memories are being pulled out like golden thread from the middle of the earth; her hunched over the sink, bleaching her roots, her singing a song for her third grade talent show, her collecting each and every affordable piece of Miku merch.

Holy shit, he’s gonna have a panic attack in the subway. There’s a kid picking his nose next to him. He’s going to have a mental breakdown in front of a snotty kid– that should be grounds for euthanasia.

Deep breaths, just like Cipher taught you, come on. Hard, long inhales and shaky exhales. Get it out. Get it together . Stop whinging. Phainon presses his palms to his eyes, hoping to stop the tears. It’s too hot in here, too crowded, too many people pressed up against him. All of a sudden he feels like he is suffocating, like air is a luxury and he is a pauper. Look, here they come– the painful sobs ripped from his chest with a violence that is sure to shock the world. He tries to suppress them, and all that come out are these small, pitiful whines that leave his torso shaking. Oh my God, people are staring, people are staring because he’s the guy whining and gasping on the subway. The car pulls into the station and comes to an abrupt stop, sending the entire train reeling. Somebody bumps into him and almost knocks him over, and Phainon truly, genuinely, wants to start biting people.

In a daze, he pushes his way past the sea of people, manhandling his way out of the car– he’s pretty sure he knocks a lady’s purse down, if her shouting is to be believed. He takes the stairs upwards two at a time, unthinking, and only begins to breathe when the cool September air hits him. Finally, some room. The people passing by him are looking, and he’s really, really trying to keep it together.

It’s just– does it hurt? Is she in pain? She’s dead, so she’s not much of… anything , but it must– it would hurt, if she was alive, and her flesh was stripped from her by bugs and worms and– he’s going to throw up. All that she has ever been; bones.

A hand lands on his back, small and cold.

He clenches his fist in anticipation for a fight, because this is becoming a fight– until he hears a voice calling for him, sweet and familiar. “Phainon?”

Oh.

Hiii, Castorice~ Oh my God, Castorice, hello~~ Castorice, you look so pretty, haha! Castorice, do you want to hear a joke? Castorice, let’s take a selfie!!

Yeah, like that. Be like that. Get it the fuck together. Phainon runs a shaky hand through his hair, and turns around to face her with his most dazzling smile.

“Casto– Polyxia!! ” Phainon squeaks like a kid on Christmas, and he reaches down to grab Polyxia’s hand. “Baby, how are you? I’m so glad you could make it!”

Polyxia weakly chuckles, her eyes flitting to the screen in front of her. ”Hi, Phainon~ I felt well enough and decided to tag along and bother Castorice.” The look in her eyes is a little mischievous, a little tired. She is paler than usual, big dark circles marring her pretty face, and she looks like she lost some weight in the past month. Still, she remains unbeaten. ”Are you okay? You look like shit, did you see a ghost or something? Haha. Castorice isn’t that scary, is she?”

“Polyxia… Come on…” Castorice flusters and blushes to the tips of her ears, and she does that thing she likes to do with her hands– rubbing them together, almost shyly.

“Don’t bully poor Cas!” The smile is starting to hurt Phainon’s face. He hopes it’s convincing. “You girls walked all this way?”

”Yes. Fresh air is good for me, and God knows Castorice needs to exercise more.” Polyxia blinks at her monitor some more, ”And I don’t even wanna bother with public transport. Are you gonna accompany us the rest of the way like a gentleman or what?”

Phainon laughs nervously, and tries to puff up his chest and peacock as much as possible. “Well, ladies– yes, of course! Your gallant knight has arrived~” and he finishes it with flair and a bow, extending his arm to show the way to Castorice and Polyxia. They seem pleased enough, convinced enough, and Phainon does not mention how Polyxia’s facial muscles are less responsive, or how her breathing comes out in hard, rattled rasps. There’s no need to think about anything now.

Bliss might be just at his fingertips.

He chats with the girls as they walk, pushing through the suicidal discomfort, trying to find something to cling on. Polyxia is recapping the latest Love Island drama, and he, well– he obliges, half-dazed and half-dead, reaching to kindle the fire of personhood from him.

Suicidality has stolen so much time from him, he’s forgotten how to live.

They stop in front of the bar, and Phainon is relieved to see that there is, indeed, a ramp. They are the first to arrive, however, and everybody feels a bit awkward going in without Tribios– because they’re just three people nearing their thirties, so of course they need their mommy to talk to the scawy waiters.

A car pulls up and everybody holds their breath, hoping that it’s their saviour.

Mydei steps out instead, looking handsome in his combat boots and this little black tanktop that’s juuuuust short enough for Phainon to see a little bit of his tummy; suddenly, he feels all warm like a Victorian man seeing an ankle for the first time. Never mind that he’s put nearly his entire fist down his throat, they don’t talk about that.

Alright, switching gears. Decreasing “killing yourself” priority, increasing “bothering the fuck out of Mydei” priority.

Mydei, ever polite, smiles and acknowledges the girls first. He greets Castorice and kisses her on both cheeks– back up, they still do that in Kremnos? He then turns to Polyxia and squeezes her hand. His smile is beautiful, easy. “Hi, nice to meet you– you must be Castorice’s sister, right? I’m Mydeimos.”

Polyxia flushes a little, barely there. ”Yes, hi, nice to meet you too. Mydei, huh? Castorice told me a looooot of things about you~”

“All good, I hope?” and he gives Castorice a look , a playful warning. He kisses Polyxia’s cheeks. Where the fuck is Phainon’s kiss?

”I’d say they’re good. You’re not local, are you? Where are you from?”

“Castrum Kremnos.”

”Ooo, interesting. Castorice and I moved around a bit as kids. Born in Styxia, raised in Aidonia.”

Phainon swears he sees Mydei’s eyes sparkle. “Chilly. I would love to visit Aidonia and see the monuments to Thanatos, and the Temple of the Maiden of War.”

Polyxia huffs a bit. ”Really, they’re not that impressive. Just a bunch of old rocks.”

“Still, the history is–”

Alright, that’s enough. Mydei is– I mean, he looks cute, done up, a little punk rock-y and very pretty. He has his hair in a low bun and his stupid braid is swinging left and right. He’s even wearing a pair of sunglasses on the top of his head. He looks good, but Phainon isn’t gonna allow him to show off in front of the ladies like that.

Blond men are the enemy. He also has a thing for them, but that’s besides the point. Phainon himself also technically counts as a blond –because he is literally a natural blond– but he bleaches and dyes his hair white, so that’s also besides the point.

“Why are you wearing sunglasses at night like an asshole?”

Mydei’s mood shifts immediately and he shoots Phainon with that frowny face of his. Jackpot. Mydei schools his expression right away, because he’s very committed to being stoic. “It’s part of my outfit.”

“It makes you look like a bouncer.”

“Are you saying that because I have more muscle mass than you? In that case, I agree.”

Alright, alright, nice shot– but Phainon has some aces up his sleeve, and those aces are called ‘innocent bystanders’.

“Castorice, Polyxia!” he claps his hands and steps closer to Mydei, who already crossed his arms in anticipation. “I have a score to settle with our dear Kremnoan. Say, since you’re an unbiased party, could you tell me… Which one of us is taller?”

Mydei scoffs, and Castorice groans. “Not this again, Phainon!” she begs, but it is futile. “This is all we ever do on our breaks now. I’ve been keeping so many scores and breaking so many draws that I lost count…”

Castorice is out, but Polyxia is cut from a different cloth. Phainon cocks an eyebrow at her, and it’s worth a million words.

”Alright,” she says, ”I’ll do it.”

Phainon moves to stand next to Mydei. Mydei’s bare shoulder presses against his as the man leans in closer too, and even their shoes are touching– sneakers to boots. Phainon finds that incredibly erotic, and he stops himself from shuddering. Mydei is so warm, like a furnace, and he can't help but steal a look at him– his eyes follow the curve of his arched nose as it dips into his cupid’s bow. He sighs without realizing, a bit too wistfully to be casual.

”Hmm…” Polyxia speaks up after a few beats, ”I would say you’re about the same height but… You might be a teeny bit taller, Phainon? Less than a centimeter.”

“HA!” Phainon chortles and shoves Mydei, to which the other man just clicks his teeth and groans.

“That proves nothing. Polyxia, whose arms are bigger?” Mydei extends his arms and flexes. Alright, Phainon can play this game too. He mirrors the action.

”Mydei’s.”

“Alright, but whose back is bigger then?”

Another change of pose.

”I think yours, Phainon.”

“Polyxia, whose shoulders are broader?” comes Mydei’s challenge.

Another pose. They’re starting to look like Jojo characters.

”Still Phainon’s.”

Phainon gets a wicked, wicked idea. “Polyxia, Polyxia~” he calls out, all innocent. “Whose waist is smaller?”

Mydei cocks his head at that like a confused puppy. “Why would we even measure that?”

“Don’t be a party pooper, Mydei, come on!” Phainon presses on, and Mydei’s only reply is a ‘hmph’ . Wow, so stoic. He bunches his shirt at the back, and his competitor follows suit.

Castorice laughs at that, and Polyxia looks amused too. The cool autumn evening breeze blows gently amongst them, ruffling Phainon’s hair and the hems of Castorice’s skirt. She puts a hand on her sister’s shoulder, impossibly fond.

”I have to give this one to Mydei. Very tiny waist, all things considered.”

Mydei blushes at that, barely perceptible, his bronze skin coloring peachy– mission accomplished . He looks sunkissed, fatally pretty, and so utterly lovely that it hurts to look at him. A little timid, but more so stubborn. Phainon wants to see him even redder, pink to the tips of his ears. He sneaks behind him like a sly coyote, and his hands easily find purchase on his waist. It’s tapered like sin, hard and muscular under his palms, yet when he starts to knead it he finds the flesh soft and yielding willingly. The tips of his pinkies graze along the exposed part of his stomach, the ghost of a touch, and it is enough to make Phainon bite his thumbs. His thumbs don’t quite reach each other, but they’re not that far apart either. A nice, curvaceous slope– the ratio of his body is insane .

Mydei gasps and shoves him off, yet he does not look nearly as pissed off as he ought to. He looks more… flustered? Embarrassed, but in a cute way. He huffs and looks away all balky.

Castorice and Polyxia are quite surprised by the show.

”Are they always like this?”

“Pretty much.”

”Haha. Castorice. Oaf4Oaf.”

Reinvigorated with fresh ambition, Mydei turns to Polyxia. He seems determined like a lion about to strike. “What’s the score?”

”Three for Phainon, two for you.”

“Alright, let’s settle it then. Whoever wins this one wins everything. It’s worth seventy-nine points. Polyxia, whose chest is bigger?”

That’s a low blow. Phainon refuses to engage in unsportsmanlike conduct– and by the way, no, grabbing your enemy’s waist does not count as unsportsmanlike conduct, thank you very much.

“That’s not fair, Mydei, you know you’ll win that.”

“Oh? Are you afraid of losing?”

“That’s not it.”

“You are conceding defeat, then.”

”No.”

“Then by all means, Polyxia, plea–”

Two taloned hands grab both of their shoulders. It’s as if the air fills with electricity– Phainon can see Castorice and Polyxia visibly relax as they are saved from this endless hellish loop he’s roped them in. He fixes his gaze on the hand grasping him, and is relieved to see a perfect red manicure. Whew. If it was Aglaea instead, this would’ve been a lot scarier.

“Snowy, De, what are you boys doing? Oh, you’re so silly~”

Tribios pulls them close to her in a suffocating embrace.

She’s, well– she’s an adult with an actual job and a loving husband. Tribbie is the most senior employee of all of them, and she’s repeatedly been offered higher positions, such as Head of Customer Support and even higher-up management roles. She always turned them down, however, saying that she and her husband make enough money to live very comfortably, and she’d rather focus on her studies and her family and her side-gig than be stressed out because of work.

Her side-gig , of course, is tinkering and making things. She makes little automated toys for children and sells them on Etsy, and her biggest hobby is taking things apart and putting them back together. She’s currently studying Engineering at a prestigious college in Okhema, and somehow she still finds the time to work full-time and take care of her seven year old daughters– Trianne and Trinnon. Two sweet little angels, those twins; Trianne is cheeky and mischievous, Trinnon is timid and polite. It’s always a delight when she brings them to the office with her.

She pulls back and lets them go, before turning to greet the others. “Cassie, Pollie, look at you! I’m so glad you could make it!” She gives each of them a hug. Tribios really likes the color red, and you can tell; she has this beautiful natural ginger hair, almost fiery in hue, and she always accessories with red lipstick, red nails, red jewels. Even the rims of her glasses are red. She’s just– a very nice older woman, a grounding presence, with all the goodness and sweetness of a wine mom in her mid to late forties.

“Why are you kids sitting outside, hm?”

“Oh, well, we–” Castorice starts to explain, shifting her weight awkwardly. “We thought we should wait for you, so yeah– we were just hanging out.”

Tribios smiles, doting, and chuckles a little. She links her arms with Phainon’s and Mydei’s and starts to pull them inside the bar. “Well then, come on! It’s already 8 PM, we don’t wanna keep the establishment waiting~ I’m sure the others will arrive soon!”

And just like prophesied, the others do start to pour in soon after. First is Hysilens, distinctly not with Cerydra. When Tribbie asks her about it, she just gives a bullshit excuse– ”Cery is not feeling well.” Phainon knows that it’s actually because those two are fighting again.

When Aglaea arrives not soon after, it is in a twirl of silk and gold. She’s wearing these gorgeous earrings shaped to look like big ancient coins depicting the last Imperator of Okhema, and her heels (Louboutin red-bottoms, of course) are so high she towers over everyone in the bar. Aglaea commands every room she enters, and for a good reason– her presence is unmatched in elegance and sophistication. The old money kind, not the luxury that yells, but rather whispers. She’s the oldest daughter of this old, famous fashion house, yet she works a mundane job because she wants to make her own wealth instead– which is like, typical out-of-touch rich people bullshit, but Aglaea pulls it off. She once told him, ”I want to make enough money to buy FLAMECHASE Inc.” and Phainon fully believes she’s capable of it. Glued to her heel is a Labrador retriever, golden like everything else about Aglaea, named Garmentmaker– her seeing eye dog that she takes to crowded, or unfamiliar, places. She looks incredibly cute in her ‘DO NOT PET, SERVICE DOG’ vest, and she lays down so politely with her head on Aglaea’s feet when her owner sits down at the table.

Hyacine arrives about an hour later, but that’s to be expected– she spends about three hours just getting ready, and her outfits all weigh over ten pounds. Tribbie exclaims happily when she makes it through the door, dressed in ribbons and ruffles and petticoats. “Cinny, you look like a little doll!” Tribios actually has to scoot over to make room for her and her skirts.

“Hyacinthia,” Aglaea delicately brings her glass of red wine to her mouth. Phainon does not like her tone. “I thought you’d be coming with Anaxagoras.”

“Aglaea,” Hyacine says, good-natured, mimicking Aglaea’s cadence. “Now why would you think that?”

“You two are nigh inseparable.”

“We work shoulder to shoulder for nine hours a day.” Hyacine shrugs and orders a pint of bitter pale ale. “I did ask them if they’d come, and they just said… What was it… Oh! They said,” she clears her throat, and Phainon knows she’s about to go into her pitch-perfect Anaxa impression. ”I would rather drink molten glass than spend time in the same room as that woman, unless it was professionally necessary, which this is NOT.”

“I think they mean you, Agy~”

When Aglaea sets down her glass, the rim is stained with her perfect nude lipstick. She scoffs and snickers. “Yes, that does sound like them.”

Nobody else arrives so, you know, this is it, and this is enough . They all order their drinks, but Phainon makes a good decision today and doesn’t get anything alcoholic; he really is trying to be better. What he orders instead is an obscene amount of cola, because Tribbie is footing the bill and nothing tastes better than free coke. Multiple conversations swirl around him, and Phainon is just happy to listen to them.

”How are the girls, Tribios?” Aglaea asks, turning to face her old trainer

”Oh, they’re just going into second grade, so we’re all very excited for that. Trianne is a little imp, and we’re trying to get Trinnon to open up more, make more friends at school. We’re planning a trip to Ladon for the holidays. How’s your mother?”

“She’s getting up there in age. Oh– Hysilens, you have to try the cocktails at this place. They’re great, you’d love them.”

“Really? Recommend me something good, then.”

“So, Mydei,” Hyacine wipes her face after downing her pint, “You have five roommates? All guys?”

“That’s right.”

“Woah. Must be like a sausage party in there.”

“Mm… Less of a sausage party, more like… the werkroom of Rupaul’s Drag Race?” Hyacine and Castorice holler at that, and even Polyxia chortles. It gets a chuckle out of Phainon too.

Eventually, he finds himself in a conversation with Polyxia and Castorice. Polyxia is telling him about her art, and Castorice is shuffling through pictures of both traditional and digital paintings on her phone. They’re beautiful, some depicting scenes from her favorite TV shows or Castorice’s fanfics, but most drawings are of landscapes, still life, and portraits. They’re all very faithful to life, colorful and vibrant. ”Yeah, so, there’s this technology that tracks your eyes and you can draw digitally like that.” Castorice shows him a portrait of herself holding a bouquet of Antila flowers, smiling demurely with her hair covered by a purple tichel, patterned with butterflies. ”That one won first place at a competition for artists with disabilities.”

It’s a beautiful digital painting, capturing Castorice’s delicate features perfectly, her quiet and comfortable beauty. It’s drawn with so much love that Phainon can physically see it in each brushstroke. Castorice hands him her phone so he can have a better look and he zooms into her eyes. “Hey, Polyxia, can I buy this one off of you? I wanna print it and laminate it and frame it. Gonna put it on my bathroom door so Drawingrice can watch me poop.”

Castorice shoves him playfully, and the corners of Polyxia’s face twitch upward. ”You know what, for that reason? I’ll give it to you for free. Though if you want to commission me to draw you and Mydei making out, I’m down.”

Phainon looks over both of his shoulders in mock suspicion, as if making sure Mydei isn’t listening; he’s not, he’s busy talking with Tribios and Hysilens. He leans in close to Polyxia and whispers conspiratorially, “Gee, can you? I’ll give you half my salary and a pack of cigarettes for it.”

”Deal.”

About two hours later, the bar’s front door opens with a loud bang, and Phainon is the only one startled enough to check. He turns around towards the commotion and his heart immediately falls out of his ass. Standing there, seemingly arguing with a waiter and a little wobbly on her feet– Cifera.

And she looks like shit, even worse than lately. Is she drunk?

“Um…” he turns back towards Tribios and tries to get her attention by tapping her hand. She looks at him, he gestures at Cipher, and her eyes light up . “Agy, Ciphy is here! Cifera, over here!” She gets up and waves her hand. Tribbie has always been a bit… oblivious. The waiter seems to understand that she’s with the group , and half-heartedly starts to lead her over to their table. She sits next to Hyacine, towards the end of the table.

The mood shifts. Phainon thought she walked a little weird, unsteady, but now that she’s closer he can tell– Cipher is not drunk, she’s high. And not on weed either, but on some serious shit; she keeps grinding her jaw, and her pupils are so blown out her irises look like little blue-green rings around a black void.

The conversations immediately die down, and Phainon can hear Aglaea sigh under her breath. Cipher looks between them, between all of them, her face twisted in manic cheer. Smiling big, all teeth showing, the muscles of her face pulled taut. “Whaaaat’s uuuuup? What’s going on~” Her voice is raspy, each lilt uncontrollable. Suddenly, she stops in her tracks, as if seeing them for the first time. “Why’s everyone so down all of a sudden?” She smiles and laughs and hiccups, throws an arm around Hyacine.

“Um, Cipher…” Hyacine tries to squirm out of her hold. “Aww, come on, Cinny, what’s with that face? What’s with everyone’s faces? Did I… get it wrong?” and she’s starting to put on her act . “Was I not invited, Tribbie?”

Tribbie laughs awkwardly. “No, Ciphy, of course you were, it’s just– are you feeling okay?”

“Oh, Tribbie, I am on top of the world. Never been fuckin’ better.” She gestures over a waiter and orders a vodka cranberry. “C’mon, why the long faces? I’m here, let’s partaaaaay!! Cassie, you look so pretty~”

To say it’s awkward would be an understanding– it’s downright unbearable . He feels like he’s choking, and he can’t stop looking at her and she very pointedly does not look back . When the waiter comes with her drink, she downs it before he can leave and then immediately orders another. He’s so, so embarrassed right now; they’ve hardly exchanged any words since his last episode and she’s been dodging him as if he were a bullet, and now this…

Cipher is self-destructive, he knows that, but Cipher is also proud . She would never expose herself like this in public, not in front of everyone else, not in front of Aglaea . Her misery is a lot more well-hidden than his, so well-hidden that Phainon himself doesn’t know what this is all about. Something is very, very wrong with her. Her hands shake uncontrollably, and she can’t stand still. She keeps picking at the same scab on her hand.

Phainon is stuck between his shame and his concern, and he doesn’t know which one to act on first. One side wants to apologize, the other wants to ask her if she’s okay. Selfish and selfless– selfish usually wins.

“So like, what’s up?” she claps her hands, “What are we talking about? Families and kids and relationships and all that bullshit?”

Hyacine’s voice is very small and very concerned when she speaks. “Cifera, I don’t think–”

“What? What’s wrong, Hyacine? Did I do something wrong? Does my presence offend you? ”

“Cipher, no, of course not!” Castorice sounds almost outraged at the accusation, but Phainon knows that’s not true. That’s unlike Castorice. He knows her well enough to know that she’s very, very upset right now.

“Oh–” Cipher breaks into laughter, then mocks Castorice’s tone and voice ruthlessly, making her sound high-pitched and nasally and annoying. ”Of course not! We’re just so worried, blehhh.” and then more laughter and more giggles, as if this is the funniest thing she’s ever heard. Castorice is wrecked at this, she’s self-conscious like that. There are tears in the corners of her eyes already. “God forbid Cipher comes in all happy, right? You’d rather have some boring work party and talk about stocks or some bullshit? Look at you, you’re not even– you’re not even drinking real alcohol. Don’t you wanna get it started ?”

Something darkens in Tribios’ gaze. “That’s not appropriate for a work event, Cifera. You can’t speak to Castorice like that. Apologize to her.” At that, Cipher’s face turns childlike and innocent, another act of hers. “M-mommy…? Are you my mother, Tribios?” and in a moment, it twists back to the amused cruelty, all ravenous glee.

Looking at her, Phainon can’t help but think of those theater masks, one laughing and one crying. Her facial expressions are uninhibited, erratic, now wrathful now cheerful. Her fingers are twitching on her new glass of vodka cranberry, as if she has no control over them. Cipher looks between them with a panther’s predatory eye, and then her gaze stops to fix on Mydei.

“Oh… Ohhhhh .” she gasps as if she made some great discovery, “That’s it. That’s why . You don’t want to be embarrassed in front of the new guy.” She fully turns around and leans on her elbows, getting closer to Mydei. Mydei, on the other hand, looks neutral and unperturbed.

“That’s your shiny new toy, isn’t it? I’ve heard how you talk about him in meetings and fuckin’ work huddles– ’Ohh, De, you’re so good, you’re already one of our top employees!’ ” she says, mocking Tribbie.

”Mydeimos, you are a great addition to our team.” mocking Aglaea.

”M-M-Mydei, can I show you my favorite horse girl?” mocking Castorice, striking deep.

”Mydei, Mydei~ Come, let’s see who’s faster~” when it’s his turn to be mocked, Phainon feels oddly… betrayed, like he would’ve never expected this from her. Something about her body language when she imitates him, the tone of her voice, hits him right in the center of his heart. Phainon is not so much sad as he is angry, and growing angrier still by the minute.

“You all are trying to replace me. You think I can’t fucking tell? Isn’t he just so damn polite and suuuuch a gentleman and he’s so emotionally well-adjusted, not like Cipher the fucking mess .” Her grin turns sharp, hateful. “Well, here’s the thing, for everyone here–” she downs her drink, “I googled you, little lion, yeah, I did, when you started working here. There’s not a lot of Mydeimoses in Okhema.”

Phainon feels Mydei tense next to him. The whole table is so deathly quiet that Phainon could hear his breath hitch. Cipher rubs her eyes and smudges her mascara. “Did you guys know…” and she– she just keeps looking at him, and there’s something incredibly unkind in her eyes, more so than when she usually teases. Something like venom. Mydei starts to bounce his leg.

“Little Mydeimos Polemos here– nice one, by the way, it rhymes, props to your mom. Oh, yeah! Talking about your mom, so I googled you and found this old news article! Did you guys know that in 2009– ”

Aglaea’s hand comes down on the table so fiercely that every glass shakes. He has never, ever , seen her look so– upset? Disappointed? Concerned? Fury is written all over her beautiful face, in the furrow of her brow and the scowl of her mouth. She is red to the tip of her ears, though if it is out of embarrassment or rage, Phainon cannot tell. ”No.” is all she says. Her voice is so commanding, so absolutely imposing, that Cipher finally, finally closes her mouth. She looks like a kid caught with her fingers in the pie, eyes wide like plates and mouth agape– a telltale sign of ’oh shit’ .

“I have indulged this for far too long. You don’t get to talk like that about us, you don’t get to say that about him.” A finger points all accusatory at Cipher; for the first time ever, Phainon notices that her and Aglaea do their nails the same way. Sharp and golden. “That’s not for you to say. You don’t get to drag everyone else down because you’re upset.”

Cipher’s look of surprise slowly transforms into a… Sad, melancholy sort of triumph– as if she’s just gotten exactly what she was looking for. “I knew it, I knew you–”

”I’m taking you home.” Hyacine stands up and knocks down a glass of soda. “Please, Cipher, just– let me drive you home.”

There’s some more talking going on, but Phainon’s tuned it out. He is focused solely on Mydei, who’s looking down at his feet and clenching his fists. Unclenching them. His mouth is agape. ”I’m leaving.” is all he says, inaudible over the heated conversation, before he gets up and walks out the door.

Castorice is already gathering her and Polyxia’s things, stuffing them haphazardly in her Kuromi bag and blinking back tears. ”Cas…” Polyxia says, and Phainon notices her hand twitching ever so slightly in her lap, an almost instinctual drive to comfort her sister. It's a gesture so small, so delicate, that Phainon thinks he imagined it. Hyacine and Aglaea are trying to get Cipher to agree with being taken home– Aglaea has even gotten up and walked around the table, her hand on Cipher’s shoulder. The grip she has on Garmentmaker’s handle is unforgiving. Cipher is arguing back with the both of them fiercely, and the waiters must have taken notice because a security guard is walking over. Hysilens is on the phone with Cerydra, asking her to drive over and pick her up. Tribios has gone to the bar to pay the bill, and–

With one glorious swing, Cipher has shattered it all, this nice little fun moment. Phainon can’t even find it in himself to really blame her. Ruining things is his specialty.

The security guard seems to be diffusing the situation, with Cipher finally conceding to going home. As Hyacine links her arm with hers and starts leading her outside through the back door, security guard in tow, Aglaea addresses him without looking at him. “Go check on Mydei.”

It all happened so fast that it left Phainon in a daze. He cannot even bear to look at Cipher as he moves past her, yet he catches the sound of her hushed, crazed apologies whispered like a prayer to Hyacine.

He finds Mydei outside, angrily tapping on his phone. He stands a little too close to the street for Phainon’s liking, and every time a car rushes by it sends his bangs flying in every direction. There is a slight shake to his hands, as if there is something uncontainable waiting to jump out of him. Phainon strides over carefully, silently as if he might spook him away, and puts his hand on his shoulder. “He–”

Before he can get the word out, Mydei startles and grabs his wrist with such force that it unstabilizes Phainon, doubling him over. Mydei is grasping him hard and twisting. “Mydei– aghh, fuck, let go!”

There is a brief moment, shorter than a breath, where their gazes meet, and the look in Mydei’s eyes is fierce, stormy and dark, almost crazed; Phainon cannot help but think it is also desperately lovely. Terrible like a triumphant king. Majestic even, awe-inspiring as only an executioner can be. A lion clutching an oryx between his jaw, and Phainon only wants to lean in and offer his jugular for the taking. His eyes search for something on Phainon’s face and when he finds it – Phainon watches with rapt attention as, little by little, every muscle in Mydei’s face relaxes, softens, brightens up in recognition and then reddens in shame. He lets go of his wrist as if he just realized he was holding a red-hot iron, and steps back. “Phainon.” he says, sounding a bit breathless, “I’m sorry. You startled me.”

“Jesus, Mydei!” Phainon shakes his wrist and rubs it. To ascertain the damage– yes, it is going to bruise, and Phainon can’t wait. How splendid it is going to be, he thinks, to wear the evidence of Mydei’s touch like a bracelet. Phainon tries to make himself seem very upset when he speaks now, because if he speaks as his heart dictates, he is going to sound so love-drunk it would even disgust the old poets. “Ouch, man, like what the fuck?”

”Sorry.” He sounds genuinely remorseful, and he cannot quite look at Phainon. Without saying anything else, he turns back to his phone. Phainon feels a bit bad for playing it up, but still shuffles over to stand next to him. Mydei allows it, at least for now, and Phainon’s a bit of a jerk so he can’t help but snoop on him; he cranes his neck a bit to see what he’s doing on his phone.

He’s ordering an Uber.

“Didn't you drive here?”

“Hmph. I did, but I had too much to drink. I’m not good to drive.”

That’s probably the responsible thing to do. Mydei did have quite a few beers, not enough to be drunk but certainly enough to be a little tipsy.

Phainon breathes in to talk again, but Mydei snaps around like a hurricane. “What do you want?”

He gapes a little, opening and closing his mouth, looking for words that won’t come. Then, finally, “I just wanted to make sure you’re good.”

“I’m good.”

“Are you… sure?”

Mydei’s frown only deepens. “I am not a child, I can self-regulate.”

“I just– look, I’m sorry about Cipher, I don’t know what came ov–”

“I am not interested in having this conversation.”

Alright. Be like that, then.

Mydei turns back to his phone, and huffs angrily. He shakes it a bit as if that’s gonna fix whatever’s wrong with it. Phainon, foolish as always, tries again. “What’s wron–”

“It says there’s no drivers nearby.” his voice is even when he says it, yet Phainon can hear him mutter under his breath, ”Fuck, I want to go home.”

“Are you, um–” Phainon sighs, takes a deep breath, “Look, I’m not sure what she was talking about and you don’t have to tell me, that’s fine, but you seem a little out of it. What about your roommates, can they come pick you up?”

Mydei doesn’t grace him with a glance. “No, they’re not at home.”

“...None of them? Not even one of five?”

“No, Phainon. Hephaestion and Leonnius are visiting their parents in Kremnos. Peucesta is at his boyfriend’s house and Perdikkas is caught in an overnight shift at the hospital. Ptolemy… I’m not sure where he went, but he’s not home. Is that sufficient information for you?”

“Mydei, I’m not trying to be a dick. I’m just concerned.”

Mydei is gripping his phone so hard Phainon thinks he’s going to break it, and he wants nothing more than to reach over and smooth his hand over his. His palms are itching at the very thought, so he shoves them in his pockets. “There’s no need to be concerned for me.”

Phainon is feeling very desperate all of a sudden. Desperate to keep him close, desperate to open him up and probe him. ’I can mend your hurt,’ he thinks, hopelessly fond, ’Let me, just let me.’

“I’ll drive you home.”

It comes out of him suddenly, violently almost, like an animal bursting out of its cage. He catches himself off guard, the usual liar finding himself incurable with sincerity. His heart nearly jumps out of his chest, and he goes to clutch at it instinctively, smoothing his hand over the core of his sternum. Caressing between his breasts as if that might help calm the nerves. He swallows thickly.

He did not mean to say it, yet he meant it earnestly nonetheless.

Mydei studies him for a while, his predacious eyes lingering over his face, over the nervous tint in his shaky breath. He is scared, he is– he hasn’t, not since, Cyrene– she… Her teeth–

“Okay.” Mydei finally says.

Phainon releases a breath he didn’t know he was holding. He feels as though he were a criminal exonerated just before the blade kissed his neck. Mydei fishes in his pocket for his keys, then hands them to him.

Phainon just… looks at him, incredulous. It’s as if he’s forgotten how to act or think. Mydei cocks an eyebrow and jingles his keys. Phainon stares still, unmoving.

A notification pops up on Mydei’s phone. “Oh,” he says, “Nevermind, they found me a car–”

Phainon snaps out of it with a gasp that startles Mydei. He reaches over and snatches the keys out of his care. “I’ll do it,” he declares boldly, more to convince himself than anything else. “C’mon, cancel the ride. I’ll do it.”

Mydei does not look convinced, not at all. Phainon is already starting to walk past him. “Look, man, it’s a free ride. Are you taking it or not?”

To that, all Mydei says is, “You’re going the wrong way,” and he gestures with his head in the direction where his car is parked.

They walk side by side in silence, though it is not a long walk– Mydei got super lucky with the parking spot. Phainon would be jealous if he was still driving a car. Instead, he is so scared he considers throwing up and running away. Every step he takes feels torturous, as if he were walking barefoot on hot coals; the soles of his feet singed off and cooked to a crisp, rendered useless by the anguish.

Next thing he knows, he’s in the driving seat gripping the wheel like he’s trying to asphyxiate it. He does not remember when he got into the car, but he feels Mydei’s warmth next to him, feels him fiddle with the seatbelt.

It was Christmas, and it was snowing, and the news never warned of black ice on the roads. That night was not much different than this one, and he was yet again the sober driver to a drunk passanger– though Mydei is not nearly as gone as Cyrene was. He hears the seatbelt click into place.

Phainon’s fingers flex and unflex on the steering wheel as if testing its stability.

“What’s wrong?” Mydei’s voice cuts through the stale air of the car so violently that it makes Phainon physically cringe. What isn’t wrong would be the better question. He thinks of how to best answer it, and then decides to show his ass and be honest.

“I got in a car crash almost a year ago.”

Mydei is quiet for a moment, two seconds too long, enough time to make Phainon’s heartbeats pick up speed. He screws his eyes shut, equal parts embarrassed and scared, and then–

A warm hand on his arm, gripping just above his wrist. Gentle this time, entirely way too delicate. Mydei’s thumb rubs in small circles, too close to the old scar. He cannot bear to look at him, not now, he does not want to see pity reflected in his eyes; not from him as well.

“You’re all talk for being such a scaredy-cat.”

“What?”

Phainon swings around to look at him, and he is surprised by the distinct lack of pity in his eyes. He is grinning, a sort of cocky half-smirk, and he looks– a little amused, a little satisfied, yet kind still. Something soft, tender, like he’s trying to not spill the yolk out of a cracked egg. Mydei approaches the matter with an odd sort of casualty, like car crashes are just part of everyday life. Like Phainon’s life hasn’t been wrapped around it like a centipede curling on itself.

This new approach hits him like a bucket of cold ice, and Phainon cannot be anything but revenant. His eyes are practically sparkling. He’s being treated with care, yet not as if he could break. He’s being treated like…

A normal human being, perhaps?

“No, no, I’m just saying. I didn’t expect Phainon of Aedes Elysiae to be so scared of a fifteen minute drive.”

Phainon’s mouth falls open, and the grin on Mydei’s face only deepens at that. His eyes are crinkling, his dimples looking positively kissable. The passing cars and the streetlamps make an odd light show of his features, shadows waltzing across his face, ever-moving. It all feels a bit surreal, the tight air, the hand that has not stopped caressing his arm. His hands are so calloused, worked to the bone, yet precise and gingerly still. Beautiful white teeth, sharp canines, made for biting and tearing flesh. All of a sudden, Phainon can only think of smooching him.

“If you can get me home in ten, I’ll give you one of my fancy craft beers.”

“Fucking deal .”

He gets Mydei home in nine, because he catches all the green lights.

His place is a house, like an actual house, which makes sense because there’s six grown motherfuckers living there. It’s… surprisingly tidy inside. Like weirdly tidy, almost sterile, everything in its place, every stylistic choice deliberate. It’s spacious, and Mydei left some windows open to air out the house; it’s cool inside, but not uncomfortably so. He’s told to make himself at home in the living room, and so Phainon picks one of the armchairs and perches on it. The buzzing in the back of his head has gotten quieter, yet it still persists.

He hears Mydei opening the fridge in the kitchen, and then he comes back with four fancy beer bottles; they seem to be like, plastic or some shit. He throws one at Phainon and Phainon catches it. Cracks it open without checking the label and takes a big sip.

Holy shit.

He swallows because he has no other choice, but it’s not a pleasant ordeal.

“Why the fuck is it spicy?”

“It’s made with hot chili.”

“Man, what the hell?”

“What? You don’t like it?” Mydei cocks his head, sounding genuinely surprised that Phainon doesn’t like fiery devil’s diarrhea tasting beer.

“No, I don’t.”

Mydei rolls his eyes and looks over the labels of the other bottles. “This one is blueberry with chocolatey undertones.”

“Yeah, that sounds good.”

This time, Mydei chucks the bottle at him, aiming for his head. Too bad, dipshit, Phainon was the top basketball player on his middle-school team. He’s still got it, because he catches it midair right when it’s about to hit him. He tastes it, now a little more careful, and– yeah, that’s blueberry with chocolatey undertones. It’s sweet, like actual juice.

“You have the palate of a toddler.”

“Sorry, not all of us are Kremnoans used to drinking boiling blood.”

“That’s not true, that’s–”

“Ancient anti-Kremnoan propaganda, I know. What about the Blade of Fury, is that also propaganda?” God, Phainon loves pulling at his pigtails. Mydei scoffs.

“How could it be propaganda? There’s pictures of it. You know, you can see it from anywhere in Kremnos, no matter where you are. That’s how grand it is. Big, huge marble statue. It’s beautiful.”

Phainon can’t even argue with that– it is beautiful. One of the last remaining ancient wonders of the world.

They drink the beers together. And then Mydei goes and gets some more from his fridge, and they drink those too. Before he knows it, Phainon’s vision is a little blurry, and Mydei is swaying while sitting. Yeah, he’s not driving back home.

“Let’s play a game.” Mydei says out of nowhere, slurring his speech a little.

“Alright, what game?”

“I tell you– hrmph, I tell you a secret, and then you tell me a secret, and then so on.”

Phainon hums a little, thoughtful. “Alright. How do we decide a winner?”

“No, there’s no winner.”

Weird, coming from Mydei. Phainon shrugs. “Sounds goo–”

“I’ll start.” Mydei shifts on the couch, getting more comfortable and sitting with one leg bent under him. “In 2009, my dad tried to kill me and then successfully killed my mom. It was all over the news and I was under anonymity because I was a minor, but it was a very public case and some junky magazine released my full name and my likeness. It’s forever on the internet now. That’s what Cipher found, and what everybody that googles me finds.”

Okay.

Phainon takes in a deep, shaky breath. Where does he even start? He instantly, like instantly , sobers up, all the haze of the alcohol gone with the snap of a finger. He can only look at Mydei, and what stares back at him is– bitterly sad. His jaw clenching and unclenching, his eyes exhausted. It is a melancholy gaze, the one that Mydei casts upon him, somber even– yet, what Phainon finds most breathtaking is the simmering fury beneath it, the odd sort of pride. An unyielding, devastating determination. ’God,’ he thinks then, and the small corner lamp gives Mydeimos a golden halo, ’He is so beautiful. He is so woeful.’

“I’m sorry that happened, Myd–”

“Your turn.”

Phainon winces at that, and the command makes him shudder. He’d do anything Mydei told him. He doesn’t feel like following up ’my mother was murdered’ with ’that’s funny, I also murdered someone’ is appropriate. So, instead–

“I tried to kill myself like, five months ago? Five and a half, maybe, I don’t remember. I got very close, too. Had to get stitches, then I was on suicide watch for a few days.”

Mydei doesn’t seem to react to that, just reaches for another beer. His voice is casual and even when he speaks. “Yeah, I noticed the scar.”

“Got matching ones.” Phainon stretches out his hands and brings his wrists together, showing off the thick white scars there, jagged like the teeth of a saw. Mydei cranes his neck to look.

“You missed, didn’t you? Got some nerve damage along the way?”

Phainon laughs nervously, but weirdly enough it is– it’s not shame that drives his nerves, not the ugly kind that he bathes in. It is the same puerile nervousness that he feels when he makes a small oopsie. Something about all of this feels incredibly normal, kind of like… Mydei gets it, and understands it, and he’s not making a whole thing out of it. “Yeah, something like that.”

He watches as Mydei drinks an entire bottle of beer, crushes it in his hand, and throws it away. “My turn. When I was twenty-two, I was raped by my boyfriend.”

Okay.

Phainon’s heart sinks to the bottom of his stomach, and a cold chill overtakes him. There it is– here comes the bad bad no good at all shame . He feels like killing himself out of nowhere.

Mydei looks worse for wear. He physically recoils when he says that, his hand coming to slap over his mouth. His eyes shoot wide open, terrified. He’s looking at Phainon, and he’s horrified . Helpless. “I never told anyone that. Just my therapist.”

“Mydei, I–”

“I’m gonna throw up.”

And with that he bolts. Runs to what Phainon assumes is the bathroom. A door is opened and the sound of Mydei’s knees hitting the tile floor is sickening . He retches, all liquid, for a long while. Phainon can only sit and sink into a strange feeling of despair. He rubs over his heart as though that may calm him, and only one thought mars his mind–

What have I done to him?

When Mydei returns, he can barely hold himself up. He’s practically dragging his feet behind him, and he sits down on the couch heavily with a thump. He does not look at Phainon, yet Phainon looks at him nonetheless. He’s grown pallid, sweat-slicked. His hands are shaking.

None speak. Phainon breaks the silence.

“Mydei, look, I just want to say I– I’m sorry, for… I didn’t know, you know, so– I apologize. For that day in the gym, for always kind of grabbing at you–”

”Stop it.”

That simmering fury, it’s boiling over. He is mad, really mad. The whiteness of terror has given way to the redness of anger. “This is why– This is why I don’t tell people this. They start treating me differently.”

“No, Mydei, I’m not treating you differently, and I’m not gonna, it’s just–” Phainon gestures wildly with his hands, desperate to get his point across. “If I ever made you uncomfortable–”

“Shut up, stop. I’m–” he looks like he’s about to cry, “I’m an adult, I’m capable of consent. I’m not–”

“No, I know, it’s just–”

”I’m not helpless!”

Mydei yells, and he grabs an empty bottle and chucks it at the wall. Knocks down a picture hanging on it and it shatters on the wooden floor. His voice is more booming than Phainon expected. Whatever argument he had dies down with it. Phainon just runs his hand over his eyes, pinching the bridge of his nose. He feels like he’s gonna throw up, too.

“It’s not a big deal,” Mydei continues, “Stop making it a big deal.”

“I’m not–”

“We were having sex and he tried to choke me and I freaked out, I told him to stop and he didn’t. That’s it. It’s not a big deal.”

“Okay,” Phainon says, trying to placate him, to diffuse the situation. “It’s not a big deal.”

“Right.”

The silence is stifling, oppressive. It’s constricting all around him, cutting off his airflow. He can’t stop thinking about it, about the what ifs .

“Mydei.”

“Hm?”

“For my sake, please, because I will drive myself crazy…” Phainon can’t finish it. The sigh that breaks out of him is painful, shaky, and it comes out as more of a sob.

Mydei shifts on the couch. “Look at me,” he demands, and Phainon follows like an obedient dog.

He looks– he’s so kind. Incredibly upset, ravaged by grief, yet so mellow. So approachable. Phainon wants to beg for an embrace.

“I’m sorry for yelling at you. I freaked out,” when Phainon opens his mouth to speak, Mydei just raises his hand to silence him. “Let me finish, please.” He takes a very deep breath. “You haven’t done anything to make me uncomfortable. I have enjoyed all of your touches a lot, even when you’re playful and you grab me. I mean, I do the same to you, don’t I?”

“Yeah, but… Y’know, it’s… different, I guess.”

“Phainon, I really don’t want it to be, okay? I have a lot of shit going on. I don’t want to be treated like a delicate flower by you.”

Phainon wants to cry. He really wants to cry. He’s going to cry. “Okay, yeah. I get that.”

“We can just pretend this never happened.”

“No, I don’t…” Phainon gets up from the armchair, and walks over to the couch where Mydei is. His gaze follows him as he moves, and when Phainon just lingers in front of him, Mydei scoffs and moves aside to make room for him. He sits down next to him. “I don’t want to pretend like this never happened. I think, maybe, it’s good that you told me. Um. Brings us closer together or something.”

Mydei’s chuckle is self-deprecating, but it lingers into a handsome smile. “Yeah, maybe.” and then a moment later– “You look like shit.”

“Look, man, it’s a lot, okay?”

“Oh, it’s a lot for you? My bad, chief.” He raises his arms in mock surrender, and then laughs so sincerely that it makes Phainon’s heart ache. Despite that, however, he can’t help but laugh a little too.

In a bout of what is perhaps pure madness , Phainon brings his palm forward, raises it up– and presses it against one of Mydei’s. Mydei startles at first, unsure of its meaning, and then he relaxes, slowly. He allows it. Phainon intertwines their fingers, and brings their joined hand to his lap.

They just look at each other for a while.

“You’re hiding something from me, aren’t you?” Mydei says, though it is not an accusation.

“Yeah, I am.”

“Are you going to tell me?”

“One day.”

“That’s cruel, Phainon. I’m all naked in front of you.”

“God, I wish you were, though.” Phainon laughs, and Mydei laughs too.

It’s so easy to hold his gaze. Twin pools of molten gold, his pretty lashes wet with tears. Phainon is a weak man. His free hand comes to Mydei’s face, cups his sharp cheekbones, and with his thumb he wipes some of the unshed tears there. Mydei simply nuzzles into his palm, pressing closer, and sighs deeply.

“It’s left me a walking corpse,” he whispers, as if he were praying, “The rape.”

“No,” and Phainon prays back, “I don’t think it has.”

Mydei sneers at that, and all the softness leaves him. He moves out of Phainon’s hold, putting space between them. “It can’t be loved out of me.”

“I know.” But I can help.

Mydei gets up and goes to clean up the broken glass and the beer bottle. “You can stay the night, if you want to. Take Leonnius’ room or something. I’m– tired. I’m going to bed.”

It ends like that. Mydei cleans up for a little bit, and then shows Phainon to Leonnius’ room. He gives him some pajamas, and then retreats into his bedroom.

Phainon lays still in this strange bed for a long time, unable to sleep, wishing he were in Mydei’s instead. He rolls over to his side and catches sight of the bruise on his wrist, from when Mydei grabbed him. It has started to redden, looking almost furious. When he probes it with his finger, he finds it tender to the touch. Phainon’s heart quickens at the prospect of it turning purple-blue, then yellow-green, and then eventually fading back into his flesh. Carrying around Mydei’s mark, if only for a week, such physical evidence of his existence, so shockingly real.

It is no wonder, then, that Phainon’s overtaken by a need to claim back.

He brings his wrist to his mouth and kisses it as if it were a lover– as if it were Mydei. He runs his lips over it, upwards and downwards, and he swears he can taste jasmine tea and pomegranate and expensive craft beer. His tongue lolls out to lick at it, to suck, to savour the salty flesh there. He imagines it is Mydei instead, his beautiful lips, his bosom, the hard, flat planes of his stomach and then lower still. He is sighing into it, gasping quietly, whispering things he’d rather not repeat.

Phainon orgasms untouched.

When he sleeps, it is with a clearer head than ever in the last nine months.

Mydei has a nightmare.

He is ten years old and he is killing a cat. The rest ought to remain unspoken– the cat wears his face, and then his mother’s, then his uncle’s. When the cat puts on his father’s face, that is when it transforms into a great red lion, and its strength overwhelms him. It pins him to the ground and dives into his soft belly, tearing his flesh, pulling out his innards.

It hurts, but only because he deserves it.

The first time Mydei looked for comfort after a nightmare, he was three years old and gripping his Simba plushie. The last time Mydei looked for comfort after a nightmare is now, twenty-five years old and still gripping his Simba plushie.

The door to Leonnius’ room creaks when it opens, and he lingers in the doorway. Phainon awakes with a small startle. He is half-asleep, face swollen and marred by lines left by the bedsheets. His eyes are bleary, unseeing. Mydei’s silhouette is blackened by the darkness, illuminated at the edges by the moonlight.

Phainon groans, shifts a little. “Cyrene?”

Perhaps that is all Mydei needed. He returns to his room, stepping softly, and goes back to bed.

He leaves the both of them to their nightmares.

When they wake up the next morning, properly wake up that is, Mydei will cook Phainon a small healthy breakfast. Phainon will undoubtedly say something stupid, and the both of them will laugh over it. Then he will drive Phainon back home, before returning to his own abode.

He will go to Leonnius’ room to make sure everything is in place, because Leonnius is a bit of a clean freak, and that is when he will see it– a small strand of hair, shining like silver amongst the pillows. He will pick it up carefully, with such reverence one might think he is handling the Shroud of Turin. He will hold it up in the sunlight, see how it glimmers pale and pearly like the mane of an unicorn.

And he will bring it to his lips, and kiss it.

Chapter End Notes

i was very nervous about this chapter because i was unsure of how explicit i should be about mydei's trauma. i decided, though, that it's better to be sincere and frank with it. call it what it is and show how it most commonly looks like. i even got emotional writing this one at some point lol

Chapter Notes

Hi, I'm back with almost 14k words. Had to take a break from this fic cause it burned me out but wahoo here we are. I love this fic so much.

!IMPORTANT!

This is a Mydei-centric chapter and that always comes with a general SA and CHILD & DOMESTIC ABUSE TW. There are two explicit scenes TW'd below, but generally, Mydei is dealing with the emotional and psychological consequences of his abuses all throughout the fic.

Click me

There are little pockets of time Mydei seems to return to.

Take, for example, this—

He is nine years old and very skinny. He’s very scared and very upset and he tries his best to be silent—he can’t sleep because he’s frightened, and he’s frightened because his dad came home drunk and angry again, and he got into an ugly fight with Mom.

Eurypon is pacing just outside his door, and he’s muttering something Mydei can’t quite make out; still, Mydei can tell he is disturbed, troubled, not quite himself. He’s hiding under his blanket and keeping very very still, as if his father were a prowling lion and he a newborn gazelle—as if even the slightest movement, nevermind the separation of the wooden door, could snap Eurypon’s cold gaze onto him.

It happens exactly as he feared—Eurypon swings the door open like a man crazed, a movement so sudden and unexpected and loud that it startles Mydei out of his cover, and he just… stands there for a moment. Slick with sweat, breathing hard. Brutally handsome, like the teeth of a chainsaw. He’s looking at Mydeimos, amber to amber, two scorpions encased in time. There was a time, many years ago, when Eurypon would hoist him up on his lap and scratch his smooth cheeks with his beard, making him laugh. He looked deep into the boy’s eyes then, intense, and said that they’re so so alike with both of their golden hues, that it’s very rare and it means God loves them so much more. Said that it’s special.

Eurypon’s eyes aren’t really amber or golden right now. They’re black like the pit of a well. Black like the abyss. Black like a bruise.

And Mydei is scared, he’s proper scared now, and his heart is running so fast it starts to skip beats.

It’s like looking into a shark’s eyes. Beady and shiny like polished stone, and cold too. There’s nothing reflected in them.

Empty.

“Mydeimos,” his father speaks, and the voice isn’t his. It sounds different, distant, nearly inhuman. As if someone took his skin and was wearing it around like a trophy. “Put on your shoes. We’re going for a drive.”

“But it’s late,” Mydei says before he can catch himself.

He knows he’s said the wrong thing, because Eurypon clenches and unclenches his fist. His anger seethes like boiling blood just beneath his skin, and his jaw is set in so much tension Mydei is afraid he’s going to shatter all of his teeth. His dad is trying so hard to be good, but Mydei can tell he wants to snap at him. Lounge at him. Eurypon takes in a deep breath, shaky, and he can see his entire chest quiver with it, as if inhalation has become impossible for him. The mere act of containing himself was physically difficult for Eurypon.

The distance between them, between the bed and the door, becomes suffocating. Endlessly stretching yet desperately close. Eurypon is both an ocean away, and yet so close that Mydei can see every eukaryotic cell in his body. The nucleus and the mitochondria. He thinks theirs must be identical, like their eyes—something fundamentally twinsome, a two-headed calf. Mydei thinks, when he’s sure God can’t hear him, that he and his father must be the same person but at different times. That Eurypon is the adult Mydeimos coming back from the future to torment him for a mistake he’s made.

When he’s sure God (that being, Eurypon) can’t see him, Mydei likes to buy a carton of eggs with his allowance. He brings them to school in his backpack (it has lion ears on it) and runs his fingers over them while the teacher is talking about the Battle of Ludon. He thinks about the baby inside of it (he doesn’t know that the eggs you eat aren’t fertilized, he’s just nine years old) and if its momma was sad when the farmer took her babies away. He wonders if his mom would be sad if the farmer took him away from her, but he overheard her on the phone once with her brother saying, “I can’t leave, ‘cause of Mydei” so of course, the logical conclusion is that she would be quite happy. Means that she could leave. He wonders what the farmer would do with him. After school, he finds a nice little park with a swing, and he sits on it while he throws the eggs on the hard pavement. He grows increasingly disappointed when he sees that each of them are white and yellow and there’s no baby. But he persists. And every month he buys a new carton of eggs and cracks them open in the park. Sometimes he watches as little birds come to eat from the yolk. One time, however, after many tries, he cracks one egg and sees that it’s different. It’s hot orange and shot with little red veins that pulse uselessly, and there’s this pink little thing inside with a big black dot in the middle of it. That’s the baby, he thinks. He scoops it up and it’s… not really a chick, though Mydei knows it’s supposed to be one. It’s just something that could possibly be a chick, just like how Mydei is something that could possibly be a person. He puts the embryo in his pocket and carries it home.

He’s not sure why he’s thinking about it now, but he gasps when he hears Eurypon’s old dress shoes squeak as he steps closer to him. He flinches away by instinct, and puts his arm up to guard himself. His dad scoffs at that, and simply pulls his blanket off of him. “I know it’s late, just come on. Stop talking back to me.”

“Okay,” Mydei squeaks, small, “I’ll let Mom know.”

That really was the wrong thing to say, because his dad groans and runs his hands over his face. He grabs onto his beard and pulls, the way he always does when he’s stressed out. “Why does your fucking mom need to know about everything that goes on in this fucking house?” He’s not quite yelling, but he’s not talking sweet either. He has an edge in his voice, simmering with rage, and it’s enough to scare Mydei into paleness. He’s learned from a very young age that when there’s an angry man in the house, everybody has to work together and try really hard to keep him calm and happy. So that’s what Mydei does right now.

“...Sorry. I won’t tell her.”

“Go put on your shoes. And get your jacket, it’s cold outside.”

“Yes, sir.”

And Mydei does as told, because his obedience keeps Eurypon at bay. He treats this whole ordeal like he’s stuck in a cage with a wild tiger—and essentially, that is exactly what’s happening. He leaves his bed slowly and realizes, with horror, that Eurypon is standing in front of the door. That means he has to go past him if he wants to leave. Mydei is too nervous to approach, scared that Eurypon might snap and grab him. He looks up at him, pleading, ashamed of it.

Hard to believe. If Eurypon’s not doing something to Gorgo, then he’s doing something to Mydei. Something is always happening in this house. Still, Eurypon moves aside. Gives Mydei a clear exit.

Mydei thinks, well, even if he’s grabbed, that’s not as bad as what Mom usually gets. And maybe his dad is being genuine. He decides to be a very brave little boy, and he steps past Eurypon. The smell of alcohol and tobacco clinging to him hits him like spoiled curdled milk. He makes a sour face, and Eurypon laughs harder at that. “Your dad smells bad, huh?” and he checks to smell his breath, “Sorry, kid. Come on.”

Eurypon grabs his shoulder and the gesture isn’t violent in and of itself, but Mydei has come to expect it so he startles nonetheless. He lets himself be led downstairs to the closet, and Eurypon keeps watch over him as he fishes out his sneakers and his jacket.

He’s fiddling with his zipper and can’t quite get it in, because his hands are trembling. He’s very nervous, because his dad wants to drive drunk in the middle of the night and Mydei just learned in school that you’re not supposed to do that. The insertion pin keeps slipping away from him. Eurypon sighs, and it is affectionate—it must be, because he gets down on his knees and helps Mydei zip it up. Then he pats the jacket down and fixes it around his shoulders; it’s a little big. Mom sized up so he could ‘grow into it’.

“There you go.”

“Thanks, Dad.”

They walk to the car, hand in hand. Two unloveable things. The air outside is so cold, and he can’t breathe. He goes to sit in the back, but Eurypon asks him to take the front seat instead. He even helps Mydei with the belt.

It smells so bad. He smells so bad. The car is dripping oil from somewhere, if the stench is anything to go by, even though Eurypon made a whole scene out of saying he got the fucking thing fixed when Mom asked him about it.

They drive in silence at first. It’s just them on the road, and Eurypon isn’t speeding up or acting crazy, so Mydei thinks they probably won’t both die in a fiery car explosion.

“Are you hungry? Let’s stop at McDonald’s.”

Mydei looks up to him, and is met with Eurypon’s expectant gaze.

“No, not really.”

That was also the wrong thing to say, because he starts to grip the steering wheel so hard that he might break it clean off. He grits his teeth. “Stupid me for trying to do something nice for you for once. Fucking—”

Everybody has to work very hard to keep the angry man in the house happy.

“Actually, um, I am a bit hungry. Yeah. We could stop at McDonald’s.”

That seems to do it. Mydei isn’t sure what to order when they get there, because he’s worried that if he orders too much, it’s going to make Eurypon mad. So he settles for a McChicken and a small portion of fries. Eurypon tells the lady at the counter to throw in a big chocolate milkshake too, even though the weather’s freezing cold. He doesn’t get anything for himself, and instead settles to watch Mydei eat outside.

He’s watching him closely and it’s kind of unnerving. Mydei tries to focus on his food, but every once in a while he will flit his eyes up towards his dad and find him staring back with a severe gaze. Though he does not seem to be staring at him, not really, but more so through him. His eyes are a little glassy, a little glazed over, and his brows furrow and unfurrow. His hands are linked together in front of his mouth like some villain from the animes Mydei likes to watch, and he can tell that his mouth is twitching over unsaid words.

It’s as if he’s arguing with someone in his head. Perhaps he’s arguing with himself. Or with the memory of his father. Mydei finds it creepy and struggles to finish his food and his milkshake, because he’s worried that if he doesn’t, Eurypon is going to be mad.

“All done,” he says, pushing his tray forward, and he’s so full it’s uncomfortable. He feels like throwing up.

That’s when Eurypon’s glare sharpens—he was somewhere far away seemingly, and only now came back. He looks at Mydei for a second, and then chuckles. “I just realized you’re wearing your pajamas.”

Mydei looks down at his jammies—they’re orange with Simba heads on them. “What’s wrong with my pajamas?”

“Nothing, just–” Eurypon chuckles again, and it makes Mydei smile a little too, “Nothing. Let’s go.”

Mydei figured out, about ten minutes into their drive, that they’re essentially driving in circles. And Eurypon is growing restless. He’s arguing with invisible enemies again, his whole face twitching in anger and dropping in sorrow. It must be a hell of a fight. Mydei tries to look away, look out the window, but feels himself mesmerized by it. By him.

“Your mother wasn’t always like that,” Eurypon says all of a sudden, “She used to be nice. Then you came along.”

“Ah.”

“Now all she does is provoke me.”

“Oh.”

“And I can’t help myself when she’s like that.”

“Mmm.”

“And you love pissing me off too. I swear, sometimes it’s like you two gang up on me.”

“Ah… I’m sorry, Dad. I don’t mean to.”

“Yeah…” Eurypon says, more to himself than anyone else, and his eyes are dazed, “I know you don’t.”

More silence passes. Mydei starts to count the times they’ve passed by the McDonald’s. Is he stalling…?

“Mydeimos…” Eurypon whispers at one point, and his voice is full of longing. Mydei looks up at him and finds his face full of strange affection. “You look just like her sometimes.”

That must be a bad thing. Dad doesn’t like Mom very much anymore.

“Oh. I’m sorry.”

When they get home, nearly half an hour later, Mydeimos is so carsick he thinks he’s going to vomit all the McDonald’s he ate. He quickly slips out of his shoes and his jacket and arranges them neatly in their rightful place, and really he’s just happy that he survived the car ride. He goes to cross the hallway, but he feels Eurypon’s burning gaze at his back. It’s enough to make him stop and look back.

“Dad…?”

He stares into the maw of a wolf. His eyes are polished stones again. He is clenching his fists, uncleaching them, flexing his fingers. Shifting his weight from one leg to the other. He’s pale like the bark of a birch tree. Everything about him is dull. Lusterless. There’s fear in those beady little eyes, almost childlike, and Mydei wonders if Eurypon is back in his childhood home, thirty years ago, standing over his mother while his dad is beating the living hell out of both of them. Eurypon has told Mydei one or two things about his grandfather. How he was a hardworking salt-of-the-earth man that also had a very peculiar hobby called ‘belting your child so hard he passes out’. “You must think I’m so awful,” he said once, drunk like a dog, “But I’m not. I’m not like him. And you should be grateful.”

All of the cells in Mydei’s body are screaming danger and telling him to fucking go. He wants to run, but if he does, then Eurypon is going to chase after him. And he’s going to catch him, because he’s older and stronger and bigger than Mydei, and he’s going to make him regret ever trying to run away.

They look at each other for a while, then Eurypon wipes his hand of sweat on his olive green jacket. “Mydei,” he says, beckoning him closer with it, “C’mere, kid.”

Mydei does, because the consequences of disobeying are worse than whatever Eurypon’s got planned for him. Mom is sleeping upstairs. He doesn’t want to wake her.

So he comes, though his legs want to betray him and book it. He walks on shaky stumps, and stops right in front of his dad.

Eurypon crouches down again, just like he did when he helped him with his jacket. He gets very close to Mydei. His face is red and blotchy, especially the tip of his nose. The stink of alcohol makes him want to retch. His golden eyes are soft and kind and a little wet. Bloodshot. He looks like he’s about to cry.

He grabs Mydei by the elbows first, gently, rubs his arms up to his shoulders. He squeezes them, manly and stoic, then moves to cup his face in both hands and caress his cheeks with his thumbs. Mydei is wildly uncomfortable, because Eurypon has never done this before. He can’t even attempt to understand what this is supposed to mean, or if it’s supposed to feel nice.

He smiles all yellow-toothed and he can barely hold his tears back. A small sob. The sight of his father crying is so novel and embarrassing that Mydei feels like crawling out of his skin and hiding away.

“Mydeimos…” Eurypon says, and he’s petting Mydei’s hair and rubbing under his eyes. “I love you very much, do you know that? Daddy loves you so much.”

Daddy…? Mydei cringes, but he tries to school his expression. He knows this is a nice thing that nice dads tell their nice sons. He’s never heard it from him before, though.

“Oh, uhm…” he shifts a little, uncomfortable, “...Thanks, Dad. Um. I love you too.”

Eurypon smiles harder at that and makes a sound stuck between a sob and a laugh.

And then his hands wrap around Mydei’s throat.

He sees his psychiatrist the next day and gets off lithium. The taste of his new medicine is as bitter as his father’s callouses.

The silver strand of hair rests in his wallet like a precious keepsake.
