Instead, he angles his head just so and Phainon, the darling boy, knows exactly what’s coming, so he settles himself and opens up wider. He’s so good for him. Mydei cradles his strong jawline with one hand and places the other on his neck, that pale, elegant column, just over his pulse point—he finds it racing at an alarming speed, yet Phainon is so languidly lascivious beneath him.

The smoke is gray and silky when Mydei blows it into his mouth, thick like molasses and slow-moving too, as if it had nothing better to do than caress the back of Phainon’s throat. He takes it all so well too, grabs harder onto Mydei’s hips to ground himself.

He pulls back to admire his work, and finds Phainon ruined; panting with his pretty mouth agape, forehead slick with sweat, his hair sticking to it like tendrils. It’s too dark here to see, but Mydei imagines he’s flushed red and beautiful. He looks fucked-out.

Shame on Mydei for letting his guard down; Phainon takes advantage of this opportunity to hook his arms around his waist and pull him fully in his lap. That gets Mydei’s heart pumping, even faster than it already was, and not in a good way—the surprise of it ruins the fragile balance of his nervous system. He frightens, tenses up, and grits his teeth; every fiber of his being is yelling danger.

Phainon notices gently pushes him off his lap before Mydei can pick whether to run away or punch all of his teeth out. “Sorry,” he says, sheepish, barely audible over the music.

And then it all hits him at once, the shame of it all, the loudness of everything, and then all Mydei can do is shut down a little. Disconnect just a tad, just enough to put some distance between himself and the world. “I want to go home,” he tells Phainon.

“Oh, sure. Let’s go.”

“No, you can stay if you want to.”

Phainon actually pouts at that, grown ass man, juts out his bottom lip all cutely and hmphs. “I don’t wanna stay without you…”

Mydei would find it very endearing if he wasn’t actively fighting against breaking every window in the house. He takes a deep breath, trying to still himself, and gets up. “Alright, let’s go.” He puts on his headphones and it all gets very quiet. It’s better, but not good, and he barely perceives Phainon holding onto him as he makes his way through the sea of people.

He doesn’t have the patience to search for Perdikkas and let him know they’re leaving, but he does find Ptolemy instead. He tells him that he’s just done, and Ptolemy nods and says something back but Mydei can’t quite hear him. He knows, however, that he gets it—that they all get it. He’s been here for four whole hours, and it’s well past 1 AM. He’s already pushed himself to his very limit. Ptolemy pats him on the shoulder as he, presumably, says goodbye and Mydei feels like gnawing his fingers off.

Mydei is so drained and so tired, but the cool night air helps a little; he feels poked and prodded and burned all over, flayed at the extremities, and he takes a moment to just breathe. This sucks, but he wouldn’t call it a mistake—Perdikkas seemed very happy that he came. With the music now no longer a problem, he can start trying to be normal. He’s half-here anyways, that light-headed buzz of dissociation settling like a heavy blanket over him, crushing him and—

Very silently, he can hear the annoying whining of Phainon’s voice. He’s talking to him and waving his hands. Mydei takes off his headphones.

“What are you saying?”

“I was asking if you’re good to drive.”

Mydei thinks about it. It’s not the first time he drives while disassociated, and he’s always careful about it. He could drive, but he doesn’t really want to.

“I mean, are you good to drive?”

Phainon hums. “I’m not high, if that’s what you’re asking.”

“I’m asking because of the car crash.”

That seems to stun him a little bit. Mydei gets a bit of a sick satisfaction out of seeing him squirm. “Ah, well…”

Phainon shifts his weight from one leg to the other as he considers it; he’s glowing beautifully in the moonlight, ethereal.

“Yeah, I think so. If we take it slow. Um. I’d do it for you.”

“For me, huh…” Mydei thinks bitterly. He doesn’t enjoy being taken care of, but if he’s to drive that means he has to keep his headphones off—and he’s not in the mood for loud noises anymore.

“Alright,” Mydei says, “Sure.”

He tosses Phainon the keys and he catches them midair. Opens his car door as if he owns it and gets comfortable in the driver’s seat; Mydei follows, settling next to him, slipping his headphones on.

“Wait,” Mydei says all of a sudden, “How are you going to get home?”

He cannot even hear himself ask it, but Phainon mouths ‘Uber’ at him. Sure, if that’s what he wants.

Phainon gets him home quickly. The streets are quiet and tranquil, and the swaying of the car almost lulls Mydei to sleep. He thinks he does doze off for a bit, because he feels Phainon shaking him. His mouth is moving for the letters of his name, M-Y-D-E-I, and Mydei thinks there are few sights more worth looking at than this one. His limbs are heavy.

He remembers his therapist telling him to be brave. To not run away. He takes off his headphones.

“Thanks,” he tells Phainon, and before Phainon can answer, he continues, “We should talk.”

“Oh? About what?”

“About…” and Mydei gestures vaguely between them, “This. Us. Phainon, look, I–”

Phainon puts a hand up. Tenses tight like a drawn bowstring. He smiles and chuckles, but it’s a sad thing; his demeanor changes, becomes distant, aloof. Cold like the ice that burns you. “I can’t. Not now. Please. I know. Another time.”

Ah. Mydei supposes that’s alright—with the Cipher thing going on, Phainon must be all over the place. He gets it, he really does. Can’t even say it bothers him at all, because it doesn’t. He’s willing to wait. To the heat death of the universe, if he has to.

“That’s fine.”

“I’m sorry, Mydei, I don’t want to—”

And Mydei gives him a little smile, genuine, because he knows that’s what Phainon needs.

“I’m not mad at you. Really.”

Phainon doesn’t seem convinced. “...Yeah?”

“Yeah,” he repeats, soft, “Why would I lie? I’m not.”

“You could lie to not make me feel bad.”

“I don’t really care about not making you feel bad. I care about telling the truth. I’m not mad.”

Mydei shrugs, and he continues, “And even if I were mad, I would get over it eventually.”

That seems to do it for Phainon, and he relaxes a bit. “Okay.”

He doesn’t feel like leaving the car yet, instead he looks out the window; gazes longingly at the dark night sky. He wishes Okhema were less polluted, so he could see the stars. He remembers a similar night, when he was being driven around by another man, some sixteen years ago. “Before my father killed my mother, he took me on a drive like this,” he says all of a sudden.

“I’m sorry.”

“I don’t like being the passenger either, just like you don’t,” he continues, and dares himself to meet Phainon’s gaze, “Though I find that I don’t mind if it’s you.”

“Yeah,” Phainon croaks out, throat sore and stiff, “I don’t mind if it’s you either.”

Mydei squeezes his shoulder, lingering on it just a bit too much to have it be just friendly. He takes the car keys out of the ignition himself. Exits the car and holds the door open for Phainon to leave, too.

He waits around with him as Phainon smokes a cigarette and orders his Uber. When his driver arrives, Phainon waves a bit awkwardly and disappears into the stranger’s car. Mydei wonders if he’s scared right now, but dispels the thought. He believes in Phainon—believes that he can be very brave.

As he makes himself comfortable in his own bed, Mydei finds that he is still pent up and frustrated and horny from their ministrations, which is unlike him, and it embarrasses him. He remembers, once again, his therapist telling him to be brave. That they are normal feelings. To experiment with masturbation.

This might as well happen, and why ever not? He’s a young man in the prime of his age, strong and virile, and perhaps it’s a waste of a perfectly nice cock. He hasn’t done this in years, at least three, but maybe before that too. He can’t remember the last time he touched himself.

Mydei sees little reason to do it. He figures he can’t cum because of his meds, common side-effect and all, and he hardly feels it anyways. He slips his hand beneath his waistband and takes himself in hand; he finds the sensation dulled. Something is there, but it’s numb. He clicks his tongue. He can’t say he’s surprised, but he is a bit disappointed. What was he expecting, really? This body is simply the miserable sack of meat he carries around, and he’s not even in it half the time. Three-quarters of the time, actually, to be accurate. He’s not quite half-hard but he’s not soft either, like a swan’s last dying song.

He pushes through it, even as his heart picks up the pace, not in arousal but in fear. Mydei’s brain can hardly tell who’s touching him, can’t tell it is himself, and his nervous system is so fucked up that even furniture accidentally brushing against his crotch sends him into a panic. But he has to be brave. His therapist told him to experiment, and maybe she didn’t mean like this, didn’t mean now, not when he’s drowning in shame and barely heaving off the overstimulation. To be fair, she definitely didn’t mean it like this. But fuck it, he finishes the things he starts, and so Mydei starts stroking.

It’s nothing, really. He barely registers the touch burning him where he is most sensitive. It’s unpleasant at best and unbearable at worst. It only sinks him deeper into disassociation, an uncomfortable disconnect, and the last remnants of his consciousness that cling to the body tell him to just think of something sexy and hot and kind.

So, he thinks of Phainon. He’s not sure how sexual fantasies are supposed to work, but in this one, they’re kissing on Mydei’s bed and Phainon is all over him. He kisses his jawline and his neck and his collarbone and Mydei knows, intellectually, that it’s supposed to feel good; instead it only scares him more, so he jumps ahead in the Sexy Fantasy timeline and suddenly, Phainon’s fucking him hard.

Fantasy Mydei enjoys it because this is a fantasy and he has to enjoy it, and he’s moaning but the voice isn’t quite his. He’s not sure whose it is, but nonetheless it makes Mydei want to cry. Fantasy Phainon is lovely and generous with his kisses, and as he thrusts upward into Fantasy Mydei, he grabs something off of the nightstand. Mydei doesn’t think about what it is, doesn’t conjure up an image, but it’s something heavy and blunt.

Fantasy Phainon kisses him sweetly and starts to pummel Fantasy Mydei over the head with the object, splitting his head open, spilling out his brains. He murders him beautifully, and he’s not Phainon anymore; he’s faceless, rather, a figure that is both his father and his rapist. That’s a little funny, his brain can’t even conceive the idea of Phainon hurting him. Through the violence and the gore, Fantasy Mydei screams ‘NO, PLEASE, STOP’. He doesn't know why he doesn't fight back. He's fully capable of doing so, with all the gym and the boxing lessons, but then again, the real Mydei was also capable of doing so.

Maybe Fantasy Mydei is just as scared as the real Mydei was.

This is kind of useless. Mydei comes back from his fantasy and finds that he’s grown soft in his hand. Yeah, he expected as much. What a spectacular failure. What was he even thinking?

He just managed to upset and trigger himself, and now he’s sitting crossarmed like a an idiot and staring up at the ceiling. Yeah, this might as well happen.

There’s something intrinsically broken about Mydei. A few months ago, he would just let it be. Accept himself as a desexed person. Now, though, he wants to fix it. He’s not sure how. But he wants to do it. For himself. Maybe a bit for Phainon, too.

His PTSD, just like his panic attacks, robes itself in the cold and heavy press of derealization. Nothing really feels real anymore, but at least he’s not exactly feeling anything. Emotionally. Physically. His poor brain, overworked to its last leg, gives him the escape of numbness, and Mydei is going to take it. It’s better than anything else it's tried in the past.

The next morning, he still feels like he’s half asleep and dreaming. All of his roommates are snoring and sleeping like logs after a night of partying. He makes himself a lazy breakfast— his limbs feel as though bound in iron, and he’s so sluggish that he bumps into the furniture on his way to the dining table. His phone chimes—a text message.

Mydei takes an embarrassingly long time to guess his password, but he gets it eventually; it’s his mother’s birth year.

Phainon

i got a cold from your friends stupid party

“Hah,” is all Mydei can manage. The tail end of a laugh.

Mydei

👎

Phainon

what do you mean “👎”

come deal with it

Mydei

What, so I can get sick as well?

Phainon

yes

we’re in this together

That does get a proper chuckle out of Mydei.

Mydei 👍

He could do that. For Phainon. Yes.

Mydei can’t help but wonder why he doesn’t mind when Phainon touches him. He knows the answer, of course, in the back of his head, but it’s a little too disgusting to think about.

No matter. Instead of thinking about it, Mydei looks up recipes for nice, warm soups that help with a cold.

Chapter End Notes

chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

This is a 17k word monster, and it could've been longer but I stopped myself. The concept is as such: scenes of love between the characters that I really wanted to show but had no better place to put, so I compiled them all into a chapter. The scenes themselves are non-linear and jump in time, but in the drop down below I've compiled a timeline of when each scene happens, alongside the usual trigger warnings.

This is probably my favourite chapter that I've ever written.

Click me

Vignettes of love—

Phainon has not been sick in six fucking years. Colds are what kids get. There should be no such thing as a grown adult with a fever.

And yet, here we are. Twenty-seven years old and sick as a dog with the flu. The flu. At his grown age. Phainon is more embarrassed than anything, really, and he’s already used his paid sick days so it’s just like—okay, sick and broke and raw-dogging psychosis. He takes a very miserable bus trip to his doctor and gets a medical note that says yeah, he’s fucked. He snaps a picture of it and sends it directly to Hyacine through DMs, because he’s in no mood to email HR and potentially have Anaxa see—that would truly be mortifying. Phainon can practically already hear them; “The flu? At your age? Hah.”  At least Hyacine would be more empathetic to his plight.

Cinny🍰🎀

The flu?

At your age?

LMAO

Phainon

hyacinthia

don’t.

Cinny🍰🎀

Grown-ass man with the flu 🥹

Phainon

??

Cinny🍰🎀

It’s kind of cute it’s like

Aww you’re sick

Sick baby

UwU

Phainon

i think i’m in hell

Cinny🍰🎀

These aren’t gonna be paid btw

Phainon

yeah hyacine i know

Cinny🍰🎀

And you have to bring the paper to me in person eventually

But I’m gonna forward the photo to Anaxa and they’re gonna take care of it

I’m not at work today

Well, isn’t that just great.

Cinny🍰🎀

League? 🥺🥺

Let’s duoq

Let me carry you to master princess

Phainon

girl NO i’m sick i’m not playing league

Cinny🍰🎀

Killing you with my mind

Killing you with my mind

Killing you with my mind

Phainon just sends a gif of a bored and unimpressed monkey. Yeah, that’ll show her.

Mydei dials his building’s interphone a few hours later and at that point it’s just… Phainon’s immune system has lost this fight. He’s waving the white flag. It’s crazy how fast it hit him. He woke up with a sniffly nose and a sore throat, but now he’s fighting a 39°C fever and coughing up so much mucus that it’s becoming concerning.

Phainon has quite literally never been this sick before in his life. Still, he crawls out of bed and makes his way past the rug of discarded used tissues. He waits until Mydei is at the door before unlocking it and swinging it wide open, in a very “Well, here we are!” gesture.

He would find the surprised look on Mydei’s face priceless if he wasn’t so under the weather. His amber eyes widening a little, eyebrows shooting up, very cute.

“You look like shit.”

“Yeah,” Phainon croaks in response, and his sinuses are so stuffed up he sounds unrecognizable. He sounds like he’s on the verge of tears and like a snotty teenager at the same time.

“You really are sick.”

“What, you thought I was lying?”

“No,” Mydei says as he pushes past him, “I thought you were being dramatic.”

Bartholos waddles from the living room to say ‘hi’; he’s such a friendly young man, so proper and polite, truly like no cat Phainon has ever met. What kind of cat is friendly and likes strangers? Bartholos short little legs are trying very hard to make it to Mydei, and Mydei— He gasps and nearly drops the grocery bags he’s holding. Throws himself backwards and away from Bartholos, back hitting the little drawer he keeps in the hallway, with such force that Phainon hears his back cracking.

“No cats,” Mydei says, breathless, “Absolutely not.”

It is the most emotionally affected he’s seen him since they met. Truly scared, and of Bartholos at that. Phainon can’t help but be a little intrigued—but not enough to be cruel, never that. “Sorry,” he says, truly apologetic, “I should’ve put him away. Are you scared of cats?”

“Not scared, just… I don’t like them.”

The reaction is a little much for just not liking cats, but Phainon’s a bit too feverish right now to be a little shit. He picks up Bartholos, a herculean task in and of itself, and takes him to Cyrene’s room. He brings his essentials as well, water, FOOD, litter box, and when the cat is nice and settled in, Phainon leaves and closes the door behind. Bartholos quite likes it in Cyrene’s room, so he’s not worried about pissing the kitty off. He finds Mydei in the same position he left him, clutching the white plastic bags like his life depends on it.

“What are those for?” he says, nodding at the groceries.

“You sound like a squeaky toy,” comes Mydei’s intelligent answer.

“Okay. Not what I asked.”

Mydei cocks his pretty head a bit—he does that a lot, and Phainon loves it. Does the question make more sense at 45°, bud? Then, he does something that Phainon finds enrapturing; he turns to look down at the bags. A simple motion, yet he finds it entirely way too lovely nonetheless—his head twisting downwards, swaying with it the long locks of her, red as if dipped in blood. They caress the side of his neck, that elegant column, and Phainon is just feverish enough to feel jealousy over it. He could reach out, simply, and touch it for himself, feel Mydei's pulse point beating faster and faster. Would he blush prettily all down to his chest, just like he did that day in the gym? Just entertaining that thought feels too lewd. Heat is rising to Phainon's cheeks—he chalks it up to the fever.

A beautiful view is granted to him, one that he loves most dearly; Mydei's profile, regal and noble like an olden prince, his nose curving down as if yearning to reach his lips. Strong, handsome, manly. There's something erotic about its aquilinness, Phainon thinks, about his august brow, high and proud, curving into his nose like a wanton lover. He has a small bump there, on the highest peak of his bridge, and Phainon's been wanting to trace it with his tongue since the first day. This truly is the best view of Mydei, from the side, and he often finds himself stealing looks at work like a shy schoolgirl.

"These," Mydei's voice rings out through whatever fever-induced nasal fantasy Phainon is having, "Are for the soup."

"The soup?"

"The soup I'm gonna make you."

Mydei making him soup… Phainon really should get sick more often.

"Woah, you're making me soup… I should get sick more often."

Mydei is already moving past him and into the kitchen, yet still Phainon hears his scoff. "Idiot, why would you want to get sick more often? It's bad for your health."

Phainon peaks his head into the kitchen, watches as Mydei starts to unpack the groceries. Chicken, lemon, rice, eggs… Certainly not a soup that Phainon's ever had before.

"Well, if I get sick more often, you'd come over and make me soup."

"If you just want me to make you soup," Mydei points a threatening spatula at him, "You can just ask me. No need to get sick."

"That's very romantic of you, Mydei…"

"Go lay down in bed," Mydei commands, his brow furrowing, "And stop bothering me."

Yessir.

Back in bed he goes, feeling just more feverish that before—though when he goes to check his temperature, he finds it unmoved from the previous 39°C. Every sinus in his body is stuffed to the brim, face flushed hot as the fever ravages him, throat sore like nails on a chalkboard. Everything is too hot, too suffocating, and there's little to no relief when he peels his sweat-stained shirt off. Everything is a little wiggly, Phainon notices, but everything is always little wiggly. Sometimes it looks as if the floorboards are breathing underneath his feet like a great beast, Georios who gave their body to create the earth. Sometimes his wardrobe undulates as if stuck in perpetual chorea. The hallucinations seem to worsen as his body temperature rises. This is probably fine.

Phainon doesn't realize he dozes off until he's woken up by Mydei shaking him. Somehow he feels even worse, as if a great big weight is pressing down on his chest. His eyes hurt. He's tearing up, not crying yet still leaking tears. His nose… Yeah, it's fucked. It's mouthbreathing time. Mydei looks downright concerned.

"Have you… taken anything for this?"

"Yeah…" he mumbles, and weakly points at a small pile of meds on his nightstand, "Got some bullshit from the doctor."

There's softness in Mydei's eyes, a parental sort of worry, and Phainon would find that very cute if his brain wasn't cooking in his skull right now.

"Hold on… Hold this," is all Mydei says before he thrusts a bowl of soup into his hands. Phainon watches as he, quite rudely, starts ransacking through his drawers. Before he can ask what the fuck he's doing, Mydei triumphantly pulls out a pair of socks and—oh. Oh no.

"I'm not doing vinegar socks."

"You are doing vinegar socks."

"No."

"You are, quite frankly, powerless against vinegar socks. Vinegar socks are happening."

Grown-ass man with vinegar-soaked socks on. Okay. This must be a humiliation ritual at this point. Last time he got vinegar sock'd, he was eleven years old and running a fever high enough to kill a small goat.

He wishes he could fight back against this fate. Alas, with his limbs heavy as iron and a bowl of hot soup in his hands, Phainon is useless. A mere victim of destiny. He can only watch in horror as Mydei departs from the room, and returns with—yeah. Socks. Soaked in vinegar. And a wet towel.

He sits on the edge of the bed next to him, Phainon sitting up hunched and a little broken. "You can either put these socks on nicely," Mydei says, his voice measured, "Or we can do it the hard way."

Phainon can only offer up his feet in defeat. He winces as the damp, soggy socks are put on, and wriggles uncomfortably. This is hell, this is literally hell. Mydei presses the cold compress to his head.

"There. That will bring the fever down."

"I don't feel comfortable."

"That's too bad."

Phainon looks at the soup miserably. It's… a little creamy, and it smells good, and it looks nice and warm. It's better than the socks, that's for sure. "Is this supposed to help?"

"Yeah," he says, "Can you eat on your own?"

"Y…" and then Phainon considers his answer really hard, "No."

Mydei looks at him for a second, studying his face. He seems unconvinced. Here's a fun fact about him that Phainon likes very much; Mydei is the stoic, silent type. His preferred answers come in the form of "hmph" and "oh". His face hardly moves with emotion as he speaks. But, but—he has these nice thick eyebrows, several shades darker than his hair, nearly brown. And, at times, they carry the weight of Mydei's expressiveness in them. This is one such moment; his eyebrows twitch upward and then furrow a bit, creating wrinkles in-between that call for Phainon to smooth over with his thumb. He can practically see the gears turning in Mydei's head. Then, his face relaxes, eyes roll, and he sighs.

"Liar. But fine."

Success! Phainon leans back like a child emperor and opens his mouth. Gives him a big 'aaaah' just to be extra annoying. There is something akin to affection dancing in Mydei's features, something fond as he grabs the bowl and the spoon. He scoops up a good nice bite, lots of chicken and lots of rice.

"Hold on, wait, can you do like, 'here comes the airplane'?"

Mydei blanks at him. Blinks once.

"No, I can't do that."

"Please? Pleaseee!"

Mydei's mouth twists a little. His cheeks flush with dusting of pink.

"Here… comes the airplane…"

Phainon's life can be so good sometimes. The soup is like creamy, lemony broth straight to his tummy. A pleasant blend of tastes, neither too overwhelming, and it's nice and hearty. His do sinuses clear up a bit.

It goes on like that for a while. Silently, Phainon sinking more and more into the mattress, full of soup and content. Mydei watches him closely as he feeds him—he has this habit of just staring at people, his gaze intense and profound, and Phainon finds that he crumbles easily under it. It cracks open a strange sort of vulnerability in him, as though Mydei can see right through him and straight into his black little heart. Phainon's movements become slow and he's lulled half to sleep from it. It's a tender thing to do, feeding someone like this. One spoonful at a time, waiting patiently for the other to chew and swallow. Phainon's mouth goes slack after every bite, falling open obediently, waiting for more. Mydei is gentle with it. Mydei is always gentle. He has these beautiful hands; Phainon knows them to be soft to the touch. At one point, he grabs Mydei's wrist—not hard, not for any particular reason, but just for the sake of it. Maybe to anchor himself a little bit.

This is nice. It feels good. An odd sort of sleepy fuzz. Mydei tells him the soup is all done and Phainon just hums. Moves his hand to grab onto his thumb. His face and chin is wiped with a towel, and suddenly he finds his eyelids very heavy.

"Mydei…" he grumbles, "Are you going to stay?"

"Hmm… Yes, I think so."

"I'm really tired."

"Let me change your socks and you can nap."

Phainon's already asleep by the time his socks get changed, snoring blissfully and breathing through his mouth. He doesn't feel the way Mydei rubs his thumb, lovingly, over his ankle.

He wakes up two, maybe three hours later, and he's burning up. The first thing he does is go into a coughing fit that makes his entire sternum ache and pulse. He spits out a phlegm into one of his bedside napkins. The second thing he does is call for Mydei, because he's not here. With his voice raspy and weak, he can barely hear it over the sound of the ringing in his ears.

Mydei comes. He always comes when he is called. He peeks his pretty head into the door, cocking it a bit. "You're awake?"

"What were you doing…"

The thought of Mydei having free reign over his home, his personal belongings, ought to make Phainon anxious. It doesn't, though.

"I was letting the cat out. I felt bad for the little guy, locked up in a room all day."

"Ah… I'm not… I don't feel well… I'm hot all over…" is all Phainon can manage, collapsing back into the sheets, face buried in the pillows.

"Poor thing…" he hears Mydei coo, and such words would ravage him if the fever wasn't doing so all ready. He hears —feels— Mydei come up next to his bed. "Tch. You've soaked the bedsheets."

"Huh…?"

"You sweat buckets while sleeping," Mydei clarifies and, yes, now that Phainon's thinking about it, his whole bed is damp and wet like a swamp. It's uncomfortable all of a sudden. He rolls over on his back, trying to find a dry spot on the bed. His eyes immediately search for Mydei, finding comfort when they of his frame; wide, broad, strong, beautiful still. It's becoming a bad habit, Phainon thinks as his brain is getting cooked inside his skull, to drink from a sweet well that does not belong to you. He could cry at the sight of him. It's all a bit too intense for knowing the guy for less than two months, but Phainon is nothing but intense. Without his consent, one of his arms stretches forward, reaches towards Mydei as if he could catch him in the palm of his hand and keep him in his pocket. Inexplicably, bafflingly, Mydei reaches back for him. Holds his hand for a moment. "Jesus, Phainon," he says, "You're burning up. You should take a shower."

Phainon laughs, weakly. His hair is wet and stuck on his forehead—Mydei brushes it aside. "Your fever's gotten worse."

"I feel worse."

"A lukewarm shower will help lower your temperature."

"Don't wanna…"

"You have to."

"Mmnooo…"

Mydei huffs like an exasperated mother. Puts his hands on his hips. "Come on, Phainon. Shower."

"I'll take a shower if you wash me."

Mydei tenses up. Rips his hand back, away from Phainon. He takes one, two, three steps back. "Why."

It's not a question—it sounds more like an accusation. Phainon doesn't understand.

"I… sorry? I thought it would be… Fun, or something. And I'm feeling pretty, uh, weak, I guess? Like actually."

Mydei crosses his arms. There's something sharp, dangerous in his eyes; it's beautiful. Phainon wants to cut himself on it.

"Are you going to do something weird?"

"Weird…? I don't understand. Like what?"

Phainon's feverish mind is trying to conjure up what 'weird' things he might to do Mydei in the bath. Maybe splash him…? Or… He could suddenly get nauseous and puke?

"Something weird."

"I don't—"

"To me."

He opens his mouth to respond, but the flu takes this moment to grip him tight and make him cough. It scratches up his throat and leaves him dry-heaving for a second. When he turns back at Mydei, his face has softened. But just a little bit.

"I really don't understand, Mydei. Can you be a bit clearer?"

"If I get in with you, are you going to…" Mydei measures his words. Seems to look for the right ones. "Touch me?"

"I mean," he answers after he blows his nose, "I totally planned on splashing you."

Mydei grows restless with his answers. Phainon can tell that he still hasn't answered the question, but truly, he's doing his best. This is all he can manage through the fever.

"I'm worried you're asking me to go to into the bath together so you can take advantage of me. Sexually."

Oh. Phainon doesn't even know what to say to him. That hasn't even crossed his mind. There's something tight coiling in his chest. Something sad. Something that makes him want to sob—he doesn't even know what to call it.

"Why… why would I do that?"

"Because you know I would let you."

"I… don't know that, actually, and I don't want to—I would never—I'm not that kind of person."

"I know."

"I've never done that to you before, I mean, I don't think—Oh God, have I?"

"No."

"Then what's this, all of a sudden?" Phainon sits up from the bed. His whole chest hurts. Mydei shifts his weight from one foot to the other.

"I don't know," he says, "I haven't been feeling well. I'm concerned, I guess."

"I've asked. In the gym. You said 'do whatever you want'. Why did you say it like that?"

Mydei hums thoughtfully. "Well, I said it like that to be a dick, but I did mean yes."

"Can you please just say yes or no from now on?"

"…Yeah. Okay. I will."

And then that's that. The conversation dies and silence falls over them, yet Phainon feels himself burn hotter still. Burn with shame, burn with anxiety. He can't bear it. He puts his face in his palms, hands gripping at his hair.

"I'm not—I don't—I don't want to do weird things to you, Mydei. The thought doesn't make me… happy. It's only fun if you're also into it. Like yesterday, it was—it was a lot of fun. I had a lot of fun. Was it fun for you?"

Mydei laughs a little, a bit forced, a bit embarrassed. The blush on his cheeks is gorgeous. "Yeah, I—yeah, it was fun."

Phainon both itches to reach out for him and aches to step away. Like a cornered animal, he's not sure what to do. He's not sure what Mydei wants him to do.

"I'm not going to like… force you or…" The Word is stuck in Phainon's throat. Impossibly heavy, though he's never had issue with it before. He can feel it fight its way out of his clenched teeth. "I'm not going to rape you."

Mydei inhales sharply as that, as if it physically hurts. As if the word is a brand he has to wear, aching incessantly, rotting. The sound of it is pain. Phainon wants to throw up—he can see Mydei's eyes glaze over. He makes a little 'oh' sound as he bumps into the wall; Mydei's been backing up, he's just realized.

Horrifyingly, Phainon realizes that he can't stop talking. "I don't want to hurt you. I don't want to hurt anyone. I want to be good. I keep hurting people but not—not like that. I'm not— perfect, fuck, I'm far from it, but I would never—I've never—I don't want to do that."

Even more horrifyingly, Phainon realizes that he's not above begging. "Please believe me."

Mydei's trying to hide how heavily he's breathing, but Phainon can tell by the quick rise and fall of his chest. He's grinding his teeth, too. Hard.

"If I did?"

"I'd stop."

"…Okay."

"Yeah," Phainon says, feeling impossibly exhausted.

A beat of silence.

"And if you get mad?" comes another one of Mydei's questions.

"…Why would I get mad?"

"Let's say we're having sex," he says, articulating with his hands, "And I tell you to stop. Wouldn't you get mad?"

Phainon is speechless. "N…no? I don't understand what's there to be mad about."

Mydei is equally speechless. "So we're having sex—"

"No, I got that part."

"And I say, oh I don't want to do this anymore. All of a sudden."

"Right."

Mydei only prompts him to answer with a gesture of his hands. As if he's just asked a very hard question.

"I'd just be like 'okay' and then stop."

Phainon can practically see the question marks popping up in Mydei's head. "You wouldn't get mad?"

"No, because like, that's a stupid thing to get mad about."

"A stupid thing to get mad about…" he echoes, thoughtfully, as if Phainon just told him the answer to 'what's the meaning of life?'

"I'd be like, worried. And I'd ask, oh, what didn't you like? Or ask if something is wrong."

"Right…"

"But like… I'm gonna be honest… Getting my dick wet isn't really that big of a deal? Like it's meant to be, you know, fun. Both of us. Having fun. Together."

"At the same time."

"Yeah," Phainon affirms, "At the same time."

Mydei… couldn't look more miserable if he tried. He is trying to hide it, but he can't hide the worried frown in his brows. Always those pesky eyebrows, being fatally honest, giving Phainon a hook to hang onto. He watches his fingers as they flex and clench onto the meat of his bicep where his arms are crossed. He's worried—you can't prove a negative. Phainon feels both drunk on the sickness and painfully sober on the reality of what they're talking about.

"I, uh, like years ago, right? I was having sex with this guy, and he straight up looked back at me in the middle of it and said 'you're fucking terrible at this, I want to stop'. So, uh, yeah. Not my first rodeo."

A cute attempt at breaking the tension. He hopes it lands. It has to land.

It's mesmerizing —downright intoxicating— to watch Mydei shift moods. Poor guy's been gripping himself so hard he's left red prints all over, so when he finally lets go of his biceps, it's Phainon that feels relief. His eyebrows twitch upward, first in surprise and then in amusement. His upper lip curls first when he smiles, showing a bit of teeth, letting Phainon gaze upon his sharp snaggletooth. His golden eyes crinkle, molten gold flowing into cute crow's feet and then, finally as if breaking through bondage, as if allowing himself this— Mydei laughs.

It's a beautiful tone, noble even, and it takes some weight off of his shoulders—weight that he didn't realize he was carrying. Phainon, then, allows himself to laugh as well. He could cry.

That stops Phainon dead in his tracks.

"Huh?"

Mydei opens the door to the bathroom and it's like, fine, he's not going to comment on the guy's body because he's just a guy and it's just a body. It's nothing special. I mean, it's quite literally cut from marble, every muscle fitting against each other like Mnestia-woven puzzle pieces, every muscle flexing with every move. His obliques are insane. Deep grooves on his ribcage, expanding ever-so-slightly with every breath, inviting Phainon to trace them with his tongue.

Mydei is leaner than Phainon is, his muscles more defined— Phainon, well, he's gained some weight lately. By all means, however, he's still a certified grade A hunk, both bigger and stronger than most men, there's just… Some fluff as well. Mostly on his stomach, and he thinks it looks quite charming so he doesn't want to work it off. Mydei, on the other hand—the split image of Nikador.

Phainon's legs are still bigger though so hah, take that!

Mydei gets into the bathtub with him, one leg after the other, and he stands looming above Phainon with his arms crossed. Phainon has, quite literally, never been this giddy before in his life.

"Two things," Mydei says, voice leaving nothing to be question. Authoritative.

"Mhmm?"

"One," and he raises a finger, "Water's gonna be lukewarm. A little cold."

"Mhmmmm."

"Two," and he raises a second finger, "You'll be good and you'll behave. No splashing."

"Yessir!"

Phainon can be good. Phainon will be so good.

Mydei turns on the water and checks the temperature. He keeps turning the 'cold' knob around until he seems satisfied.

The water is a bit too cold for Phainon's liking—he prefers boiling hot showers. Still, though, it's comforting. He feels downright pampered, like a spoiled baby or one of those vegetables at the store getting misted. Ah… Cabbagenon. Celerynon, perhaps.

When Mydei crouches down to wash his legs, Phainon smiles. Laughs.

"What?"

Phainon's heartbeats pick up at that; oddly enough, he starts feeling overwhelmingly guilty. "Why did he say that?" he asks, as though Jesus' words were directed at him. "Why'd he say it like that?"

Mydei's eyebrow cocks, but he does not look up to meet his gaze. "He knew one of them was going to betray him."

He can't help himself—Phainon bursts out laughing. Hard. It takes him by surprise because fuck, that's really funny but also Mydei is being so earnest right now. He covers his mouth and tries to stifle his laughter. "Sorry, no—I don't mean to laugh, it's just—That's unique."

A beat of silence. Heavy.

"Ah…" Phainon, all of a sudden very shy, speaks up. "I was wondering… If I were Judas and you were Jesus, would you forgive me?"

Why is he having a mini-panic attack over this? He feels awful. He feels guilty. What if he betrayed Mydei and got him killed? He would never do that, but what if he did?

Ah.

It's ringing in his ears now, real, and he wonders when all of this will stop. The dreams. The hallucinations. This searing pain. His chest burns, both with the flu and with the weight of his sins. His fingernails dig into his palms, and he's trying to keep his breathing very steady, and —

"Yeah," Mydei says, and a second might have passed, or an eternity, "Sure, I would."

"Why not?"

"Well, if I'm Judas and you're Jesus, and I betray you, then that means I kill you."

He wants to say something else, but Mydei hums instead, a bit sing-song—

He leans in and places a soft, delicate kiss on his knee. Tucks a strand of hair that got wet behind his ear as he does so. Beautiful thick eyelashes brushing against his cheek, fluttering close like butterfly wings.

Phainon could really cry. Awe-struck, scraped raw inside, he thanks Gods he does not know the name of for his failed suicide attempt. Blessed with things he does not deserve, beautiful and tender things, things that Mydei keeps putting in his arms—things that he cannot hold.

It quiets, a bit. The beating of his heart, and the trombones too. He reaches out with both hands, headed for Mydei's broad shoulders, and stops just short of touching them; Mydei sucks in a little sharp breath. Flinches.

Mydei chews on his bottom lip. "…No," he says quietly, as if the word can shatter whatever there is between them, "Not right now."

"Okay, that's fine."

His hands come back to rest on his thighs, well-behaved, yet Mydei's lips linger on his kneecap still; a second too long, long enough to hurt. He's too sensitive to the touch, skin too frail and now tender too, from the wash. He feels the kiss like knives; delicious and delirious, he wants more, he wants everything, he wants nothing else. He wants to touch the crown of Mydei's head.

He does not.

"I don't want to," Phainon gasps out, quickly, "I want to take a bath. An actual bath."

Mydei takes back the stool to the kitchen, commanding him to stay still and prepare the damned bath. When a beautiful man tells him to do something, well, Phainon obeys.

They don't set any rules for their competition, so Phainon and Mydei just… end up staring at each other in silence for ten or so minutes. Both of them very much blinking, which does go against the typical rules for a staring contest. It's not about the competition, though, is the thing. Phainon just wants to look at him. He does.
