They walk back home hand in hand, and in silence.

It was beautiful, too beautiful. The night sky above them, painted with shining dots of light, seems as though drawn by the hand of an impressionist; blurry and unconceivable, romantic, yes, but ultimately not real. When they look up at that dark blue welkin, they both find it entirely too starry considering Okhema's air pollution levels. 'Must be a trick of the eye', one of them thinks, though it is impossible to tell who.

The realization of what just happened sets into their backs like spears. It sits on the precipice of too much and too little, which is shaping up to be the central theme of their life; longing for something too out of reach, breaking your legs to get it and, when it is finally in the palm of your hands, discarding it and running far away. It's a clever little paradox, and if there were still philosophers worth their name around, they might enjoy debating over this night. However, with no philosophers around, they are left fearful like two children wading through the dark, blind and seeing only with their hands.

Even so, hands are still held, tightly grasped between sweaty fingers. Once in a while, on their short trek home that now seems to span thousands of miles, one will throw the other a shy little look; the other while catch it and return it, and they will both smile and flush. If they are to fall, well, they might as well fall together—their grip on each other tightens, only a little bit.

Woe, two unlovable creatures, the chorus sang as such, and behold, how lovely they still are.

"I was thinking, uh," Phainon says as he opens the door, "What would you like me to call you?"

Mydei cocks his head and frowns. Phainon's been calling him correctly just fine until now? "Uh, you can call me Mydei, or Mydeimos."

"No, no, I mean—" Phainon takes off his jacket and hangs it, "I mean like, now that we're, erm… Together… What would you like me to call you? My boyfriend? My partner?"

He considers it—boyfriend is good enough, but it's wholly unromantic and has no drama or tragedy to it—Mydei has a bachelor's in Classics and has studied ancient history at length, so what's the point if there's no blood and sweat and open wounds? He's been called boyfriend by all of his exes, and look how that turned out. Partner is downright egregious. It's sanitized and unaffectionate; what, are they doing business together?

Mydei mulls it over in his head, and makes a show out of "hmmmm"ing and rubbing his chin. Just to be a dick.

"Well—" he starts, and Phainon perks up, "You can call me boyfriend when we're around others, but when we're alone, Phainon…"

—And Mydei presses very close to him, close enough to feel the breath escaping from him, trapping him against his body and the wall. Phainon gasps in surprise, a soft and darling sound, mouth opening almost as if by instinct. His eyes glaze over instantly, the heat rises to his cheeks, and in the blink of an eye, he's lovely-red like a ripe apple.

Mydei knows he's beautiful, that much he's certain of; it's kind of impossible to not be aware of it, not when a two thousand year old statue of Nikador is the fitness goal he's been working towards for most of his adult life. Point is, Mydei knows how to use it to his advantage, and bullying Phainon is a constitutional right of his; so he does what he knows works very well. Mydei bats his eyelashes and tilts his chin down, gazing up at his through his lashes with that smoldering golden look of his, and he rises his shoulder coyly just a little bit. If he could blush on command he would—alas, this will have to do.

"Phainon…" he says, low in his throat, wringing his braid around his finger, "When we are alone, I would very much like it if you called me your lover."

His prize for this performance is as such; Phainon whimpering and blushing an even deeper shade of red, his mouth pursing and twisting, his eyes getting all big and crazy. Mydei can practically see him go cross-eyed and see the steam coming out of his ears. Phainon shoves his hands in his pocket and looks away for a moment.

"L—yeah, man, yeah, sure, that's cool, whatever, I'll do whatever y—Yeah no, yeah like no yeah, for sure, anything you want—Lover? Yeah, that's cool, I like—I like that."

Delightful. Mydei laughs and shoves his shoulder—Phainon just pouts. "Asshole, you're fucking with me!" He shoves Mydei back, and it makes him laugh harder.

They're standing in the hallway and their shoes at still on. Mydei feels impossibly warm on this October night. He tilts his head. "I am serious, though. I'd like if you called me lover. I think it's very romantic."

Phainon huffs a small breath. An incredulous laugh. "You sound like Cyrene sometimes. She liked stuff like that."

His eyes widen a bit—it's the first time he's really talked about her. "What stuff?"

"Romance and…" Phainon gestures vaguely, "Kind, beautiful things. When she was younger, she—Ah, nevermind."

"No," Mydei steps towards him, "I'd like to know."

"She would write a lot when she was young. Lots of fairytales and poems. They were beautiful, but she stopped one day."

"Why?"

"I don't know," he shrugs, "It was a gradual thing. She wanted to go to college for literature, but then decided to go into finance instead. Maybe she thought a future in writing wasn't possible? Then she started saying it's a silly thing for kids. She wanted to be a model for a while, though. She was very beautiful, but she had a hard time, I guess, because she was uhh… too old."

Mydei frowns. "How old was she?"

"Two years older than me."

"That's fucked up. She wasn't even thirty."

"No," Phainon sighs, "And she never will be. But she had a love for fashion and clothes and pretty pink things. She said she wanted a big platform so she could do some good things in the world. Have a bigger reach. She was a very popular girl, kind of a small-time influencer. She'd have these flights of fancy sometimes, about a life out of a fairytale, where money was never an issue. She'd talk about stained glass windows in the kitchen and a great big garden of flowers," he looks away, "I don't think she liked finance very much, though I don't know why she didn't just go back into writing. Nor do I know where this model thing came from. She was always a contradiction," he clicks his tongue, "I should've mentioned it to Aglaea, fuck. She would've loved to have a girl like Cyrene at her family's fashion house."

"I don't know her, but somehow…" Mydei tilts his head, "I don't think she would've liked that."

"Ha! No, she wouldn't have, I think. She wanted to be self-made and she was stubborn like a bull."

"Ah, so it runs in the family."

"What? I'm not stubborn at all!"

Mydei laughs, "You are, sometimes."

Phainon doesn't reply, instead grabs his hand, shy, and pulls him into the living room. He settles into the couch and pats the space next to him—naturally, Mydei takes it.

"So, I was thinking—"

"You've been thinking a lot today," Mydei grins, shit-eating, and it makes Phainon groan.

"Yeah, man, it's been a long day and a lot happened. We have some kinks to iron out."

He cocks an eyebrow, inquisitive, and gestures for Phainon to continue.

"So, right, you're my boyfriend when we're with others, and my l… Uh, my lover when we're alone," Mydei can't help but smirk at how flustered Phainon is, "But, what about pet names? Are you into those?"

This does stump him a little bit. Is he? He's always found them terribly romantic, ever since he first got his hands on his mom's bodice-rippers when he was ten, but… He's never liked it when his previous boyfriends called him 'babe' or 'baby'. It always made his skin crawl, like they were trying to forcefully bully their way under it. It was too close and impersonal at the same time. Like a bad play he was forced to be the face of. Frankly, it was just a little bit gross. Bland and fake. He likes a certain type of pet names, but they are embarrassing.

Phainon, though… he does seem like a 'baby' type, but also a 'beloved' type. A 'my love' type or a 'sweetheart' type. He blinks at him. Phainon blinks back and is seemingly starting to get embarrassed at Mydei's silence—he opens his mouth to backtrack, so Mydei has to speak up before Phainon spooks.

"I like pet names," he says, not sure how true that is, "We can do pet names."

"Oh, that's great!" Relief is evident on Phainon's face. "I was thinking—"

"The thinker…"

"Shut up. I was thinking we can each take like five minutes and write down some pet names we like being called? And we can read it to each other and like… Talk about it."

Mydei shrugs. "Okay. That sounds good."

"Yeah?"

"Mhm. Yeah."

They spend the next five minutes typing away on their phones. Mydei spots Phainon stopping to wipe the sweat from his brow at least twice, which is just crazy because these are just pet names.

"I'm done," he announces when the time is up—five minutes on the clock. He counted.

Phainon looks up at him. "Okay, nice. I'll start. Um, I like dear a lot. Like just dear or my dear. Your turn."

"I like dear too."

"You have to say another one, dude, those are the rules!"

Mydei scoffs. "Rules. Fine. I like darling."

"That's in the same vein as dear, though."

"No, it's not."

"Yes, it is."

"It's not and that's final. Your turn."

"Whatever. Uhh… I like honey."

"Honey? What, are you a husband from the fifties?" Mydei teases, and Phainon huffs incredulously at it.

"Dude, don't make fun of me, we're being vulnerable."

"Hm, are we?" Mydei cocks his head and gives him that smile he knows absolutely disarms him. A little sharp and wolfish and hungry. Phainon like his snaggleteeth so he puts them on full display. His lion's fangs, Hephaestion calls them. Phainon loses his breath so fast it's almost funny; he is so easy to blush, too, and he turns pretty pink all the way down to his chest. It's past midnight now, so not his birthday anymore—this means Mydei can tease him all he wants. He reaches his hand over and delights in the way Phainon searches his touch, already looking to nuzzle his cheek into his palm. Mydei denies him the satisfaction, and instead swipes his thumb across his sweaty forehead. He brings it to his lips and gives it a lick.

It's sweaty and disgusting, but the look on Phainon's face is worth it. Lips parted, cheeks flushed, eyes wide and pupils blown; he looks absolutely ruined.

"What the fuck is wrong with you?" Phainon's voice is raw as if he's thrown it apart. Mydei laughs at him. "That's yucky!" he continues, and Mydei laughs at him harder. "Let's just go back to the pet names please. It's your turn."

"Right," Mydei looks down at his phone, "I do like honey by the way. It's sweet. Ah, there, I also like sweetling."

"Sweetling…" Phainon echoes, "Okay. I like love and my love."

"Heart."

"Pet."

"The Lance of Fury."

Phainon sputters. "What?"

Mydei keeps reading. "The Sovereign of All Battles. Grand Artisan of the War Chariot. General that all the world shall heed. The Eternal Sharp Sword. The Law of Strife. Greatest of Conquerors, Greatest of Guardians, The Strong—"

Phainon does not laugh. Instead, he just stares blankly at Mydei, and then shoves him. "Take this seriously." he whines.

"I am." Mydei shoves back, and then it becomes a whole thing—next thing he knows, he's got Phainon pinned to the couch, arm on his throat. Phainon chokes and waves his hand around. "I yield, I yield!"

Mydei lets him go with a triumphant laugh.

"In all seriousness though," he says, "I like the names you picked. You've got good taste." Phainon grumbles stubbornly at that. "I also like personalized pet names. And you can also call me 'dude'. And Mydei, obviously, you are also allowed to call me that."

Phainon shifts a bit where he is sitting and he simply watches Mydei. Eyes a little heavy-linden, lips a little pouty. He rests his cheek on the backrest of the couch, and blinks slowly.

He looks tired, very tired. He looks sad, and a little in love too.

"What's wrong?" Mydei asks, dropping his voice to a whispers.

Phainon sighs. "I'm just worried, y'know. About… us, I guess. About… I don't know. What if I'm not ready for a relationship? I'm kind of a fuck up, I have a dead end job and shitton of debt and I really don't feel like I have much of a future, and like, my mental health is bad—"

"Phainon," Mydei stops him, "I'm not letting you spiral on the first day of our relationship. Look…"

Mydei leans to him, brings his arm to the side of his neck and rests it right over his sun tattoo. Phainon immediately melts into the touch, as if he has been waiting for it the entire night— and how cruel Mydei is to leave his lover to wait so long for a caress! With his thumb, he traces the rays of the sun. His darling boy. Mydei is impossibly fond, and impossibly scared.

He shifts and moves on the couch, closer and close to Phainon until Mydei is sitting on his knees next to him, draped over him, holding his face and forcing him to look up. His long hair falls around their faces like a curtain, making this intimate, making this safe. It is just the two of them; it has always been, perhaps.

"We're only dating, we're not getting married or anything, so you don't have to worry about your job or your debt. It's fine, you'll pay it off one day," Mydei says to him, voice hushed as though it were a secret. "I knew all of these things when I said yes to dating you, so clearly they aren't a deterrent, if that's what you're worried about."

He bends down, touching the tips of their noses together. He feels Phainon's hand on his waist. "I have many reasons to like you. I even like you when you're unwell… I especially like you then, I think, because that's the only time you've been honest with me. Phainon, we can be fuck-ups together."

"Together…" Phainon repeats dumbly, and Mydei closes the distance between them.

He kisses Phainon's cheek and his eyelids, the bridge of his nose and his forehead. He kisses him all over his handsome face until he is breathless and giggling and red in the face.

"You worry as well?" Phainon asks, arms now wrapped around Mydei's middle.

"Yeah. I'm worried you'll find me unbearable or… too much. I'm worried that you'll hurt me."

Phainon doesn't answer, nor does he have to. Mydei gives him one last kiss, on the tip of his nose.

They break apart after that. Phainon goes to change the sheets, and Mydei goes to take a shower. He's still toweling his hair dry when he returns to the bedroom, and he sees Phainon in a staring match with his Simba plushie.

"Hey," he calls out, "Leave Simba alone."

Phainon grumbles unhappily.

"What, are you jealous of him?" Mydei grins, and Phainon just puts the little lion away.

After Mydei changes into clean sweatpants, he crawls under the sheets with Phainon. It's toasty and comfortable and they just look at each other for a while. Bartholos scratches at the door, unhappy with being left out, but Mydei cannot—he cannot bear to be around him, still.

Phainon breaks the silence.

"Mydei, I've been wondering, um… If we don't kiss, then what do we do? As a couple?"

—And whatever they have, shatters.

Mydei sits up and pushes the covers aside. Jolts of shame hit him like lightning strikes, quick and electric and spreading through him from his chest to his extremities. A familiar feeling bludgeons him over the head. Shame. He has known it well. Been spoonfed it as a child but never understood its taste until he was twenty-two. His body is suddenly two sizes too small, too little to house whatever immensity is threaten to burst like a boil out of his stomach. In an instant, he is gone. His eyes glaze over and his tongue is thick in his mouth. It all feels hazy all of a sudden, like a terrible dream. When he looks at Phainon, he sees static.

"Mydei? I'm sorry, did I—"

"Uh…" Mydei manages, and sounds are acrid in his mouth. He understands the telltale signs of shutting down, and it makes him all the more ashamed. He wants to kiss Phainon, of course he does. Phainon is nice, sweet, funny and a little stupid. Phainon wouldn't take it too far, he never does. Phainon is good and gentle and not a rapist, and here is the point of tension: he wants to kiss him so badly, needs to kiss him like a hungry wolf needs a lamb. He wants to desperately, selfishly, but he cannot. The disconnect is too strong. His nervous system does not match up with his brain does not match up with his heart. He is in a cave, looking at the shadows on the wall, pretending it is love.

Phainon's hand comes to touch his bare shoulder and Mydei slaps it away. The sad little look on his face is enough to break his heart, poor Phainon, his Phainon. Bartholos scratches louder at the door, and the sound becomes unbearable.

"Make it stop," he tells him, but he does not recognize his own voice, "Make it stop!"

The bed creaks when Phainon gets off of it. He distantly hears him lead Bartholos to his food bowl and pour some kibble in.

God, he's broken. He's wrong, all wrong. Mydei looks down at his hands and finds himself unable to count his own fingers. He's going to have a panic attack. He tries to name five things he can see but truly, the only thing he can see right now is that twisted face, dry and cracked as though carved into the bark of an old tree, sweating and gritting its teeth above him.

Kissing—it's just kissing and God, he'd really like to do it too. Would like to wake up like any normal man every morning and not have to take a handful of pills, all carefully picked to make sure he doesn't keel over and die, and lean over to kiss a sleepy Phainon. He would like to push him against a wall and kiss him deep and nasty and, yes, he would also like to kiss him while riding him stupid. All those thoughts disgust him. Desire disgusts him. Why does he feel guilty? It was never his fault.

Why is Mydei unable to live while he is out there somewhere, all happy and none the wiser?

Phainon returns and stands in the doorway.

In this lightless night, he looks menacing. Mydei suddenly wonders if he could take him down if Phainon tried to lounge at him—the answer is yes, but he could've taken him down back then too, and he didn't.

"Look, Mydei, I'm sorry. That came out wrong, I didn't mean to, uh…" he steps inside and Mydei startles. He steps back. "I didn't mean to sound like it's an accusation or something? I mean like, you know, were a couple, and I thought we should do couple things, you know? I really worded it badly, I mean, you know, we're lovers now, so I thought some things would… change."

Do they have to? Why do things have to change? Is what they have not good enough?

"No, no, it is. I love what we have now. I'm not disappointed or anything, I mean, I do want to kiss you, but it's alright if I don't, really I just like being around you, um, it's just—Look, I'm sorry I asked. I didn't mean to make you feel ba—"

He was kissing him back then and Mydei could feel his sweat on his lips. The tongue in his mouth was a terrible dragon—

"Stop, no, you don't have to tell me. Sorry, I understand, but please don't tell me any more. I can tell it's making you very upset. Listen, I can drive you home, do you want to go home?"

Home? His mother died in his home. He kept a piece of her scalp. It was by the oven. When he was giving his testimony everybody was looking at him. He doesn't want to go home. That's where he killed that small orange cat.

"What?"

His roommates are home. Peucesta said his boyfriend is coming over. That's too many people in one home.

"Do you need to, uh, be alone?"

He needs to be put down.

"Mydei, don't… don't say that. Do you need me to call someone? An ambulance?"

No. They'll institutionalize him again.

"Then, uh… I'll just, I'll sleep in Cyrene's room, okay? And you can sleep here."

He cannot be alone but he cannot be around people either but he does not want to be alone. He wants to be able to be so full of people that his skin can't quite fit all the love they give him. But he cannot be alone. And he cannot be around people. But he wants to be—alone. And around people.

"I'll… just let Bartholos in and I'll sleep in Reney's room. That way you won't be alone, but you won't be around, uh, people either."

He'll kill him.

"You won't. You won't even notice him, he's so good. He'll sleep by your feet, okay?"

Okay.

Phainon calls over the cat and Mydei kind of hears his small feet tapping on the floor. A weight jumps up and settles on the mattress by his feet. Phainon smiles at him, a little awkward, and comes in to grab his phone.

He's ruined it.

"You haven't," Phainon looks at him, "You haven't. I'm concerned for you, that's all, dear. But I'm still very happy. And I'm very excited."

Mydei does not say anything else—has he been talking?—and Phainon leaves the room. He does not close the door on his way out.

He sits there for a while, blanket pooled at his waist, looking at the door with his mouth agape. He hears Phainon watching TikToks in the other room. Every once in a while, his phone pings a new message. Phainon's sent him a link.

He thinks it must be hours before he lays back down on his heavy back and tries to sleep. Bartholos is purring at his feet and he dislikes the sound, but he does not try to kill him, either. He reaches over and grabs Simba. Pulls him tight to his chest.

In his dream that night, Mydei is wandering the halls of his childhood home and he is naked. It is morning and the wooden floor of his living room is stained with blood. Light bathes him from every window, of which there is one on every wall. On the floor, there is a small, shiny black spike. He watches it with curiosity. He cannot tell what it is.

It rattles and stands up. Grows larger until it is much bigger that Mydeimos. He looks up at it. He is scared but he does not run. He is frozen. The spike breaks off into a hundred shards, sharp like onyx arrowheads. They are spear-tall and obelisk-thick and they try to force their way inside his mouth but he clenches his jaw and grits his teeth. It does not matter. They hit him and stab him until they break his teeth and they rattle like fractured pearls. Blood comes like a waterfall, and then they are down his throat and in his stomach, and they groove and sway and squirm inside him, poking him in all his bits, shaping him and deforming him while he is writhing on the floor. He does not scream nor does he try to claw at them. It is futile. They are already inside. When they settle, the pain dulls, but he knows they are still there and he knows he will have to carry them.

Phainon finds Mydei the next morning naked and standing to look out the window of his bedroom. The sight shocks him at first. Mydei's naked back, his buttocks, his strong thighs, bare for him to see. He averts his gaze.

"Mydei?" he calls, but Mydei does not answer him, does not flinch at all.

"Mydei," he tries again, and now he stirs. He turns his head to look at him out of the corner of his eye.

"Sorry. It was too warm when I woke up."

The house is freezing. The district mayor hasn't turned on the heating yet. Phainon spares a look at his face. He hasn't cried, but he looks exhausted and red-eyed nonetheless. He takes a careful step inside.

"No, it's okay, don't worry. I wanted to apologize for yesterday. For the way I asked you that question."

Mydei scoffs weakly. "I forgive you."

Mydei moves, and Phainon looks down at the floor. He sits down on the edge of the mattress and covers his lap with the blanket. Stillness for a moment, and then Mydei beckons him closer—Phainon, bewitched, follows like a bloodhound hot on a trail. He stands in front of him, looking down at him, and Mydei sits, looking up at him. His face is not tumultuous, but it is not peaceful either. It's more something like tired, if Phainon had to give it a name. He clenches and unclenches his fists. Shifts his weight from one foot to the other.

"Are we still together?" he asks, barely loud enough to drown out the birds chirping outside.

Mydei laughs at that, full-mouthed and full-teethed. "Yes," he says, "I don't see why not."

His laughter lingers into a smile. Both of his snaggleteeth are peeking over his lips, like vampire fangs. Phainon is filled with such unshakeable affection. "You have a scar on your back, did you know?" he teases.

Mydei doesn't dignify him with a look. "Do I, haikas? I had no idea! Thank God you told me!"

Phainon laughs and leans down to bite his earlobe; that always makes him good and pliant. Mydei huffs at him in exasperation, but he does not pull away.

"Where'd you get it?"

"Scoliosis," Mydei answers curtly, "Had it as a kid, got the surgery as a teenager. I don't recommend it. It's why my back keeps fucking hurting."

Phainon hums in acknowledgement. He cranes his neck to get a better look at it. It is beautiful, in a way, but he finds everything about Mydei beautiful. Pale like a snake in the grass, hiding between the curves and lines of Mydei's tattoos.

His back is beautiful. Broad and strong like an oxen, perfectly muscled, a woven tapestry. He loves his back. He loves everything about him, but his back most of all.

"Can I?" Phainon asks, putting his thumb on the tip of the scar.

"Go ahead," Mydei answers, shifting to give him better access.

He runs his thumb across the length of it, from his shoulder blades down to where his back dips down with his waist and hips, and stops at his tailbone. He burns the oddly smooth feeling of it to memory. Mydei hums when he touches him.

"Is it sensitive?" Phainon whispers.

"Yeah, a little bit."

Phainon has to bite down his tongue. He finds it intensely erotic and he is not sure why. Scoliosis scar. Intensely erotic.

He is suddenly seized by a great yearning, an uncontrollable yearning. His fingers itch with the desire to pull Mydei into his chest, through his skin, through his ribcage, and straight into his heart. They are not close enough, physically, they are never close enough. Phainon does not know how to close that maddening distance between them.

He leans over him like a guardian, hands on each side of his shoulders, hovering above Mydei. Mydei does not stir at it, rather he grows more comfortable with his position. Phainon slowly lowers himself, until his mouth is at his ear. "Mydei…" he mutters, "Can I—Can I kiss it? The scar?"

"The scar…?" Mydei echoes, turning his head so that Phainon's lips brush his cheek, "Yes."

Phainon rubs his nose against his cheek and kisses it. Mydei cranes his head just so, giving Phainon leverage to kiss the corners of his mouth, both of them, just the way he likes it. His favorite way of being kissed.

Phainon shifts again and tenses his shoulders as he dips his head to Mydei's back. A small kiss between his shoulder blades, tongue peeking out to taste the scar; it tastes sweet, rich, it tastes like Mydei, it tastes like life. He moves down, wiggling on the bed to reach the lower parts of Mydei's back. He feels the muscle relax under his lips with every lingering kiss. Mydei sighs and puts his phone away. Turns his neck so that he can catch a glimpse of Phainon behind him. When he reaches his tailbone, Phainon gives it a filthy, wet kiss, mouth open and warm.

Then, he traces his way back to Mydei's shoulder blades with his tongue.

Mydei grunts, reddens, hides his face in his arms.

There is something terrible inside Phainon, and it makes him fever-hot. He runs his forehead between Mydei's strong blades, grasps his shoulders with his arm and massages them. Mydei pushes up into him, buttock to crotch. Phainon allows himself to sigh into his ear, to nibble at his lobe, and press his lips to his nose.

He nuzzles into him. Runs a shaky hand through Mydei's hair and toys with his braid a little. The other kneads his waist. His mouth goes dry with a question that burns his tongue.

"Mydei," he says, breathless, "Can I kiss you?"

Mydei stiffens all at once. He looks at him, just one golden eye. "If I say yes, are you going to fuck me?"

"No," Phainon says immediately, as though there is no other answer to this question—for Phainon, there isn't. The possibility doesn't even cross his mind. "I'm not going to. I don't want to. I want to kiss you just to kiss you. Just… for the sake of it."

Mydei moves and gets up to sit, forces Phainon to do the same. He twists around so he is facing him.

He looks… drunk, flushed, dazed. Not unhappy, but nervous. He is playing anxiously with his hands. Mydei looks off to the side and chews on his bottom lip. He turns back to Phainon.

"In that case… if you promise—"

"I promise."

"Then…" Mydei bows his head a bit, tilts it. Looks at his hands. Looks at Phainon.

"Then… yes."

Phainon did not think he would get this far. He did not think at all when he asked that question.

Yes. What a wonderful word, coming from Mydei's mouth.

They move awkwardly together. An off-beat waltz where the dancers keep stepping on each other's toes. Mydei shuffles closer to him, scooting on his butt, and once he is close enough, Phainon puts a hand on the side of his face. His cheeks are so hot. His other hand grabs Mydei's and intertwines their fingers. They are both shaking.

He tests this fragile thing by running his thumb across Mydei's bottom lip. Mydei swallows. Twitches away from the touch, and then leans into it. Phainon veers closer and when he sees Mydei close his eyes and tilt his head, he knows that he is completely lost and does not want to be found.

It is not a kiss, not entirely. It is terribly chaste, incredibly modest, and just a brush of lips against each other. A half of a half of a split second of contact. Warm, sweet, gentle. Phainon pulls back and looks at Mydei. They are both feeling very shy.

"Okay?" he asks. Mydei nods and closes his eyes again.

Phainon gives him a proper kiss this time, though it is still courtly, like a knight might kiss a noble prince. A fairytale kiss, if he had to describe it. Tender, delicate, and easy to shatter, yet still bearing the miracle of true love.

Mydei's lips taste as sweet as he has always imagined them. His Cherry Cola lip balm tastes just like Cherry Cola, and it takes a lot out of Phainon to not just lap at the taste until it is gone.

They break apart, but do not pull away. They sit impossibly close, forehead to forehead, and they look at each other.

Another small kiss. Then another. Phainon sighs into it, his thumb rubbing circles over the diamond tattoo on Mydei's cheek. The smacking of their lips makes an embarrassing sound, but it not filthy—rather, sweet. Cute, tiny kisses, obedient tongues locked behind closed mouths. Like schoolchildren, Phainon thinks.

Though Mydei kisses him back, he does not move at all. He is still as a board in front of Phainon, and it makes some of his confidence falter and crack. An ugly thought gnaws at the back of his head, and though he tries to ignore it, it grows more insidious.

Phainon pulls back all the way suddenly. Mydei chases after the touch and when Phainon looks at him, he finds him looking back, confused, frowning.

"Why did you stop?" he asks, voice raw and hushed and a little out of breath.

"You weren't moving so I… I thought—"

Mydei blinks, and then his features soften. He smiles and laughs a bit. Tucks a strand of hair behind his ear. His chunky hoops clink with the movement.

"It's okay, I like it," he says timidly, averting his gaze.

"…Yeah?"

Mydei just hums in response. He grins with all of his pretty teeth, his adorable fangs. He moves, then. Takes Phainon's hand and places it over his chest, lets it rest there. His heart is beating so fast, he is blushed deep and peachy, he is shimmering like a precious stone in the golden rays of the sun.

"You and I are Earth, 1661…" he says, trailing off. Phainon does not know what that means, that much is clear, so Mydei continues, "A plate that was found in a sewer had that engraved on it. It reminds me of us."

Phainon blinks. The two of them, Earth—that sounds about right.

Mydei cants forward and closes the distance between their mouths.

It is the same, the most they can manage. Tiny pecks, chaste, though now Mydei winds his arms around Phainon's neck and pulls him to his chest. Phainon, too, embraces him back, arms snake around his waist and so they kiss, like an entangled chimera, unnatural and a little crooked, but beautiful nonetheless.

They kiss until they are both out of breath and giggling, and when they are done for good, they lay down in bed together. Phainon's head on Mydei's chest, hearing the steady drum of his heart. Mydei's hand playing with his fingers.

"Was that scary?" Phainon asks.

"Yes, it was, but I enjoyed it. Thank you for…" he sighs, "For being patient with me."

Phainon blinks. "I don't feel like I've been patient. To be honest, I haven't been waiting or anything. I was just… in that moment I felt like kissing you. So I asked. But I haven't thought of kissing on the mouth a bunch before this."

Mydei nods, though more so to himself than to Phainon. "I'm still scared of it. I'm nervous, you understand, my nervous system is just fucked. But… I'm not scared because it's actually scary. I'm scared because of… you know, stuff… I did enjoy it, really. I would like to do it again. I might just be a bit nervous during it, that's all. It's not your fault."

Phainon leans in and steals a quick kiss to his temple. "It's not your fault either, you know. I wouldn't change anything about you. About us. I love this, just the way it is."

Mydei is silent for a long time, so long that Phainon would think he fell asleep if he were not seeing his eyes be open. Then, he turns and looks at the window, directly at that big source of light. He squints, then gazes down at Phainon. "Look," he says, pointing at the sun, "That's you."

"…Me? The sun?"

"Yes!" Mydei laughs, loud, wild, a bit like a wolf's howl, head thrown back, "How lucky I am. I am holding the sun, and he does not scorch me at all!"

Chapter Notes

This chapter was supposed to be longer, but this felt like a good place to end it. The rest of the scenes that I had planned for it were a bit too different tonally and they wouldn't have fit. Sorry it's a little short (and it still managed to be 11k words!!) and not much happens in this!

!IMPORTANT

This is a Mydei-centric chapter and comes with a BIG SA TW as it explores his trauma and his reactions to it throughout the entire chapter. There are also CHILD AND DOMESTIC ABUSE AND ANIMAL ABUSE/DEATH TWS. Specifics below vv

To say that Polyxia is unhappy with her decision is an understatement—she is absolutely downright furious, and Castorice can tell by the blazing glint in her eyes and the almost imperceptible twist of her mouth. She turns to her screen and blinks and, with each blink, a hot tear falls down her face. She weeps like that, silently, proudly almost, until she cannot see her screen anymore, and therefore cannot talk.

Castorice kneels besides her and takes her cheeks in her hands. She has lost so much weight there, in her face, and for the first time in her life, the visage that looks back at Castorice is not identical to hers anymore; this too is a loss, she thinks, but one that she can bear. One that prepares her for the unimaginable.

She wipes Polyxia's tears.

"Don't be upset with me, please," Castorice says.

She holds her pretty face until she stops crying, but the anger within her continues to simmer. Polyxia flits her eyes to the screen, and blinks.

"I do not want your life to revolve around me, Castorice," is all she says and what a silly girl she is—does she not know that they are two astral bodies, orbiting around each other, burning up, burning out? Castorice smiles at her, and she is so taken with affection that she bullies her head into her lap. She moves her hand so that it is resting on her scalp. Castorice still remembers the day they recorded her voice for the monitor. She remembers how hard she cried, and how Polyxia wouldn't stop going off-script. She insisted on recording every word ever, including the ones she's never used, like quixotic.

"That's nonsense, Polyxia. Taking care of you doesn't mean my life revolves around you. It's just something I do out of love and something I'm passionate about. Is that so hard to believe? That I might want to do this?"

"You're saying it like it's easy."

Castorice blinks up at her. "It is easy."

"It's not. I don't want to be a burden for you."

Her, a burden? Is she ridiculous? Is the moon a burden to the sun? Is the rain a burden to the grass? The pollen to the bee? They are dancing around the cycle of care, and where it once was Polyxia taking care of Castorice, now it is Castorice's turn.

"You are my sister and I don't ever want to hear that out of you, okay? You are not a burden, you're just… burdened by something, and I want to help you ease it. I want to help you carry it. How could you ever be a burden to me? You are my sister."

Swallowing is becoming difficult and while her breathing is holding up for now, a ventilator is in their future. Whatever little independence she has is about to shrink even more. She is going to be very sad and very depressed, and she is will need friends around her more than ever; she will need love and companionship, and Castorice wants nothing more than to provide those for her. She is going to need around-the-clock care, more than they can afford and more than she's willing to trust a stranger with, even a trained professional. Above all, however, a selfish want—

"Whatever time we have together is terribly finite, Polyxia. I don't want to spend it at some stupid job I hate that makes me feel bad about myself. I want to spend it with you. I want to… I want to wash your hair and help you in the bathroom and help you eat. I do those things anyways, yes, but I want to do them all the time. And before you start—you know I can see what you type, right?—it's not duty. It's just care. That's literally just it. We've always been a team, why can't we be a team now, too?"

Polyxia doesn't answer. She slumps a bit and sighs. She looks off, away at a random door. After a while, she turns back to her screen.

"I am scared. I'm really scared all of a sudden."

"I know. I'm scared too. Let's just be scared together, okay? We can figure it out like that. I'll… I'll talk to the insurance lady, maybe it covers some sort of family therapy for this, you know? Maybe that will help."

Polyxia has been brave for so long. Unshakeable as though made of steel. Somehow, through her illness, she has still been Castorice's pillar—Castorice thinks that, now, it is time for the roles to change. She has to be the strong one, she has to be brave when Polyxia falters, and she has to catch her when she falls.

She remembers them as children, Polyxia fighting off the kids that bullied her. She remembers them as teenagers and the time Polyxia broke the nose of a guy that groped her. She remembers prom, when two boys fought over who got to take Polyxia as their date, and Polyxia instead took Castorice as her date. She remembers their matching purple dresses, Polyxia's dark, Castorice's light. She remembers when she got her diagnosis, how they cried in each other's arms, and how in the end, it was Polyxia that assured her that everything will be okay.

Castorice kisses her hand. "I love you so much," she tells her, and she is bursting with it, falling apart with it, "Please let me take care of you."

She hears her gulp and swallow thickly. "Okay," she says and Castorice jumps to her feet to —carefully—wrap her arms around her.

"That's good, because I already signed the resignation papers, so…" she says with relief.

That makes Polyxia chortle a small laugh, which is an immense win for Castorice.

"You are ridiculous," Polyxia tells her and yeah, Castorice is ridiculous, she's silly and a little weird, but right now, she is just her little sister, eager to help.

"You are ridiculous too," she says back, "I guess it runs in the family."

Mydei is staring and his reflection and a stranger stares back at him. It is a stranger that wears his face, shockingly similar, yet foreign nonetheless. There are just… these little things that are off about him, like the length of his eyelashes, the color of his lips, the flush in his cheeks. The stranger's hair is done up in elaborate ringlets—is that a wig?— and dusted with glitter, and he is wearing this ridiculous frilly bonnet, like the old-school kind that wraps around the head like a cone. The stranger is wearing a beautiful red dress. Mydei squints at the mirror. Who is this? Who is he?

"All done, Mydei, oh, you're so cute I could just eat you up~"

So cute? Eat you up? Is that a threat? Somebody is talking to him. A girl. He and the stranger turn to look at the same time.

He finds himself face to face with a pink monstrosity, something exploding with ribbons and lace. His pulse picks up and he is wrecked with anxiety. Mydei is caught between reality and dream, unable to break away. She speaks to him and the more she yaps, the more the heavy fog lifts from his brain.

The sketch starts to take shape and color. An overly decorated cute room, the weird cooing of a pigeon, and the woman in front of him—she is pretty, fair-skinned, green-eyed, and has a gigantic pink wig on. Her nails are long and weighed down with charms, and her make-up is soft and doll-like.

"…Are you okay?" she asks, her eyes softening with concern. The pigeon, which must be the same as the one that was cooing, flies on her shoulder and gives her cheek a peck.

Mydei blinks once, twice, and—

Oh yes, this is Hyacine. And this is her TikTok room, and that's Little Ica, and they were supposed to film a video for her TikTok. They've been trying to set it up for like, a month, but something always came up.

"…Uh, I…" he manages, "I'm—disassociating? Why am I disassociating?"

She blinks at him. "Why are you disassociating?"

He turns back to the mirror and, oh God, that's no stranger, that's him in a bonnet and a red dress and dollcore makeup. Jesus Christ, he looks ridiculous. Mydei touches his cheeks and moves them around, then runs them down the corset of the dress.

"Hyacine, this fits me so well…" he points out. In response, Hyacine puts down whatever it was she was holding—looked like a makeup brush—and comes over to put a hand on his back.

"Fuck that, what was that about disassociating?"

Mydei's tongue is so heavy in his mouth that he fears he might choke on it. He tries to swallow around it and finds that it is impossible. He looks at her instead, and whatever she sees on his face worries her. "Alright, okay, let's just go out on the balcony, yeah? Phainon, come out to the balcony!" she calls out and, huh, Phainon must be with them too.

She grabs his hand and pulls him along to the balcony. Little Ica follows them, planted firmly on her shoulder. The cool November air hits him like a bag of bricks, like the shock of cold water. He parts his mouth a bit, just to take a small breath, to feel it burn down his throat and settle into his stomach. It is some relief, yes, not entirely but enough to ground him. He pulls out a chair and sits on it, vaguely registers Hyacine leaving and coming back with a glass of water. He takes it from her, thanks her graciously, and downs it in one go. Then wipes his mouth with his arm.

"Ah!!" she screams, "Oh, Mydei, you brute! You piss me off! You ruined your lipstick!"

Mydei looks down at his arm and finds a pink-ish red stripe smudged there. It smells good. And it's a little glossy. "…Oops," is all he says.

Hyacine groans. "I took so long doing your makeup!"

"I said oops," he repeats, as if that's supposed to make her feel better. She throws her hands up in defeat and sits down on a chair next to him. Weirdly enough, Ica is still on her shoulder and it makes no attempt to fly away. Mydei tilts his head as he looks at the pigeon. It's snow-white with a purple-green ring around its neck, pretty black eyes and chubby cheeks. It is nearly entirely spherical. Like, just a perfect… ball of feathers. He squints at it and makes a swift judgment: that thing should not exist. That is not one of God's creations.

Mydei feels… spacey, like he is floating through stormy clouds. Everything is slow. Words roll out of his mouth like wet bricks, heavy enough to weight him down yet soft enough to be crushed beneath his teeth. He asks Hyacine for a glass of water—he feels impossibly parched. An ocean's worth of water could not sate him now, and yet he still drinks with absentminded futility.

A dream is the best way he can describe this feeling. That odd feeling where you know you're dreaming and yet cannot break away from it. Mydei tilts his head. It is not entirely unpleasant. At most, it's safe. It has kept him sane through the worst moments of his life. Finding his mother's body, testifying against his father, and those torturous, long hours where he laid in bed, staring at the ceiling, wondering what happened while his boyfriend was snoring away happily next to him. He looked down at his hands then, and realized he could not manage to count his fingers. He knew, logically, that there should be five of them, and yet when it came to the one, two, three of it… Oddly, that moment marked him about as much as the assault that happened earlier. That is all he remembers of that night—feeling scared and not being able to count his fingers.

Mydei thinks, briefly, that this is what it must have felt to be in his mother's womb. Overbearingly safe, but finite. He must be birthed at some point, and so too does the haze of disassociation lifts from him eventually, leaving Mydei to deal with all the consequences. And the consequences are always heavy, and they always end in some type of bloodshed. Dead cats and cut wrists.

When Phainon joins them on the balcony, wearing a ridiculous little sailor suit, Mydei realizes that this might be less of a dream, and more of a fucking nightmare. He is bursting out of those goddamn clothes. Hyacine got them a size too small, doubtless on purpose to show off his musculature, but it's like… A grown man with hair on his balls. In a sailor suit. Holding a lollipop the size of his head—actually, a bit bigger than that.

Weirdly, this whole look fits Phainon, little hat and all. His smile is luminous when he sees Mydei.

"Mydei, wow, you're so…" he covers his mouth and giggles, "You're so cute!"

"Don't make fun of me," Mydei grumbles.

"I'm not! You're really, really cute, wow, you really do look like a doll!"

Mydei's dress has these long billowy sleeves that he keeps getting his hands tangled into. He remembers Hyacine wanted to give him press-on nails but now that he is looking down at his hands, he finds his nails bare. He must've refused her at some point.

Hyacine blows a puff of smoke out of her cigarette and the smell is pleasant and sweet, kind of like cherries. "Mydei, you said you're disassociating," she presses on further.

"Uh… Yeah, I am."

Her face grows even more concerned. Phainon steals one of her cigarettes and lights it.

"Sometimes that happens to him if he looks in the mirror, and you did do his makeup, so…" Phainon trails off. He seems casual as he takes a drag out of the cigarette. Mydei likes that. He likes not being fussed over as if he's made of glass.

Hyacine is not convinced. "So it's, what, normal?"

"Hyacine, don't you have a degree in psychology?" Phainon teases, "You don't seem very well-informed~"

"I am well-informed, okay? I know what disassociation is, I'm also just worried about my friend!"

"It's fine, Hyacine, uh… It just happens sometimes, it's okay," Mydei says, reaching over to nudge her, "I'll be back to normal soon, just gotta… I don't know, wait, I guess?"

Phainon is right, this does happen to him sometimes if he looks at his reflection for too long. On his worst days, he has to cover every mirror and reflective surface in the apartment with a towel. Being reminded that he is of flesh and bone, that a physical body accompanies his thoughts and feelings, is jarring. Mydei catches himself staring in the bathroom mirror for minutes at a time, looking dumbly at his reflection as if he were a baby seeing himself for the first time. He cannot believe it, sometimes. That he is real. That he tangibly exists. That he takes up real space in the world, that he is made of atoms and carbon and connective tissue. Really, most of the time he just feels like a specter. Being reminded that he is not? Crazy stuff. No wonder he disassociates.

They decide to wait it out. Hyacine goes inside at some point, and that leaves Clown A and Clown B sitting on the balcony, dressed up in costumes.

"Are you feeling better?" Phainon asks after a long time. Mydei checks his phone; an hour has passed.

He is feeling much better, more grounded in reality, but he still floats. Mydei grumbles noncommittally, waving his hand around vaguely.

"So-so?" Phainon interprets for him, and Mydei nods. "Okay. How do we speed it up?"

Mydei shrugs. "I mean, there's some grounding exercises I do, but I'm like… not feeling up to it, honestly. Let's just wait it out."

"Hyacine's gonna kill you, dude."

"I'm more worried about that thing she calls a pet."

"Ica? Ica's got quite the story," Phainon says with a laugh.

"What is it?"

"I'll let Hyacine tell it. You have to hear it from her."

Mydei hums in agreement and then he turns to look at him, and he finds Phainon scrolling on his phone, cigarette hanging loosely between his lips—and he thinks that in this moment, at this time as the sun is starting to creep downwards into the sea, Phainon looks ravishingly handsome. Even in his stupid sailor suit and hat. His heart thrums in his chest as it picks up speed. Mydei will, possibly, never get tired of looking at Phainon, not when his features are so fine and precise as though one of the great masters worked him from marble. Has there even been a more beautiful man? Mydei finds it hard to believe.

His jaw clenches around the cigarette as he pulls from it and blows out smoke; Mydei wishes he would've blown it down his throat. He likes the soft parts of Phainon, but he likes the sharp ones, too. He likes the intensity of his gaze, how in some lights those blue eyes seem dipped in gold. He likes the strength of his arm and the curve of his broad shoulders. He likes that he is tall, though Mydei dislikes that he is half an inch taller than him.

Most of all, he likes the forlorn look in Phainon's eyes. It reminds Mydei of his first true love, the first man he spilled his seed to; the Saint Sebastian himself, bound with rope to a tree and shot through with arrows. Nude, tensing, flexing, bending at the waist in surrender. In the painting that he was taken with, the Saint's meaty thigh was pierced with an arrow, and so was the great column of his pale throat. Most captivating of all was the look in his eyes, which Mydei often finds reflected in Phainon's. An agony that does not differentiate between pain and pleasure. Eyes rolled up to the Heavens, perhaps to invoke God's name through his torture, or perhaps to steady himself through the pulsing currents of an orgasm. His pretty mouth parted over a scream or a moan. Le petit mort as blood runs down his thigh; the imagery of deflowering. Suffering is good, suffering cleanses, and so in that painting, Saint Sebastian suffers on the precipice of climax—the divine agony reflected in his eyes is both pain and pleasure, beautiful and ugly, real and unreal, mixing together like myrrh and muck.

All of that to say—Phainon just kind of has that look in his eyes. The look of a suffering saint in the throes of God's trials, not knowing whether to bleed or come. That beautiful, detached pain that burns hot enough to reach the Mount Sinai and demand new commandments of God. Untouchable, dishonest, and terribly lovely. Mydei wants to break all of his teeth.

His cheeks feel impossibly hot. Phainon's eyes are wet and mellow like a lamb being led to slaughter. He has a lovely mouth, pretty cupid's bow, and it would be so easy to capture it between his sharp teeth and make him bleed. He would like to see if their blood is the same hue of red.

Mydei licks his lips and finds them tasting like lip gloss.

"Kiss me," he demands all of a sudden, and it catches Phainon off guard for a second. He coughs and sputters but composes himself quickly.

"Here, of all places?" Phainon rumbles low in his chest, clicking off his phone—Mydei catches a glimpse of Umamusume before he does—and turning to look at him. He rests his cheek on his hand, leans into it just so, and gives Mydei that smirks that he loves; it tries to be self-assured and cocky, but only manages to look fake. Mydei is only so enamored with it because he can see all the cracks of insecurity underneath it.

Mydei wriggles closer and puts his hand to the back of his head. He pushes Phainon closer to him and knocks their foreheads together; then he, too, gifts Phainon with a smirk of his own, though his is far more convincing. Phainon grunts, Mydei growls, and so they sit there, both baring their fangs, pushing and knocking their heads against each others like young rams in rut. He feels Phainon's hand rest on his nape. He feels terribly warm there, and doubtless that he is flushed and peachy-pink like a maiden; well, given all of the make-up Hyacine put on him, his real blush is probably indistinguishable from the fake one.

"Yes, here, of all places," Mydei rasps and tilts his head up just enough to make his lips brush against Phainon's. The ghost-promise of a kiss.

Phainon falls for it immediately and closes the distance between them.

Mydei has learned over this past week that he really does enjoy being kissed for the sake of being kissed, when it's not just a motion he has to go through before sex. He brought it up to his therapist and Mrs. Sofia couldn't hide the look of triumph in her eyes. Mydei is a little dumbstruck for a moment, and then warmth returns to him in waves, nice and pleasant, filling him up. Phainon lets his hand rest on the center of his chest, where his heart beats fastest. His cheek finds its place on Mydei's shoulder and he sighs wistfully into it. Finally, he looks up at him with a small smile.

"Go on," Phainon says simply, "I'm listening."

Mydei is so in love. He is so in love.

"I…" he starts, "I didn't even know what happened or why I suddenly felt so bad," he whispers, hating how weak it sounds, "My therapist couldn't figure it out either, you know, why my mental health just took such a sudden dive. One day she just asked me to recall every event of the past however many months in detail, and I offhandedly mentioned it to her and—" he sighs, "I'm never going to forget her reaction. Her eyes got big and concerned and I thought… Oh, that must've been something bad that happened, and she—She told me she was sorry and that I was sexually assaulted and at first I didn't… believe her. Didn't want to. Honestly, I wanted to drop her as my therapist, but I stuck by it and—"

He runs a hand down his face. Looks away from Phainon. "The more we talked, the more I realized that it wasn't the… only time, I guess. I didn't know that… being nagged into it counted. Or just giving up so he'd stop bothering me about it—I'm sorry, this is a lot. It's not your fault, Phainon."

Phainon chuckles a little, then kisses his shoulder again. "I know. Oh, sorry—was that alright? The kiss?"

"...Yes."

"It's not a lot, it's—" and he brushes a lock of hair out of Mydei's face, "I just don't know what to say. I'm not very good at this. But I'm happy to just listen. I'm glad you told me. I get it, some of it I mean, that feeling of being empty and not whole… Yeah, I get it."

Mydei blinks at him. "Are you going to tell me about Cyrene?"

"Soon," Phainon answers with a twitch of his mouth, "Before her anniversary. I promise. I just—I just need a bit longer."

Mydei, weirdly, does not mind this. He thinks that Phainon is patient with him, so he, too, can be patient with Phainon. And just between him and God, he's put two and two together—the car accident, Cyrene's passing, Phainon's need to be forgiven. He just wants to hear it from Phainon. Mydei sighs, and recognizes the tell-tale signs of the death throes of a mental breakdown. The deep exhaustion and bone ache. The haze of disassociation saving him from all of it.

Phainon leaves his side and the room is suddenly much colder. He sits up and looks down at Mydei. "Darling," he coos, stroking his hair, "Dear. Beloved. Sweetheart. Lance of Fury."

He makes himself laugh at that, because he always laughs at his jokes, and it gets a chuckle out of Mydei too. "I'm going to take a bath, okay, love?" Phainon continues, "You can join me if you want to."

"Okay. I'll think about it."

With that, Phainon gets up from the bed, leaving it much lighter than it ever was and Mydei sinks deeper into the mattress.

He does think about it for ten or so minutes and decides that he does not feel up to bathing, but that he does want to spend some time with Phainon. He discards his pants, and he is already shirtless, so…

The walk to the bathroom does not feel real. Tiredness presses on his shoulders like a murder of crows looking onto a deserted battlefield, waiting, wanting. He can hardly keep himself upright. Every movement is slowed, as though he were covered in molasses and fighting against the current. He has to stop once, when he gets dizzy, before he can continue.

As tired as he is, and he is exhausted, the need to see Phainon is stronger. He wants to see him—he has to see him. Every moment spent with his eyes looking at anything but him is a moment wasted. If we are talking about pyramids of necessities, Phainon is at the very top, trumping them all.

Mydei cracks the door open and finds Phainon in the bathtub, doubled over on himself, knees to his chest. When he hears the door creak, he looks up. Looks at Mydei.

His eyes are puffy and red, like he has been crying, and if he has been crying—he has done so silently. What a beautiful weeper his lover is, just like Saint Sebastian, just like the Virgin Mary.

When he sees Mydei naked, fully naked in all of his bare glory, he quickly looks away. He seems a little embarrassed, and Mydei finds it very endearing.

"Phainon…" Words are hard and slow right now, and so they come out a little slurred, "Why are you crying?"

"Oh, uh…" The tips of Phainon's ears go red, "Nothing, it's just, what you said, I felt—It was sad, and I felt bad that it was happening to you."

Phainon, crying for him? What a fool. What an utter waste of hydration. Phainon should never cry, Mydei thinks, instead he should laugh. He loves his laughter, his ungainly snorts, the way it shows off all of his teeth and his gums. He should never cry, and especially not for Mydei of all people. He can shoulder the burden. They can do it together, maybe.

"You can look at me, if you want to," Mydei says, and it is barely the whisper of a whisper. What remains unsaid is: please, please look at me.

Phainon looks, turns his head slowly as though unsure. He looks at Mydei's face first, and then his gaze lingers down like a shooting star. His collarbones. The swells of his breasts. His strong, flat stomach, his narrow waist. Lower then, to his hipbones jutting out, the curve of his thighs and, finally, his flaccid cock between his legs. He stops there, looks at it for a moment or two. Tilts his head a little, breathes in heavy. They have never been naked before, not like this. It's freeing, in a way, and terribly intimate. Mydei finds that he does not mind it.

When he has gotten his fill of staring, and Phainon is truly shameless about this, he looks up back up at Mydei's face and meets his eyes.

In this sickly yellow light of this cold bathroom, Phainon is beautiful like a ghost, like something forgotten. Like a small prayer between lovers carved into a random wall, or the footprints of someone that has left long ago. He is as though a beautiful memory, unreal in its sincerity, and Mydei cannot believe that this moment exist, that it is tangible and in the physical realm, that he can stretch his arm forward and touch it. Touch him.

"I'm sorry for freaking out," Mydei says, "You've been very good to me. I feel like I haven't been—"

"You're the best thing that's ever happened to me," Phainon says immediately, cutting him off, his voice resonating off of the tile walls like an echo.

Mydei blinks, stunned. "I haven't done anything."

"Nonsense. You've helped me a lot. Before we started dating, I—" he groans, "This is a little embarrassing, but seeing you at work, it was kind of the only thing I was looking forward to. I had a massive crush on you."

Mydei smiles, bemused, and allows himself this, "I feel like I am meant to be here, with you. I feel like it's fate or something. I think… I would do it all again, if it meant meeting you. I would go through all of it again."

Phainon's eyes get big, "I would rather you didn't."

"I would, though, seriously. I would do it all again if it meant I would end up in this bathroom, on this night."

Phainon flushes, just the way Mydei likes it, and chuckles nervously like a schoolboy in love. He moves in the bathtub and it makes the water slosh around him. He makes some space for Mydei.

"Come in?"

He does not need to be asked twice. Mydei is pulled in by Phainon's gravitational force, like a planet happily orbiting the Sun. One leg in and then the other, and then he is sitting down and facing Phainon.

He looks at Phainon. Phainon looks back. He is reminded, briefly, of a similar position they have taken, millions of years ago, when Phainon was sick like a dog and Mydei was so full of love he could barely take it. Back when he confessed his feelings to him and Phainon, beautifully, returned them. What a happy night that was. What a happy night this is, too.

They look at each other and none speak. He does not mind being naked around Phainon. He loves it, actually. Loves how simple and primal it is. Two of them, one two, so simple, so easy to count. Naked, just like they were always meant to be, and this is certainly erotic, but it is not sexual. It is not threatening. Phainon is not threatening.

Mydei smiles at him and Phainon smiles back. He can hardly keep his eyes open, the poor thing, and the water is getting cold around them, but none want to step out.

Mydei opens his arms in invitation, says, "Come to me," and Phainon comes.

('Just like Cyrene,' Phainon thinks then. Just like in his dream, her on the rocks of a wrathful sea, calling him to his doom. Mydei calls him too, now, calls him to something sweet and, like a moon orbits the Earth, so too does Phainon orbit Mydei.)

He snuggles up in Mydei's arms, applying weight to all the right places, emptying his head of thoughts. He is so comfortable to hold, so soft, and Mydei wraps his arms all around him. Phainon finds solace in the crook of his neck, and Mydei buries his nose in the crown of his head. This is the most natural way to exist. Together, entangled, inseparable.

"I killed a cat once, did I ever tell you?" Mydei tells him, though he is not sure why, "It was after I first testified against my father. My uncle was called into work out of nowhere, even though he took the day off, and he asked one of the neighbors to look after me. She was a bit busy right then but ah, she said she would come as soon as she is done, and…" Mydei kisses his head, "While I was waiting for her in the yard, a cat came over. Orange and small. It rubbed on my leg and purred and I've always hated the sound of cats purring. It makes me want to cry. I was so… so mad. I was so upset. I was so upset, I can't even describe it. I felt like an infected wound, like… pus. I was pus oozing out."

He stops for a moment. Remembers. He picked it up, then, and—

"I didn't even know what happened until I was looking at its body. I didn't—I didn't mean to. I didn't want to do it. I kept thinking about my dad. About the way he pulled my hair and unbuckled his belt, about the way he would shove my mom into walls. I thought about her body. About how scared she must've been. About how much it must've hurt. I… I wanted to feel…"

"Strong?"

"…Yeah. Strong. It's my biggest regret. I can't even think about it. It hurts so much to think about it. I can't stand being around cats anymore. I think I'll hurt them. I'm not—I'm not the type that hurts animals. I like animals. I hate myself for it, I don't want to be someone that hurts animals, but—"

"I don't think you are," Phainon slurs in his arms.

"If I could change anything, it would be the only thing I would change. The cat didn't deserve that."

"No. Neither did you."

"Are you mad at me?" Mydei whispers, and Phainon makes a noncommittal sound.

"You did tell me you killed a cat before, remember? The night we started dating?"

Mydei does not remember, but he does not remember much anyways.

"I… Look, I'm not mad at you. You were a kid and you're not a cruel adult. It was a mistake. I've done worse."

"With Cyrene?" Mydei tries.

"Yeah, with Cyrene."

Mydei sighs and holds Phainon closer. "I'm not going to hurt Bartholos."

"No, you won't. But you could try being his friend. Who knows? Maybe he's the reincarnation of that cat and this is like, your chance or something."

"…I'll try."

Phainon kisses his breast then, and once more on his collarbone. "You're so… soft…" he trails off, sinking deeper, "Mmm… Soft Dei…"

They stay silent for a few minutes. Phainon's breathing slows more and more, until Mydei hears a low snore. He cracks his eyes open and sees Phainon, sleeping deep in his arms, comfortable and content.

He pokes his cheek and Phainon does not stir, and then he pulls some of his hair a little. He stays still through it.

After Mydei thoroughly makes sure Phainon is asleep, he leans down to the shell of his ears and stamps a lingering kiss there, something to warm him in his sleep. "I love you," he says, "I love you a lot."

It is an hour before Mydei finds it in him to wake Phainon up and drag him to the bed.
